entries.title: Independent Web Environment Center
entries.summary: Desktop combines an environment center with its existing local Runtime lifecycle. Web Center deploys independently; Runtime never requires Center or Desktop to start. Both hosts share Contracts/Core/Controller/UI. Web Center has one administrator, with no registration, users, roles, organizations or user ACL service.

entries.title: Single-administrator Web Center access
entries.summary: Center has one administrator and multiple devices. Center, Gateway and Runtime retain independent authorization: Center permits directory/open actions, never Runtime login bypass or management authority. Device revocation cancels every derived admission.

entries.title: Deploy and qualify standalone Web Center
entries.summary: Center binary/UI deploy separately from Desktop and Runtime. Evidence records source/artifacts, host, browser, real elapsed duration, cleanup and limits. Smoke tests cannot certify an eight-hour soak or a different native browser. Qualification uses isolated service names, ports and state, and preserves existing Runtime processes.

entries.title: Flower startup and recovery presentation
entries.summary: Env App/Desktop project one owner's readiness and typed Stop/Retry while retaining navigation and drafts. Close failure requires restart; unknown or contradictory facts are non-retryable contract failures. No surface adds an availability controller. First content admits the workspace; later refresh/reconnect retains mounted conversation state.

entries.title: Flower persistent-index startup acceptance
entries.summary: Published Floret 7.52.0 on an isolated 710,344,704 B/219-thread database achieves full product construction/activation P95 9.429 s over 20 runs, with maximum GC-live heap 261.052 MiB upstream/295.018 MiB product. Targets≤10 s/350 MiB pass for this dataset; canonical validation still has substantial temporary allocation.

entries.title: Flower conversation switch performance qualification
entries.summary: Published Floret v7.87.3 owns windows, bounded item-text reads, View/Summary. Redeven owns [sidebar](../ui/flower-thread-sidebar.md), [bridge](../desktop/desktop-runtime-bridge.md) and bounded presentation. Local targets: short-detail P95 reduction ≥70%, warm synchronous P95 <8 ms, feedback before commit.

entries.title: Flower conversation selection and detail reads
entries.summary:
Flower acknowledges navigation before transcript work. One coordinator serves
navigation, command confirmation and reference preflight. ThreadCache owns
selection and detail; the loader owns bounded ephemeral demand.
Readiness controls reveal; elapsed time controls feedback only.

entries.title: Control-plane capacity qualification
entries.summary: Control-plane capacity qualification measures ten thousand enrolled Runtime sessions through real Nginx/TLS, MySQL, and canonical authority decisions. The harness uses production heartbeats, signed Gateway observations, and credential recovery. A full acceptance result combines client latency and recovery counts with independent server CPU, RSS, database, queue, and challenge-backlog measurements.

entries.title: Tessiven DSL versioning
entries.summary: Runtime owns schema selection and explicit v1→v1.0.0→v1.1.0 migrations. New documents use redeven.io/tessiven/v1.1.0; each edge changes only its version scalar, preserving legacy automatic layout. Reads preserve YAML/digest/revision; authorized edits save current snapshots. Invalid/unknown versions or migration failure leave storage unchanged and require compatible Runtime/repair.

entries.title: Tessiven stable canvas presentation
entries.summary: Runtime projects current DSL into frozen data-only redeven.io/tessiven-presentation/v1; clients use bundled renderers. DSL releases do not change display format or require client updates. Preserve historical YAML, digest/revision and write authority. Unsupported source remains viewable/exportable without invented topology; integrity failure has no export. Never return executable code.

entries.title: Tessiven canvas contract
entries.summary:
Tessiven is the Runtime-owned library of immutable service canvases. Each
canvas stores a complete `redeven.io/tessiven/v1.1.0` YAML document and every save
creates a new version. The Runtime is the single owner of canvas data; the
Desktop Welcome surface and the local Env App render that same library. A
failed validation or version conflict leaves the last saved document intact.

entries.title: Native Runtime bridge
entries.summary: redeven native-bridge --state-root PATH attaches to the existing Runtime via its owner-only management socket. Stdio carries redeven-native-runtime-h2/1 and only native-runtime CONNECT. Missing/inaccessible/stopped/incompatible targets fail without install, startup, address fallback or Desktop credentials. Disconnect releases this client, not Runtime.

entries.title: Flower working files and deliverables
entries.summary: Flower stores intermediate files in Runtime state and final files at the user's destination. Redeven owns filesystem policy, bytes and UI; Floret owns canonical results/identities. No artifact index, transcript copy, new upstream API or domain migration.

entries.title: Flower browser source ownership
entries.summary: ComputerUseRuntime authorizes targets; its source Host owns CDP/extension adapters. Discovery grants no input. Each admitted page has one debugger/input order; private opener ancestry stays hidden across inventories. Source loss retires only affected bindings. Unknown effects never replay and Host failure never creates replacement authority.

entries.title: Flower browser Linux preparation
entries.summary: Runtime discovers installations and registers Native Messaging; Host Applications owns graphical lifecycle. The guide prepares a persistent Linux Chrome/Chromium profile without launch or target authority. Clients pass opaque installation IDs, never paths/argv. Preserve personal profiles; unsupported platforms, missing installs and unsafe directories fail before launch.

entries.title: Database schema migration ownership
entries.summary: Each repository migrates its own stores: Redeven product data, Floret and ReDevPlugin internals. Open validates the complete SQLite/WAL view before service admission. Contiguous atomic migrations preserve data; future, drifted, wrong-kind or unsupported inputs remain untouched. Failure stops the affected service, never patches upstream data or replaces a database.

entries.title: AI readiness and service generation lifecycle
entries.summary: Floret owns durable Agent/Store facts; Redeven's single process-local readiness controller owns AI construction, retry, publication, request leases, drain and close. Non-AI surfaces remain usable through startup/migration/recovery. Requests use one generation. Unavailable startup returns sanitized typed state without publishing a partial service, repairing Store data or creating durable Agent state.

entries.title: Runtime startup presentation
entries.summary: `redeven run` startup is modeled as a lifecycle event stream. Human terminal output and public machine events are renderers over the same state snapshot, while a separate private Desktop report carries machine-only attach data and stable failure codes needed to open or recover the local Env App safely.

entries.title: Observation and target action events
entries.summary: Target actions are ordinary Flower tool observations. The workspace stream remains the only lifecycle and replay channel; screenshot descriptors are canonical keyframes, while short-lived live frames are target-scoped media and may be dropped without changing thread state.

entries.title: Local UI surface
entries.summary: Runtime Local UI supports concurrent independent Desktop/browser sessions. Public HTTP/WS or HTTPS/WSS shares one port; private Desktop uses numeric loopback and flowersec-private-loopback/1. Versioned SQLite owns one-shot authorization/browser spend across transports. Network exposure owns protocol, scope, password, certificate and migration policy.

entries.title: Env App session event transport
entries.summary: One Floe HTTP proxy runtime serves each Env App session and all built-in/plugin logical event streams. Features cannot consume parallel native HTTP/1.1 slots, retarget upstream identity or create another transport. Session replacement cancels observations; stopping observation never cancels business work.

entries.title: Activity navigation restoration
entries.summary: One Redeven Activity record selects the saved target before mounting and commits navigation/recency immediately. Floe owns geometry only. Invalid targets use available built-ins or Terminal; transient inventory failure retains the target, and late restoration never overrides a newer user selection.

entries.title: Env App resource snapshots
entries.summary: Floe owns disposable restoration, coalescing, fencing, persistence and eviction; Redeven confirms identity/projection. Host Apps, Containers, Web Services and Codespaces retain last successful inventory during refresh, animating only its icon. Cache grants no authority. Denial/locked access clears affected display; connectivity failure retains facts with error/Retry.

entries.title: Redeven loading and layout continuity
entries.summary: One product presentation registry declares initial loading and reload eligibility for every built-in Activity page and Workbench widget. Modules load inside their own surface, preserving existing successful content. Data services own readiness; access/authentication changes override retention, and loading never grants permission.

entries.title: Env App document reload presentation
entries.summary: Floe owns the anonymous reload geometry placeholder; Redeven hands it to current Activity inventory. Never replace restored content with a blank or mismatched skeleton. Geometry grants no data/authority. Denial, navigation, errors or auth change end it, and unavailable storage cannot block startup.

entries.title: Web Services interface
entries.summary: Activity/Workbench share service collection/drawer: identity, current status, action, then facts. Retain readable narrow/localized/enlarged-text layouts. Historical failure cannot replace state; failed checks retain facts with explanation and authorized inspection. Env App resource snapshots own inventory continuity; restored presentation grants no lifecycle/route authority.

entries.title: Web Service browser sessions
entries.summary: Web Services accepts ports or HTTP(S) deep links to the current Environment's loopback and opens them through authorized forwarding. Other targets fail before session/window creation. Registry-owned `access_mode` selects secure `unified_proxy` or HTTP-only Desktop `desktop_loopback`; heuristics and failures cannot override it. Stale windows, mismatched routes, invalid modes and expired temporary forwards fail closed.

entries.title: Managed host application preparation
entries.summary: Floe Native Apps acquires, verifies, stages and activates Linux components. Redeven owns routes, placement and progress. Preparation needs no VM/container/package manager/admin password. Runtime upgrades are independent; optional failure preserves compatible installs. Activation requires verification and graphical qualification.

entries.title: Human remote desktop sessions
entries.summary: Redeven owns authorization, ephemeral sessions, placement/config/audit; published floe-native-apps owns OS selection, capture/input/codecs/playback and Linux acquisition/physical service. Share the signed-in macOS/Linux desktop without creating private desktops or changing OS policy. Disconnect preserves apps/work. Unavailability revokes input until a fresh active frame.

entries.title: Administrator-authorized remote desktop deployment over SSH
entries.summary: Desktop owns SSH authorization/UI lifetime, Floe Native Apps privileged preparation and Runtime service authorization/audit. Every connection ensures current policy and authenticates actual Runtime. Unknown state is preserved. Cancellation reports rollback; verified completion may win but cannot auto-open after cancel.

entries.title: Persistent remote desktop sharing approval
entries.summary: Redeven owns sharing preference/reset; published Floe Native Apps owns OS authorization and private recovery credentials. Logged-in Runtime defaults to reusing first approval, attempting recovery before new consent. Saved credentials are opportunities, never proof of OS admission, and never reach viewers, URLs or audits. This optional user Portal chain is separate from [SSH system-service deployment](remote-desktop-ssh-deployment.md).

entries.title: Remote desktop connection launcher
entries.summary: Env App owns one remote desktop flow in Host Applications/Workbench: identify the host, show readiness and one primary action, then continue authorization in place. [Session policy](remote-desktop.md) enforces platform/permission limits. Failure retains recovery; dismissal before creation finishes releases that session. An opened viewer has an independent lifetime.

entries.title: Flowersec transport for graphical windows
entries.summary: Flowersec owns encryption, carrier/multiplexing/framing/backpressure; Redeven owns resources, authorization and routing. All graphical state, tickets, input, clipboard, audio, pixels and disconnect use native session proxy. Static bootstrap/acquisition stays authenticated browser traffic. Missing authority fails closed; raw graphical HTTP/WS bypass is forbidden.

entries.title: Graphical window native transport qualification
entries.summary:
The [graphical transport contract](../architecture/graphical-window-transport.md)
passes native direct, real encrypted tunnel, resource-authority and Linux live
checks with published dependencies. Active macOS capture and the Electron
fullscreen portion remain blocked by the host lock screen. Locked-host refusal
passes, but does not qualify an unlocked desktop. These functional checks do not
replace the separate [performance measurement contract](remote-desktop-validation.md).

entries.title: Remote desktop viewer interaction
entries.summary: Redeven controls/feedback use published input/playback; session contracts own authorization and capture generations. Only painted current control admits input. Separate cursor frames permit immediate pointer motion; embedded cursor hides local pointer. Recovery keeps local controls usable. Disconnect stops input/media, confirms removal or offers Retry; frozen pixels never imply connection.

entries.title: Remote desktop media and input scheduling
entries.summary: Published native components own capture, encoding and playback; Redeven consumes them. [Session authority](remote-desktop.md) owns authorization/generations. Media work is bounded and cursors follow painted pixels. Input admission does not prove host delivery. Capture/input failure retires authority; delayed work cannot overwrite or authorize a successor.

entries.title: Wayland cursor and scheduling optimization evidence
entries.summary: Native 0.22.12 qualifies separate cursor/scheduling semantics with synthetic PipeWire frames. Input replies cannot block capture/authority; damage must retain post-gap changes. Fresh GNOME consent fails HOST_CONSENT_TIMEOUT, so distribution tests establish no live-GNOME latency. October 5 user waiver covers udesk24 performance only.

entries.title: Wayland legacy MemFd capture compatibility
entries.summary: Readable authorized MemFd frames must work when older producers omit MAPPABLE. The repair validates size/aligned offset/pixel range before mapping; 19 native tests pass. The normal udesk24 product reproduces CAPTURE_LAYOUT_UNSUPPORTED, but repaired real GNOME capture and complete release qualification remain unpassed.

entries.title: Wayland capture pool optimization evidence
entries.summary: Native 0.22.14 replaces full-frame copies with a bounded pool.36 native tests pass. Alternating udesk24 synthetic 1440p60/x264 improves encoded 46.86–48.06→59.90 FPS and capture 19.34–19.96→2.64–2.79 ms; paint ACK improves too. This is not live GNOME or physical-input certification.

entries.title: Current-desktop acceptance method
entries.summary: Qualify the desktop contract using published dependencies/GOWORK=off. Preserve failures and meet agreed-host thresholds before acceptance; integration, a picture, admitted input or synthetic fixture cannot substitute for real performance. The acceptance record owns measured results and remaining work.

entries.title: Current-desktop qualification results
entries.summary: Native 0.22.6 passes scoped Mac/X11 office, performance and ten-minute queue/input checks. Mac minima 57.582/57.657 FPS cover 1080p/1440p. udesk24 is functional-only with retained Wayland failures; 0.22.7 owns later reconnect tests. Integration proves neither full release acceptance nor hardware encoding/parity.

entries.title: Remote desktop latency and NVIDIA encoding
entries.summary: Native 0.22.29 physical-seat and 0.22.10 X11/NVIDIA lanes measure different paths. X11 candidate click P95 improves 84.8→71.7 ms(light),88.3→75.2 ms(scroll), with lower decode-to-draw. Results qualify named hardware/configurations only, not photons, universal GPUs, zero-copy or WAN behavior.

entries.title: Remote desktop drag latency
entries.summary: October 4 X11/Floe 0.81.6 over Desktop SSH/HTTP 2 observes lower drag latency on i7-14700KF/RTX4090D/1080p60. Four baseline P95s84.06–86.51 ms and three candidate 69.13–74.06 ms retain all runs. Correlated frames cannot establish physical-photon latency or NoMachine parity.

entries.title: Physical desktop responsiveness and local input
entries.summary: Native v0.22.33 wakes idle capture; Floe owns bounded pointer/local text. Media/viewer contracts own authority/modes; locks are physical-only and generation/mode changes revoke input. Document contents, DRM feedback and encoded arrival are separate checks. udesk26 passes; Orange AFBC follow-up owns later repair. Native success is not complete Viewer/performance acceptance.

entries.title: Orange AFBC capture qualification
entries.summary: Native 0.22.34 decodes Orange 1920×1080 Wayland legacy AFBC through EGL. Real pixels/lock/unlock and udesk26 regression pass; unsupported layouts reject. Input still requires privileged service/fresh paint. Native checks do not certify product update, browser/network latency or physical photons.

entries.title: Physical-device remote desktop Viewer qualification
entries.summary: Native 0.22.34 on udesk26 qualifies real Viewer picture/input, assisted Unicode, physical unlock, switching, fullscreen/disconnect and ten socket-loss recoveries. Median recovery 2015.7 ms/P95 2230.2 ms excludes photons. Real IME, matched cursor, command RTT, complete Orange acceptance and parity remain unqualified.

entries.title: Orange remote desktop Viewer follow-up
entries.summary: Orange 0.22.37 passes thirteen release jobs and Viewer Unicode/lock/unlock/input/media checks. Mac Pinyin is deferred; host Pinyin unvalidated. Improved paired latency/FPS does not erase missing idle responses/SSH recovery failures or later RustDesk tails/disconnects; measured LAN loss limits comparison.

entries.title: Physical desktop RustDesk comparison
entries.summary: Full RustDesk parity/historical repeatability remain unaccepted. Native v0.22.48 six-frame, three rounds: mean FPS 46.21 vs 32.54; pooled P95 310.60 vs 207.59 ms; >250ms gaps nine vs three. Round three reaches 53.04 FPS/150.20ms with no gaps, but cannot replace adverse round one. Preserve safeguards; C05/decision ledger own results and experiments.

entries.title: LAN desktop experiment decision ledger
entries.summary:
The LAN record shows a measured deficit without establishing its cause or full
RustDesk parity. The published v0.22.48 six-frame path reached 53.04 FPS in one
round, but did not restore three-round stability. C01-C03 hypotheses were
rejected; C04 supports optional Linux six-frame delivery as a throughput
diagnostic only. C05 owns current paired results and remaining limits.

entries.title: Published LAN C05 outcomes and unresolved boundaries
entries.summary: C05 owns results under the comparison contract; preparation owns immutable inputs/controls. Six-frame delivery exceeds 51 FPS but does not restore three-round stability or RustDesk parity. Count adverse complete trials. Lost source inputs invalidate ordinal latency; missing presentation with all inputs is failure. Retry only named fixture repairs or discriminating hypotheses recorded in the ledger.

entries.title: Published six-frame LAN qualification C05
entries.summary:
The primary qualification task owns C05. The optional six-frame implementation
must use a published native module and preserve four-frame legacy/macOS behavior,
confirmed paint, generation/order fences and finite admission. C04 establishes a
diagnostic throughput benefit, not released recovery or full RustDesk parity.
The [comparison contract](remote-desktop-rustdesk-comparison-results.md) owns
acceptance. A failed release gate or invalid fixture stops qualification; retain
its evidence and repair the named failure before retrying.

entries.title: Remote desktop platform reacceptance
entries.summary: October 17 task-owned reacceptance uses consumer 7230cf1ae40316efed23c6ff572d03656aded6cc, epoch 62, native Go 0.23.3/Swift 0.22.27/Electron 41.10.7. Actual pixels/input qualify named platform behaviors only; service startup alone proves neither Runtime authentication nor capture. Audio, latency, hotplug and first-time TCC remain excluded.

entries.title: Desktop reconnect qualification results
entries.summary: Native 0.22.7 reconnects Linux/macOS AudioWorklet sound and requires fresh paint for input. X11 two 100-sample rounds yield 66.5/67.6 ms input-paint P95. Mac lock/hotplug and Wayland mode recovery are separately scoped; udesk24 performance stays unpassed and functional-only.

entries.title: Wayland desktop qualification results
entries.summary: udesk24 GNOME 46/native 0.22.7 passes office/mode recovery but still fails 1080p/1440p scrolling at 27.458/23.458 FPS after authorized graphics provisioning. User designated functional-only on October 2. Preserve failures; X11 and synthetic fixtures cannot replace them or certify three passing repetitions/window-motion.

entries.title: Host application catalog and owned native sessions
entries.summary: Redeven owns discovery, authorization and independent client sharing leases for host-user apps, without containers/VMs. Open admits/resumes sharing; last-viewer closure ends transport, not the process. Quit/confirmed force quit are explicit. Linux recovery is verified; macOS uses OS inventory. Missing capability/capture never proves exit.

entries.title: Cross-platform host application behavior
entries.summary: Viewing, sharing, closing windows and ending processes are distinct on every OS. Ordinary actions preserve unsaved work and app cancellation; only confirmed Force quit bypasses saving. Backend facts drive supported controls. Session/display policy remains authoritative and unavailable recovery cannot silently relaunch.

entries.title: Linux application instances and independent sharing
entries.summary: Redeven owns Linux instances, authorization and ephemeral shares; Floe Native Apps owns GIO/process observation. Applications outlive viewers and window count. Closing a share or Runtime never requests termination. Recovery requires original user/private state plus matching kernel process generation and endpoint; persisted PID alone never permits signaling. Reboot, display destruction or external cgroup cleanup can end dependent apps.

entries.title: Client input for host applications
entries.summary: Published Floe remote-input owns viewer keyboard/composition. Clients own input method/preedit/candidates; hosts deliver confirmed Unicode/keys to the painted window. Each operation has one output owner. Binding loss cancels composition/releases keys; reconnect never replays. Unsupported old protocols require save/quit/reopen without automatic process termination. Flower, terminals and editors keep their own input.

entries.title: Pointer gestures for host applications
entries.summary: Floe remote-pointer owns Linux/Xpra/macOS viewer gestures: swipe scroll, tap click, long press drag/right-click. Bind each to one painted window/generation. Cancellation drops queued movement/scroll and releases owned buttons. Remote-input owns composition. Missing capability requires save/quit/reopen; viewer closure neither upgrades nor stops the app.

entries.title: Host application display and window layout
entries.summary: Published Floe Native Apps owns Linux display configuration, constraints and cursor coordinates. Redeven declares layout/quality; Desktop owns actual maximize/minimize. Remote receipts cannot create resize loops, and unchanged configuration preserves canvases without commands. Old display backends retain logical density with explicit high-resolution limits; apps never auto-restart.

entries.title: Native Linux host application picture streams
entries.summary: Floe Native Apps owns capture, region encoding and composition. Redeven presents preferences/measurements. Only composed pixels authorize input/ACK; quality changes retain process/connection identity. Malformed/incompatible frames need explicit recovery; surviving legacy sessions remain viewable under the display contract.

entries.title: Host application viewer resources and layered upgrades
entries.summary: Published Floe Native Apps owns immutable `PreparedViewer` documents/assets, digests and capabilities. Redeven pins one snapshot per authorized Xpra share. Compatible surviving apps reconnect after viewer/Runtime updates without PID/content changes. Preparation failure offers retry, never historical resources. Backends and loaded modules retain process lifetimes without hot swaps.

entries.title: Host application viewer state and recovery
entries.summary: Runtime/native events own app facts and bootstrap owns viewing. Decoded pixels precede input; transport loss never proves exit. Reconnect keeps process identity. Only confirmed final-window/app closure dismisses an established viewer; terminal pages remain readable and application/titlebar authorities stay separate.

entries.title: Host application platforms and initialization
entries.summary: Floe Native Apps owns Linux graphics/package/service adaptation; Redeven owns catalog, authorization, instance and viewer. Default private Wayland/Xwayland or explicit preselected X11-only Xpra needs no full desktop/monitor. Never retry another backend. Snap/Flatpak need installed runtimes/services; missing capabilities fail explicitly.

entries.title: macOS application picture quality and delivery
entries.summary: The native helper owns resolution/encoding; viewer owns preferences/statistics. Current-generation decoding precedes acknowledgement. Quality/reconnect preserves app identity and native-session permissions/input. Unavailable video selects explicit image transport; report actual producing transport. Capture failures retain the existing reconnect boundary.

entries.title: Native macOS host applications
entries.summary: Redeven discovers installed macOS bundles and opens real apps as the Runtime user. Trusted Desktop Local routes launch directly; remote routes capture the selected app's actual windows, including existing single-instance processes. [Application authorization](host-applications.md) gates every operation/stream. Missing graphical login or permissions blocks capture; disconnect preserves the app and reconnect binds the same process.

entries.title: macOS application window lifecycle
entries.summary:
Redeven's native helper owns macOS application-window lifetime. Its registry binds
exact AX windows to the selected process instance; capture surfaces do not define
window lifetime. Only confirmed destruction can start the last-window grace.
Uncertain inventory, unavailable capture and transport loss retain the session and
its recovery entrypoint while revoking stale input. Runtime preserves the helper's
explicit end reason; the shared viewer owns whether an established page can close.

entries.title: macOS application menu scope
entries.summary: The helper exposes single-app menus, removing Apple/cross-app visibility branches before handles exist. Keep native titles literal. Only an enabled current leaf with verified live ancestry executes; stale/rejected actions retain app/capture and localized errors. Inspect menus only on explicit requests/actions, never launch/first frame.

entries.title: macOS application capture process ownership
entries.summary: One Manager-owned lazy Swift helper serves catalog, application and remote-desktop sessions for a Runtime. Suspend only the selected capture; identity, permissions, input, credit and cleanup stay independent. Helper failure ends sharing, not apps; explicit reopen may restart it. The native session contract owns OS permission and process/window validation.

entries.title: macOS application management and graceful quit
entries.summary: Redeven owns management UI and authenticated actions; OS owns liveness and apps own saving/cancelled quit. Manage running apps without sharing. Quit validates original process generations; never force-kill, retarget or infer exit from acceptance. Stale/unavailable targets retain sharing and actionable errors. Native sessions own capture, input and viewer closure.

entries.title: Prepare Linux hosts for native applications
entries.summary: Published Floe Native Apps supplies managed Wayland/Xwayland; the library owns preparation/recovery and Desktop can transfer verified offline archives. No full desktop/monitor is needed. Snap/Flatpak require installed runtimes/services; missing prerequisites get explicit guidance, never automatic system/security changes. Platform/preparation contracts apply; refresh after admin changes.

entries.title: Host application distribution validation
entries.summary: Historical Xpra userspace checks certify only their tested stack, not host policy. Current combined-backend, sandbox and product evidence belongs to desktop/package validation; platform contracts own capability/isolation. Missing subscriptions, CPU translation and untested policy remain explicit. Administrators use the setup route.

entries.title: Host application picture performance
entries.summary:
The [display contract](../architecture/host-application-display.md) owns picture
behavior. Floe Native Apps owns capture, encoding and region decoding; Redeven owns
forwarding, picture choices and acceptance. Measure pixels and bytes, not limits.
Failed budgets retain their raw result and block the associated claim. Documents
do not certify video, WAN, physical displays or universal remote-desktop parity.

entries.title: Host application input validation
entries.summary: Qualify client input using real application receipts/saved bytes. Upstream owns native/Xpra adapters; Redeven verifies viewer, authorized transport, launch/recovery. Request dispatch or DOM focus is insufficient. Existing apps retain backends/resources. Simulated events cannot certify real system candidates or physical mobile input; those require separate acceptance.

entries.title: Linux desktop and package compatibility validation
entries.summary: Real processes, native input and saved files qualify the named platform/source. Floe Native Apps owns reusable graphics/package evidence; Redeven owns launch, viewing and recovery. Prototype success cannot certify the exact release, arbitrary applications, physical GPUs or untested desktop versions.

entries.title: Host application platform validation
entries.summary:
Host application platform acceptance records real installed-stack and native
session evidence under the [platform contract](../architecture/host-application-platforms.md).
The matrix identifies exactly which userspace, Runtime, CPU and display combinations
were exercised. Container or translated-CPU results cannot certify host boot,
kernel, security policy or native hardware behavior. Missing permissions, unavailable
subscriptions and untested environments remain unqualified; they never become
successful simulated acceptance.

entries.title: Host application cursor acceptance
entries.summary:
The [viewer contract](../architecture/host-application-viewer.md) owns cursor
geometry; published `floe-native-apps` owns its implementation. Acceptance checks
decoded images and application click receipts separately from the operating
system's displayed pointer. A CSS declaration or ordinary page screenshot cannot
qualify physical pointer appearance. Unavailable devices remain unpassed.

entries.title: Host application lifecycle acceptance
entries.summary: Qualify process, window, decoded-frame and authenticated-viewer facts independently under application authorization/window-lifecycle contracts. Only confirmed closure ends physical viewers. Missing/inaccessible surfaces preserve apps and recovery, never retarget processes or inject stale input. Cross-platform operations retain OS differences; this is not all-app certification.

entries.title: Portable native Runtime binaries
entries.summary:
The shared Runtime builder owns native terminal linkage for Runtime and Gateway.
Linux artifacts run on glibc and musl systems without a host dynamic loader;
Darwin artifacts require a matching Apple builder. Missing native tools fail
preflight. Linux releases must include matching source and relink materials for
the statically linked LGPL library, and publication fails when that kit is absent.

entries.title: Desktop loopback Web Service access
entries.summary: Desktop-only `desktop_loopback` gives one Environment session/forward a random `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` origin while every request follows its protected Runtime route. It never connects directly, changes interfaces, modifies applications or falls back to unified proxy. Closing the owning window/Environment removes the gateway and authority.

entries.title: Web Service system-browser authorization
entries.summary: Runtime alone admits system-browser access to Desktop-private `unified_proxy` services. Desktop requests a short-lived single-use entry for an exact forward/path; Runtime redeems it into a Host-only session on `pf-<forward_id>.localhost:<bridge_port>`. Bridge credentials stay out of browsers and browser credentials out of services. Failure opens no URL; `desktop_loopback` is excluded.

entries.title: Managed Web Service opening
entries.summary: Released templates own entrance parsing; Runtime owns verified preparation/persistence, Desktop navigation and Env App display. Host/Container/Compose open current verified entrances through protected Forward, including running upgraded instances. No restart, upgrade or data change; HTTP 401 proves availability only. Unsafe/unverified entrances fail with recovery, never stop healthy apps.

entries.title: Managed Web Service Templates
entries.summary: The released `redeven-service-templates` module owns built-in identity, specifications, releases, localization, icons and service-specific notices. Redeven embeds a reproducible digest-verified offline bundle. Recommendations set defaults, never constrain source choices or replace installed releases. Malformed, missing, mismatched or future content blocks startup without local-definition fallback.

entries.title: Redeven Service Template format compatibility
entries.summary: Released template code owns schemas, historical adapters and current types; Runtime owns execution/authorization. Supported old directories retain bytes, filenames, modes, digest and commit. Adapt only in memory into one executor; no persisted definitions or automatic lifecycle effects. Invalid, ambiguous, future or unsupported formats fail unchanged with explicit recovery.

entries.title: GitHub service template sources
entries.summary: Upstream owns acquisition/format validation; Redeven owns authenticated import, review and active-source pointer. Import public/private GitHub templates via Desktop or Runtime without git. Credentials are request-scoped. No background updates, installs, scripts or restarts. Failure preserves active source and blocks only its template; no old-definition fallback.

entries.title: Independent Host service lifecycle
entries.summary: Applications own execution; Redeven owns authorized lifecycle, native identity, launch records and opening validation. Desktop/Runtime restart or upgrade preserves launched PID/generation. No supervisor, app-specific driver, output pipe or PID-only authority. Distinguish absence/mismatch/uninspectability; only proven absence permits startup, and opening failure never stops the app.

entries.title: Managed Web Services
entries.summary: Redeven owns service instances, bindings, resources, operations and protected forwards; verified external templates define behavior. One generic engine handles Host, Container and Compose installation, lifecycle, recovery and uninstall. Registry state and exact resource identity are authoritative. Invalid catalog, release, ownership, permission or health facts fail closed without adopting unknown resources.

entries.title: Web Service management recovery
entries.summary: Registry owns lifecycle records/transactions; Manager observes resources and available actions; Renderer presents current state, last result and next step. Unavailable inspection is not absence; historical failure is not current state. Destruction requires fresh ownership/explicit cleanup. Authorized detach works with an offline engine but preserves resources and claims no process stop.

entries.title: Service resource ownership
entries.summary: Registry records allocations/identity; engine/filesystem inspection proves current facts. Instances across Runtime state roots get independent default data/workspaces. Names grant no ownership; stopped containers count. External/unverified legacy resources cannot become deletable. Uncertainty preserves resources for review; upgrades never move/copy running data.

entries.title: Managed Service operation progress
entries.summary: A Manager Reporter owns live operation output; Registry owns history. One operation ID preserves drawer disclosure and brief completion through list/stream refresh. Redact safe command templates before persistence; output never defines Runtime identity. Persistence, capture or stream failures must not expose secrets, URL queries, private paths or control characters.

entries.title: Managed Service release discovery and updates
entries.summary: Configured npm/OCI registries own release metadata; Redeven validates candidates, installed identity, updates and rollback. Users explicitly select compatible releases without a Redeven version service. Discovery never installs; recommendations are defaults only. Expiring opaque IDs are revalidated at execution. Failure preserves healthy service and last-success summaries without implicit installation.

entries.title: Managed Service version interaction
entries.summary: Redeven owns version selection; Manager owns exact update-plan admission. Users select and submit in one drawer. Preparation executes nothing, only changed required notices need confirmation, and selection/browsing survives preparation or admission failure. Accepted operations retain their existing controller after drawer closure; source failures stay actionable in place.

entries.title: Managed Service Instance Configuration
entries.summary: The verified current template owns Runtime baseline; Redeven owns overrides, exact release, digest, Resource Plans, secrets, journals and rebuilds. Renderer owns an unsaved draft. One resolver combines baseline and differences. Runtime apply requires stopped state, current revision, exact plan and risk checks; invalid input fails before commit and failed rebuild restores prior state or reports rollback failure.

entries.title: Runtime Service snapshot
entries.summary: The Runtime Service snapshot is a typed boundary between Runtime, Desktop, Local UI, and optional Gateway supervision. Runtime protocol/version, compatibility epoch, capabilities, service readiness, and workload identity are explicit facts. Gateway is optional for Runtime startup and ordinary access; its absence only closes Redeven-managed lifecycle actions.

entries.title: Runtime session permission gates
entries.summary: Runtime validates session metadata and supported app/channel pairs before intersecting control-plane and local policy. Code App and Port Forward add their own gates. Read permits existing monitor/process observations; process termination independently requires execute and cannot inherit authority from visibility.

entries.title: Runtime system monitoring
entries.summary: Monitor owns one CPU/memory/network/process snapshot for page and Workbench. All OS-marked loopback interfaces are excluded from the shared network counters/rates. Failed network samples never enter history or fall back to unfiltered totals; later samples recover independently while other metrics remain usable.

entries.title: Runtime transport dependencies
entries.summary: Runtime composes Transport v3 and published Flowersec connection/session/RPC/stream primitives; Floeterm owns terminal lifecycle. Each Env App shares one current protocol session across RPC and live streams. Desktop SSH placement HTTP/2 is separate and does not redefine Flowersec wire or public SDK behavior.

entries.title: Runtime artifact spend and control pool
entries.summary: Remote control and data artifacts are opaque, single-spend capabilities. Redeven binds each Lease to one digest-global tombstone, persists idempotent bootstrap and top-up request identities, and rejects stale, duplicate, malformed, expired, or cross-environment responses before a connection can consume them. Pool replenishment and relink are terminal state transitions, never silent fallback.

entries.title: Runtime terminal lifecycle
entries.summary: Floeterm terminal-go owns each PTY, native Ghostty VT, geometry, controller epoch, input encoding, semantic history, clear/reset, and atomic Presentation. Redeven maps permissions, session metadata, and Activity/Workbench placement around that actor; browser views consume bounded semantic streams and never become a second terminal state machine.

entries.title: Product RPC request encoding
entries.summary:
Redeven request codecs own product JSON construction; published Flowersec owns
transport validation and dispatch. File creation accepts empty content and
omitted encoding. Absent optional fields must be omitted, while explicit false
and empty content retain their meanings. Invalid request objects fail before
dispatch and require a codec correction, not transport retries or relaxed
validation.

entries.title: Git workspace inventory lifecycle
entries.summary: Git workspace queries produce bounded immutable process-local snapshots; paged/path reads bind exact revisions. Git and Files mutations share repository/topology coordination and invalidate affected snapshots before and after effects. Display state never authorizes mutation. Oversized, stale, malformed or exhausted requests return small typed errors while the Flowersec session remains usable.

entries.title: Env App upstream web dependencies
entries.summary:
Env App adapts published floe-webapp UI/runtime and protocol, FloeBrowser projection, Floeterm terminal-web, and Flowersec artifact helpers into the Redeven shell.

Pins are Floe Webapp Boot, Core, and Protocol v0.86.73 (Env App Core v0.86.73), FloeBrowser v0.1.28, Floeterm terminal-web v0.19.2, and Flowersec Core v5.11.1. Floeterm supplies semantic Presentation and session exports.

[Page asset recovery](../ui/page-asset-recovery.md) uses Floe's document asset monitor and per-view error boundary for deployment and lazy imports.

entries.title: Env App terminal and surface composition
entries.summary: Env App adapts Floeterm PTY facts and Floe shell/focus/selection/KeepAlive. Redeven owns product views and localized controls. Runtime nodes stay keyed by session ID across views. Visible panes paint independently; active session owns input/search/commands.

entries.title: Env App connection and recovery
entries.summary: Env App uses Floe's published artifact-source and connection-controller contracts for public HTTPS, explicit HTTP, remote controlplane, and Desktop-private loopback paths. It binds each source to the current origin and environment, requires exact Service Worker control, and projects Flowersec diagnostics into one immutable recovery snapshot without replaying requests or inventing retry policy.

entries.title: Whole-window status surfaces
entries.summary: Floe owns window layout/artwork/retry/shimmer; Redeven maps actual connection/access/Desktop state. Recovery/access uses opaque neutral backgrounds over retained inert workspace, without duplicate disconnect notices. Floating windows, widgets and drag content exclude this material. Preserve recovery owner/actions; appearance grants no access or second loop.

entries.title: Env App page asset recovery
entries.summary: Floe owns asset comparison/view isolation; Redeven owns authenticated entry, secure trigger, localization and explicit reload. Connected Runtime does not prove old page modules still load. Changed builds/import failures expose recovery instead of endless placeholders. Never reload over drafts; notices stay inside active content below unchanged shell/native controls.

entries.title: ReDevPlugin host integration boundary
entries.summary: Redeven consumes the coordinated published ReDevPlugin Go, npm, Rust and machine-contract artifacts without forking platform mechanics. It owns session mapping, source policy/review, placement, product runtime builds and business adapters. Missing/unverifiable identity, lifecycle, interaction, package or runtime contracts fail closed without local compatibility or sibling-source fallback.

entries.title: ReDevPlugin Redeven adapters
entries.summary: Redeven owns only the adapters that bind authenticated product sessions, source policy, business capabilities, and Activity or Workbench placement to released ReDevPlugin contracts. ReDevPlugin remains the authority for host protocol, package trust, runtime execution, and platform state. Adapter failures stop at the product boundary and never create copied platform state or implicit grants.

entries.title: Plugin platform integration
entries.summary: Redeven mounts released ReDevPlugin through one Go Host, HTTP namespace, Env App client and surface scope. Published Process Supervisor runs a verified product-built Linux/Darwin runtime. Redeven adds authenticated sessions, source policy, placement and business adapters; upstream owns package, state, protocol, trust and execution. Missing or unproven identities fail closed.

entries.title: Plugin process sessions
entries.summary: ReDevPlugin Process Broker alone owns plugin processes; Redeven supplies authenticated scope, permissions, minimal environment, secrets, state and diagnostics/audit. Opaque handles expose bounded binary stdio, never a second protocol. Overflow may lose output; Host close, disable, uninstall, revocation and owner teardown stop owned processes.

entries.title: Plugin background entries
entries.summary: ReDevPlugin owns headless Worker lifecycle and durable intervals. Redeven supplies environment permission policy and presents verified status through ordinary plugin management. No hidden surface, host scheduler, replay endpoint or second Worker protocol is involved.

entries.title: Plugin package and runtime lifecycle
entries.summary: ReDevPlugin owns package trust, inspection, installation, runtime readiness, release cache, and durable lifecycle. Redeven supplies authenticated source policy, review presentation, and localized outcomes. Every source follows inspect, explicit confirmation, and released Host installation; unverified bytes, stale trust, missing runtime identity, or uncertain mutation outcomes fail closed.

entries.title: Plugin surface recovery and permissions
entries.summary: Env App owns one authenticated plugin client, one shared scope, and one installation observer. ReDevPlugin remains the authority for inventory, Executions, Events, permissions, revocation, and runtime recovery. Closing or reconnecting a panel preserves the exact request identity and authoritative outcome; a product refresh never becomes a second mutation or recovery lifecycle.

entries.title: Plugin market consumption
entries.summary: Redeven atomically refreshes the validated latest-only catalog from `https://plugins.redeven.com` and exposes it only to trusted Env App. Market metadata identifies GitHub Releases; it neither hosts packages nor grants trust or installs. Exact declared assets enter released ReDevPlugin verification. Invalid responses fail closed; validated last-known-good data may support stale discovery, never automatic updates.

entries.title: Native container operation observation
entries.summary: Every Containers mutation has one durable operation ID and resource lock in containerresource. Submission, progress, cancellation and restart reconciliation share that owner. Inventory/UI never create another lifecycle; stale plans, lost replies or unavailable engines remain explicit without automatic replay.

entries.title: Native container resources
entries.summary: Native container management uses one `containerengine` Docker/Podman execution layer shared with Web Services. `containerresource` alone owns native mutations, persistence and reconciliation. Managed Web Service resources are visible but read-only here. Unknown targets, stale preflights, uncertain outcomes and failed authoritative reads fail closed without mutation replay.

entries.title: Container runtime execution
entries.summary: containerengine owns Docker/Podman discovery and execution. Each request binds engine, endpoint and canonical resource. Observe engines independently without probing inactive contexts or changing global selection. Failures stay explicit, never empty success or fallback; resource mutations retain their own admission owner.

entries.title: Volume usage observation
entries.summary: The engine supplies bounded volume observations to authenticated active Runtime resources. References include stopped containers and sizes mean occupied bytes, not capacity. Partial inspection proves no unused state. Failed size reads preserve inventory with unavailable metrics; mutations still require current preflight.

entries.title: Container engine service management
entries.summary: One `ContainerServiceController` owns Docker/Podman service discovery, lifecycle, configuration, preflight identity and reconciliation. Opaque IDs hide endpoints. Host mutation requires full RWX and Admin without privilege elevation. Unknown ownership/revision/final state fails closed; interrupted work cannot be replayed.

entries.title: Native container console
entries.summary: Containers provides native Activity and Workbench views over [authorized targets](container-resources-capability.md). The console owns selection/navigation; [resource snapshots](../ui/env-resource-cache.md) owns shared presentation/refresh. Old-target responses cannot commit, UI exposes no endpoint selector, and every lifecycle mutation remains within `containerresource`.

entries.title: Runtime access sessions
entries.summary: Runtime accessgate alone owns ordinary validity/revocation. Valid browser sessions survive refresh/tabs/disconnect; cookie names isolate HTTP/HTTPS/ports without extending authority. Expiry/logout/security changes/restart require reauthentication. Invalid authority/incompatible Desktop fails closed; two-factor contract owns credentials and host recovery.

entries.title: Runtime two-factor authentication
entries.summary: Runtime accessgate owns authentication independently of Cloud. MFA requires password then TOTP/single-use recovery for browser/direct/Cloud sessions; password challenge grants no application access. Native/SSH management has separate authority, never inferred from loopback, Cloud admin or headers. Missing/corrupt state fails closed; recovery blocks access until new credentials commit.

entries.title: Local UI network exposure
entries.summary: New Runtime endpoints explicitly use HTTP localhost:23998; network exposure retains local access and requires fixed port/effective password. HTTPS is separate with strict certificate/trust checks. Pages and WS/WSS share the public port. TLS failure never downgrades; private Desktop bridge cannot become public fallback.

entries.title: Local UI certificates
entries.summary: Runtime validates saved HTTPS identity; registered Desktop management exposes explicit create/import/regenerate/remove. Validity, trust and operation result are independent. Never silently replace identity/install trust. Invalid imports preserve the pair; changes affect next HTTPS start, not running sessions. Default HTTP needs no certificate.

entries.title: Permission policy and filesystem scope
entries.summary:
Redeven treats endpoint runtime policy as authoritative. Control-plane grants can authorize a session, but the runtime clamps those grants with a local permission policy and file-facing features use explicit filesystem root policy.

Runtime permissions are clamped by local policy and file features are scoped by directory root policy.

entries.title: Plugin platform integration security
entries.summary: ReDevPlugin receives authenticated host identity/source policy, never browser-claimed ownership/trust. HTTP checks auth, origin, CSRF and closed-action policy; direct calls check owner/action/resource. Package provenance, signature, execution approval, update eligibility and permission are independent. Integrity, runtime identity or scope mismatch fails closed.

entries.title: Verified Environment access routes
entries.summary: Desktop associates Gateway routes only after matching member ID, Runtime public ID and paired Gateway key against trusted management facts. Health is independently verified; names/URLs/catalogs/renderer claims grant no association. Local/Cloud ownership remains separate. Changed/unverified routes stay separate; missing default requires explicit replacement, never login/management authority.

entries.title: Host application component cache
entries.summary: Published artifactcache owns verification, locking and eviction. Desktop supplies its private directory, seven-day idle retention and 2 GB budget plus document-local transfers/UI. Devices reuse verified archives; cancellation retains completed cache. Unknown catalogs fail and cleanup cannot negate successful preparation.

entries.title: Desktop qualification lifecycle
entries.summary: The Desktop supervisor owns scenario/resource/cleanup deadlines and final status. Acceptance leaves no owned Electron/Runtime/bridge/fixtures. Preserve production Quit and independent Runtime lifetime; names, generic ports or foreground state grant no stop authority. Timeout/interruption/unexpected exit/force/cleanup/residue fails with retained diagnostics and explicit manifest cleanup.

entries.title: Desktop development sessions and bundles
entries.summary:
- Authority: launcher owns Desktop, local Runtime, saved Gateways and bundles.
- Outcome: run current source, stop together, prune old bundles.
- Invariants: preserve data, identities, unrelated services and recent/selected/live bundles.
- Failure: preparation cleans up; incomplete inventory prevents pruning.

entries.title: Desktop Web Service browser window
entries.summary: Desktop owns protected target views, toolbar, navigation and cleanup over Runtime-authorized Web Service routes. Reopen reuses the same live forward; content gets no Desktop bridge. Invalid navigation rejects, while marked upstream failure offers local retry without reauthorizing or restarting the app.

entries.title: Desktop host application titlebar
entries.summary: The Redeven bootstrap owns host application toolbar presentation; macOS capture and Xpra remain the command and session authorities. Desktop provides native window geometry through the restricted [application presentation boundary](web-service-browser-window.md). One compact titlebar exposes window selection, picture settings and normal close actions without another connection or startup wait. Disconnection disables unavailable actions while preserving the native window and retry path.

entries.title: Desktop shell theme state
entries.summary: Desktop owns global `system | light | dark` mode and remembered Floe light/dark presets. One validated snapshot drives Welcome, Env App, native chrome and generated documents. New/reset selections use Porcelain Light/Dark; valid choices survive upgrades. User changes paint pending feedback before asynchronous persistence, retain acknowledged state on failure and permit retry without losing mounted content, drafts or focus.

entries.title: Desktop runtime bridge
entries.summary: Desktop opens independently runnable Runtime through machine-readable startup, scoped transport and session contracts. Its process-local coordinator owns direct Local, WSL, SSH and container lifecycle. Gateway/Provider remain access routes. Runtime service, health, process and session observations cannot become competing owners; plugins use their released brokers rather than Desktop control credentials.

entries.title: Desktop Environment library
entries.summary: Welcome projects authoritative owners into one library. Exact Runtime/Cloud links share a card; paired Gateways add access tabs. Independent registrations remain separate. Grouping grants no permission or fallback transport. Unlink restores cards; Cloud failures preserve known entries with stale-result context.

entries.title: Desktop interaction continuity
entries.summary: Welcome owns interaction sessions; Launcher/Runtime own business operations. Observations retain open panels, draft, focus, selection, steps and scroll. Only explicit user transitions or current completion alter visibility. Invalid authority blocks submission with recovery; closing progress never cancels work.

entries.title: Environment card presentation
entries.summary: Environment cards preserve geometry across perspectives, snapshots, narrow layouts and long translations. Each perspective selects an explicit route without granting authority or falling back. Snapshots retain nodes, selection and focus; owner removal invalidates submission but retains open sessions.

entries.title: Desktop Welcome navigation
entries.summary: Welcome owns immediate local page selection. Flower/Environments navigation never waits for Launcher IPC, snapshots or Runtime preparation; visited pages retain state. Runtime readiness still gates Flower requests without blocking return navigation. Explicit Environment Center tab changes may animate destination cards, while refresh and retained-page return preserve stable headers and never replay entrance motion.

entries.title: Desktop Environment connections
entries.summary: Welcome and settings share a pure connection model derived from host access, placement, Runtime public addresses and health. Presentation never selects transport. Addresses retain their host/container namespace; missing or failed observations remain unconfirmed rather than proving process exit. Private bridge credentials never become browser, clipboard or QR targets. Explicit Stop clears addresses even when a prior window remains open.

entries.title: Desktop runtime readiness
entries.summary: Desktop admits a managed Environment only after its exact direct target reports compatible Runtime service and Local UI readiness. Gateway/Provider/URL access readiness is separate. Missing, stopped, outdated or damaged Runtime selects direct Start, Update or reinstall recovery. Startup status gaps remain bounded waits. Retained diagnoses preserve presentation only; current Presence and command-time validation own authority.

entries.title: Runtime platform facts and icons
entries.summary: Runtime owns OS/distribution facts; Desktop consumes recognized trusted observations and displays bundled original-color marks with localized names. Last-known facts survive disconnect, failed probes and restart until replaced online. Unknown platforms show a device mark without blocking supported Runtime. Display retains card geometry, selection and focus; client/provider identity never substitutes for Runtime OS.

entries.title: Desktop transport recovery
entries.summary: Each placement bridge owns HTTP/2, immutable recovery generation and registry identity. Its owner replaces stdio/session once, verifies process/Runtime, rejects late callbacks and disposes resources at one terminal boundary. Health observers or individual streams cannot independently restart transport.

entries.title: Desktop SSH runtime operations
entries.summary: Desktop manages SSH-host and SSH-container Runtime only through the saved connection and placement. One process-local lifecycle coordinator, Launcher Operation, transport lease and temporary helper serve Start, Stop, Restart, Update, Refresh, Open recovery and Reinstall. Gateway/Provider credentials never substitute for SSH authority. The target stores no Desktop lifecycle lock or supervisor state.

entries.title: Desktop WSL runtime operations
entries.summary: Windows 11 x64 runs Electron only: no native Local, Windows or local-container Runtime. Register initialized Linux x64 WSL2 distributions independently; manage only exact distribution/user Runtime. Windows owns WSL installation/lifecycle/removal. Missing/WSL1/uninitialized distributions, commands, damaged packages or lost Bridge fail visibly with explicit recovery.

entries.title: Desktop session and model source
entries.summary: Desktop publishes each Environment session's explicit target route and identity. Accepted Runtime Stop, Restart and Update invalidate attached sessions. One model-source process handle per session starts without delaying Env App; that process owns reconnects while provider credentials remain local. Persisted Flower history stays readable when the live model source is unavailable.

entries.title: Desktop Environment registration ownership
entries.summary: Each Environment action names one registration owner: `local_environment` for built-in Local, `runtime_target` for WSL/SSH/containers, `saved_environment` for URLs, or the Gateway-held member identity. Linked cards never choose storage or mutation behavior. Desktop serializes changes against current preferences, immediately publishes committed snapshots and fences late probes/Open tasks so removed registrations cannot reappear.

entries.title: Desktop environment settings
entries.summary: One settings window/session per Environment opens without waiting for access reads. Registration controls sections; explicit Environment IDs resolve registered management authority for every operation. Runtime owns access config. Failure preserves drafts/diagnosis; stale responses cannot alter newer opens. Cloud/URL/Gateway cannot read or save Local access settings.

entries.title: Desktop environment settings presentation
entries.summary: Desktop composes Floe dialogs/tabs/controls into one bounded settings surface. Theme tokens own material, product CSS grouping/geometry. Every page retains readable labels, reachable actions and draft ownership through loading/errors/disclosure. Settings sessions retain authority and persistence without styling state.

entries.title: Desktop SSH environment settings
entries.summary: SSH creation/editing share one form and registration API. Common controls precede advanced options, retained in an inspectable summary. Failures preserve drafts. Registration contracts own connections/secrets, while Environment settings owns the window, tab, draft and asynchronous recovery lifetime.

entries.title: Desktop runtime process lifecycle
entries.summary: One RuntimeLifecycleCoordinator owns managed Local/WSL/SSH/container operations through saved direct channels. First admission retains the target until terminal; conflicts return its identity without preemption/queueing. Gateway/Provider grant access only, and old process or renderer state cannot create another owner.

entries.title: Desktop managed Environment reinstall
entries.summary: Wipe reinstall is Desktop's recovery for a broken managed Runtime. After exact-target/root confirmation, Desktop verifies a Runtime package, attempts process stop, isolates/replaces the root, starts and verifies Runtime, then cleans old data. Old health, databases, journals or unknown process state cannot block the direct filesystem attempt. Preserve-data reinstall instead replaces managed files and rolls back when verification fails.

entries.title: Desktop application updates
entries.summary: One Desktop update coordinator serves Welcome, menus, command palette, settings, status and compatibility recovery. Packaged macOS uses signed architecture-specific Sparkle appcasts; Linux uses matching DEB/RPM metadata through `electron-updater`. Development, unsupported and misplaced macOS builds fail closed with manual recovery. Internal Windows NSIS builds expose no production feed and report updates unsupported.

entries.title: Gateway Cloud access
entries.summary: Gateway Cloud v3 manages a Gateway machine and its local directory. RCPP v5 independently enrolls and recovers a Runtime over either direct HTTPS or the selected Gateway proxy. Gateway local v6 owns membership, invitations and restricted egress. Cloud owns environment identity, Namespace ownership and approval. Runtime owns one Cloud association, one selected route and one Flowersec connection controller.

entries.title: Gateway client access
entries.summary: Gateway exposes two fixed paths: verified host administration and environment-only URL access. Clients cannot choose roles or persist management authority. Runtime lifecycle and application authentication remain independent; Cloud operations still require Cloud authorization.

entries.title: Gateway service
entries.summary: redeven-gateway owns durable membership, one-time invitations, client grants, policy and restricted forwarding. Runtime verifies address/code, previews signed enrollment then explicitly joins. Gateway never scans/dials Runtime addresses or manages Runtime lifecycle. LAN needs no Cloud; Gateway loss affects its paths, not independent management authority.

entries.title: Gateway network settings
entries.summary: Gateway independently owns admin-confirmed share endpoints, listeners and optional Host restrictions, saved atomically by verified host admin. Listener edits require explicit restart; live sockets persist. Empty restrictions allow hostnames without weakening TLS/invitation/member/Desktop authorization. Invalid input or failed writes preserve saved/live state.

entries.title: Gateway Desktop interactions
entries.summary: Desktop enrolls managed Local, SSH, WSL and container targets through one app-owned session. Runtime management, invitation verification and local consent remain separate authorities. Membership appears only after joining; observations preserve drafts, while confirmed faults require explicit recovery. No Runtime URL enrollment form exists.

entries.title: Gateway access sessions
entries.summary: Desktop opens a joined Runtime over its existing outbound Flowersec connection to Gateway. Gateway forwards bytes to the Runtime's fixed application entry; it has no Runtime URL to dial. TLS terminates in Desktop and Runtime. Password, MFA, Host/Origin checks and application authorization remain Runtime-owned. Access artifacts limit initial redemption; no Gateway timer shortens established business sessions.

entries.title: Gateway deployment qualification
entries.summary: Qualification must prove Runtime-to-Gateway connection direction and real application behavior. Unit tests alone do not establish Electron certificate handling, browser MFA, MySQL migration or an isolated network path. Record each command's actual result; source changes or installer builds are not proof that an application flow passed. These affected-feature checks are separate from release packaging and the aggregate push gate.

entries.title: CodeSpace system-browser access
entries.summary: Desktop resolves a trusted resource ID through the environment transport and opens an isolated short-lived loopback entry. Browser exchanges it for resource-bound HTTP/WS sessions; private bridge tokens never enter it. Runtime owns permissions, AccessGate and editor generation. Environment closure ends routes; failed open leaves no new authorized listener.

entries.title: Native Desktop CodeSpace access
entries.summary: Desktop owns each CodeSpace window, browser profile, protected loopback listener and selected route. Runtime owns editor generation, permissions and AccessGate. Editors use native HTTP/WebSockets without privileged preload or transport injection. Closing a window, revoking access or stopping an instance ends its connections. Route failure and occupied saved ports fail visibly without transport substitution or request replay.

entries.title: Browser Editor runtime
entries.summary: Browser Editor support is owned by the Code App app server. Codespaces are opened through Local UI `/cs/<id>/` routes or through remote `cs-*` sandbox hosts, while Desktop and Env App can prepare or update managed Browser Editor runtime versions through code workspace engine APIs.

entries.title: Flower MCP runtime
entries.summary: Redeven configures MCP and adapts the released official Go SDK, which owns stdio/Streamable HTTP sessions. Floret owns invocation, approval, one-shot effects, history/recovery. Add no second execution queue/lifecycle/retry authority. Unknown call outcomes are terminal and never replayed; invalid persisted config fails without changing bytes.

entries.title: Flower Agent Plugins
entries.summary: Flower loads Agent Plugins 1.0.0 as environment-scoped Skills and MCP extensions. This domain is separate from native `.redevplugin` packages, their SDK and marketplace. A manifest identifies a package; it does not register a marketplace listing or grant execution permission.

entries.title: Flower plugin catalog integration
entries.summary: Flower can consume an explicitly configured plugin directory without shipping or maintaining a default index. Runtime sources and user-managed sources use the same catalog reader and GitHub installation workflow. Catalog availability never owns installed plugin authority.

entries.title: Tessiven canvas
entries.summary: Tessiven maps services to Runtime cards, tinted groups and distinct external dependencies. Root connections give overview; focus reveals local relationships. Canvas owns pan/zoom while details remain selectable. Flower edits documents; the canvas progressively presents them without a parallel manual editor.

entries.title: Tessiven relationship summaries
entries.summary: Shared Tessiven projection summarizes group relationships: at most four collapsed patterns, one expanded pool overview and exact physical-node rows. Canonical endpoints, IDs and evidence remain unchanged. Search, filters and paging expose detail; missing visible endpoints suppress previews without substitutes.

entries.title: Tessiven canvas navigation and rendering
entries.summary: Floe owns layout, routing and viewport painting; Tessiven provides topology, controls and palette. Folding/filtering never rewrites documents. Canonical relationships remain inspectable while only the selected scope paints. Worker/data failures stay visible, retaining the last valid scene during ordinary view changes.

entries.title: Tessiven Flower replies
entries.summary:
Redeven presents canvas replies in a compact, themed floating reading window.
Flower owns the conversation, actions and live feedback; Floe owns window
geometry, pointer interaction and floating-layer projection. Hiding the window
keeps the composer and conversation alive. Errors, approvals and retry retain
their canonical Flower behavior rather than a canvas-specific recovery path.

entries.title: Runtime settings
entries.summary: Env App owns runtime settings destinations, localized drafts and API adapters; published Floe owns reusable layout/navigation. Narrow layouts remain usable and revisited panels retain draft/scroll. Authenticated APIs own writes; readers cannot edit administrator fields. Failures preserve input, while maintenance uses its existing controller after explicit confirmation.

entries.title: Flower extensions
entries.summary: Shared Flower owns retained Skills/MCP/Plugins management; both carriers supply typed authenticated adapters. The rail entry below New chat preserves draft/tab filters, with no duplicate runtime Skills destination. Readers inspect catalogs; administrators mutate configuration. Failures retain input and expose Retry, and every shipped locale supplies explicit copy.

entries.title: UI presentation transactions
entries.summary: Heavy navigation acknowledges selection synchronously, commits target visibility after that intent can paint, then performs focus, resize, scroll or measurement after content paint. Published Floe separates visual from committed values; Redeven applies this ordering across Activity, Workbench, terminal, Flower, Files/Git and heavy panels without duplicating business state.

entries.title: Env App floating layer order
entries.summary: Env App assigns global layers to movable windows, Flower, plugin surfaces, blocking modals and command UI. Interaction reorders only its window band. Published Floe owns visible-viewport constraints and drag geometry; Redeven persists settled geometry and preserves reachable controls, local scrolling and destination interaction.

entries.title: Dialog content placement
entries.summary:
Published Floe Webapp owns the shared Dialog structure. Redeven supplies localized
titles, body guidance, and actions. Headers contain identity and controls;
instructions and consequences belong in the body. This applies to ordinary
dialogs, confirmation dialogs, drawers, and window-local confirmations. A missing
or misplaced description is a content integration failure, never a reason to
restore a header subtitle or hide the text.

entries.title: Adaptive desktop layout
entries.summary: Native Desktop keeps desktop interaction. Browser mobile mode requires width below 768 CSS px, coarse primary pointer and no hover; narrow mouse windows keep Activity/Workbench. Floe observes layout and owns drawer focus; Redeven owns navigation. Automatic placement preserves saved navigation and collapse choices.

entries.title: Mobile shell navigation
entries.summary: Redeven owns mobile navigation; Floe owns viewport, presence and focus. Mobile hides the framework toolbar behind a fixed More action while keeping bottom navigation reachable. Covered content stays inert through exit, confirmations remain modal, and closing navigation preserves content and admitted operations.

entries.title: File preview window actions
entries.summary: Redeven owns file actions/drafts; published Floe supplies titlebar slots and window lifecycle. Desktop Activity and Workbench place compact actions beside the filename before window controls. Actions preserve permissions, text selection, download mapping and discard confirmation. Close fences pending work immediately while retaining visible content through retirement.

entries.title: File preview dismissal
entries.summary: The preview owner cancels reads immediately; Floe owns exit presence. Accepted close retains document/title through motion and releases resources at unmount, without blank iframes, brighter intermediate surfaces, extra reads or delays. Disposal always cleans up and late responses cannot revive closed content.

entries.title: File preview viewport and rendering
entries.summary: Redeven owns preview modes/identity; Floe owns sizing, PDF layers and static PPTX. Initial automatic fit may enlarge; resize preserves manual zoom. One owner renders each page and stale work cannot replace current content. Errors stay local, cancellation neutral, and incomplete HTML never executes.

entries.title: Static PPTX file preview
entries.summary: Floe parses/renders static PPTX; Redeven authorizes bytes and presents the reading surface. Local windowed slides retain text selection and zoom, with external resources disabled. Stale work cannot replace current source. Errors expose bounded recovery, and redistribution retains licenses and corresponding MPL source.

entries.title: HTML file preview
entries.summary: Redeven classifies files and authorizes reads/edits/placement; Floe constructs isolated HTML pages. Opening renders by default and source editing is explicit/write-authorized. Content cannot reach trusted Shell/resources. Oversized, incomplete or unreadable input never executes and retains localized recovery.

entries.title: Git workspace generation and Files decoration
entries.summary: Each Git projection belongs to one protocol client, repository and revision generation. Changes, Branches and Files have separate owners sharing monotonic invalidation. Files renders immediately and keeps committed decorations while a bounded replacement loads. Stale or invalidated responses cannot restore old state, including after unknown effects.

entries.title: Shared surface material
entries.summary: Published Floe owns material and motion. Env App/Welcome select soft-neumorphic roles while business content stays flat. Preserve input, portals, widget identity and hot interaction ownership. Resolve conflicts at the product override source without copying shadow logic or introducing another theme/dependency owner.

entries.title: Product accessibility for AI agents
entries.summary: Redeven owns names, descriptions, state and relationships while preserving geometry/styles/handlers/focus and hidden/inert exclusion. Published Floe owns reusable controls/focus/layers. Shared gaps require source/behavior evidence and released upstream fixes. Report audit scope accurately; accessibility changes alone certify neither full WCAG nor model performance.

entries.title: Input focus boundaries
entries.summary:
Published floe-webapp owns input focus presentation. Redeven supplies product
layout, semantic state, and one declared boundary for custom compound inputs.
Focus changes only the existing border color; geometry and decorative shadows
stay stable. Conflicting host styles fail source or browser checks and must be
removed at their owner. No fallback stylesheet overrides the released contract.

entries.title: Git browser visual states
entries.summary: Git file selection and inline diff inspection share a contained surface with independently owned request state. Floe interaction accent marks selection; semantic Git colors mark repository facts. Checked-out and inspected branches remain distinguishable when they coincide. Layout preserves local scrolling, keyboard actions and a current diff across widths and themes.

entries.title: Git diff request lifecycle
entries.summary: One shared Git panel owns preview/full-context reads by target, refresh revision, transport and mode. Stale responses cannot replace current content. Unchanged Workbench placement retains requests, content, expansion and scroll; target changes/refresh invalidate them. Missing transport waits for Shell recovery; empty/errors settle explicitly without automatic retries.

entries.title: Workbench interaction contracts
entries.summary: Workbench interaction is governed by explicit ownership contracts rather than widget-specific event heuristics.
