This overview is the canonical navigation point for input ownership and surface lifecycle. Focused concepts define wheel, pointer, text, terminal, selection, recovery, lazy loading, and shared overlay behavior without mixing those independent responsibilities into one retrieval unit.

entries.title: Workbench composition surfaces and editing
entries.summary: Published Floe owns composition rendering, direct editing, materials and anchored tools; Redeven owns localization, defaults and layout persistence. Native caret, selection and IME remain intact, with optional empty region names. Save/reopen preserves content, color, geometry and material; failed upgrades retain the prior supported layout.

entries.title: Workbench input ownership
entries.summary: Workbench input ownership is declared through explicit marker contracts so canvas zoom, local scrolling, pointer actions, and text selection remain distinguishable. A selected widget boundary does not automatically own wheel input, and local-scroll regions must declare their role rather than relying on incidental DOM structure. These contracts let the canvas remain predictable while nested product surfaces preserve native interaction.

entries.title: Workbench terminal interaction
entries.summary: Floeterm terminal-go owns PTY, native VT, geometry, controller epoch, semantic history and atomic Presentation. Released terminal-web renders one canvas per view and collects local input. Authority/renderer violations fail closed; auxiliary history or search errors stay local and retryable without disconnecting live output.

entries.title: Terminal fonts across client devices
entries.summary: Env App owns document-local terminal fonts. New preferences use bundled JetBrains Mono at size 12; existing IDs/sizes remain unchanged and each client resolves availability. Floeterm retains canonical cells, cursor and session grid. Font presentation cannot replace terminal authority or erase stored preferences.

entries.title: Terminal session groups
entries.summary: Runtime catalogs own groups, assignments and named views. Activity/Workbench share environment projection; expansion/active view stay local. Default is immutable; every session has one known group_id. Membership is independent of placement, cwd, controller identity and recovery.

entries.title: Official installation progress
entries.summary: ReDevPlugin owns the durable official-install Execution and its progress, idempotency, and recovery. Redeven observes that authority, presents exact market review and permission setup, and retains the operation when management closes. Response loss never creates a second installation. Only current authoritative inventory can expose a launch target; failed setup cannot revive stale permissions or remove saved canvas components.

entries.title: Plugin package review
entries.summary: ReDevPlugin owns inspection, validation and atomic mutations. Redeven presents the exact candidate/source/permissions before confirmation. Cancel affects only pre-submit inspection; unknown effects require reconciliation without replay. Updates preserve layout with fresh slots; only confirmed uninstall removes it.

entries.title: Plugin layout continuity
entries.summary: Redeven persists exact plugin widget/instance/surface identity and geometry; ReDevPlugin owns live authority. Upgrade, disable, permission/reconnect failures retain placement. Only explicit removal or confirmed exact-instance uninstall deletes it. Recovery reconciles unknown outcomes without focusing/rearranging the canvas or silently recreating authority.

entries.title: Workbench surface lifecycle
entries.summary: Workbench preserves widget identity across selection, activation, loading and recovery. Floe owns generic Dock focus; Redeven adds no visibility store. Selected Terminal local viewports own wheel input without DOM focus; unselected widgets remain Canvas-owned. Shell recovery makes retained content inert above the canvas, with overlays in the shared surface layer.

entries.title: File icon presentation
entries.summary: Floe owns filename recognition, SVG icons and palettes; Redeven supplies names, directory/link metadata and size. Formats retain reviewed distinctions and unknown files use the generic upstream icon. Icons confer no preview/execution/extraction authority, whose independent format and permission checks remain.

entries.title: Files context menus
entries.summary: Published Floe owns file-menu placement, measurement, scrolling, submenu gestures and dismissal. Redeven supplies workspace bounds, actions and localization. Menus remain eight CSS pixels inside Files/surface/visible-viewport intersection; invalid explicit bounds close them. Files never escapes its global layer or duplicates Workbench coordinate conversion.

entries.title: Plugin Center interaction
entries.summary: Redeven owns Plugin Center navigation; Floe owns dialogs, presence and input. Workbench uses a retained drawer and Activity the same directory page. Search/filter/selection/scroll persist. Closing management does not cancel Host execution; released ReDevPlugin owns lifecycle, permissions and surface authority.

entries.title: Plugin surfaces
entries.summary: Redeven owns plugin discovery, navigation and placement; released ReDevPlugin owns admission, surface authority, bridge sessions, confirmation and revocation. Activity and Workbench use independent SDK slots. Management preserves search/selection, exposes actionable failures and reconciles unknown outcomes against authoritative state.

entries.title: Flower thread Goals
entries.summary:
Published Floret owns the canonical Goal, model tool, reflection and completion.
Redeven authorizes mutations and presents the typed facts. One current Goal per
thread describes the desired result clearly and concisely without a text-length
recommendation, ceiling or truncation. Goal never depends on Todo. Stop, thread
navigation and recovery remain available; an unresolved request never claims a
successful mutation or completion.

entries.title: Flower command and composer flow
entries.summary: Each input intent has one request ID reused for retries; accepted receipts echo exact request/Thread IDs. New-thread HTTP nests it under create, existing-thread HTTP uses top-level client_request_id with URL-owned ThreadID. The short-lived outbox retains non-secret unconfirmed input/settings; composer, Stop, navigation and interactions remain usable during work.

entries.title: Flower Activity origin page references
entries.summary: A new desktop companion captures one removable origin snapshot without reads/editor replacement; existing threads do not. Opening with no selection/New refreshes it, later navigation/editing does not. Submission/retry use exact visible text and existing draft/transport recovery. Terminal context captures current screen like Ask Flower; omit unloaded/unauthorized facts.

entries.title: Flower conversation references
entries.summary: The composer owns unadmitted references; Floret owns admitted snapshots. Reference appends basic facts without sending or disturbing selection. Identity includes Runtime and Open requires authorized reads. Failed/canceled reads retain draft/preview; transport retries keep the frozen source even after rename/deletion.

entries.title: Flower composer references
entries.summary: Redeven owns authorized reference discovery and unadmitted connection-local drafts; Floret owns ordered references after admission. Composer chips show files/directories, frozen conversation references and page context. Stale discovery preserves the editor; captured submission failures retain outbox recovery without overwriting newer edits; labels never supply canonical identity or authorization.

entries.title: Flower input history
entries.summary: Floret/cache supplies canonical user text; published Floe owns transient history navigation and Redeven owns shared drafts/candidates. Unmodified ArrowUp in an exactly empty ordinary editor recalls text for editing, never submits. IME, selection, menus and structured answers retain keys. Scope or external-draft changes stop browsing without discarding text.

entries.title: Absolute filesystem directory selection
entries.summary: Published Floe owns picker navigation, validity and request lifetime; Redeven supplies connection, authoritative path context, localization and form state. Paths are absolute and / means the target filesystem root. Home/Root shortcuts grant no access. Failed navigation preserves intent/form, disables confirmation and offers Retry; execution revalidates current policy.

entries.title: Floating Files window dismissal
entries.summary: Files controller owns active request and immediate return focus. Floating host retains title/key/live browser through Floe exit presence, with no extra timer/copied content/second browser. Floe makes exit inert and disposes after motion, including reduced motion. New requests cancel exit through that same lifecycle.

entries.title: Personal directory favorites
entries.summary:
Runtime owns one directory-favorites store. Each authenticated namespace, endpoint
and user has an independent ordered path set and revision. Env App and Desktop
supply this metadata to published Floe controlled pickers and filesystem menus; the
existing filesystem navigator remains the only path validation and selection owner.

entries.title: Flower working directory navigation
entries.summary: Flower owns draft/durable-thread directory intent; Env App owns destination navigation. Full-page controls select new draft directories or browse the current directory; the companion omits them. Menus freeze exact thread/directory targets. Activity opens Files/new Terminal; Workbench creates widgets without changing scale or injecting commands into existing shells.

entries.title: Flower mobile navigation
entries.summary: In shared mobile mode, Flower opens its list in a large bottom drawer over retained detail. Floe owns presence/focus/motion and scroll-preserving focus return. Keep draft/selection/DOM and stationary detail/header throughout animation. Covered detail is inert and cannot acknowledge reads until exit. Desktop uses the same adaptive-layout contract.

entries.title: Flower Activity companion
entries.summary: Env App retains one Flower product tree across its Activity page, desktop companion and available Workbench widget. Published Floe owns the companion shell; Redeven owns placement, focus and read acknowledgement; Floret owns conversation lifecycle. Changing placement or canvas selection never creates another Flower surface or workspace stream.

entries.title: Ask Flower window boundaries
entries.summary: Redeven places Ask Flower in Activity, Workbench and Welcome beneath visible Shell/native chrome. Header/composer stay reachable during drag and resize; maximize and titlebar double-click are unavailable. Floe constrains shrinking viewports while retaining the same composer, draft and interaction state.

entries.title: Flower companion composer and motion
entries.summary: One native Flower textarea serves collapsed entry and expanded composer, retaining draft, selection, focus and IME. Redeven owns content; published Floe owns shell motion/geometry. Expanded text precedes a bottom toolbar, with controls in More and guidance above. Phase-driven close/reversal never remounts the editor or introduces lifecycle timers.

entries.title: Flower companion presence
entries.summary: Collapsed Flower projects canonical summaries and current-run detail through the existing workspace stream. Work, pending decisions and drafts have explicit precedence; historical completion is never new feedback. Presence neither expands Flower nor acknowledges reads. [Activity companion](flower-activity-companion.md) owns placement, focus and dismissal.

entries.title: Flower read state
entries.summary: Redeven owns per-user read confirmation. Unread indicators compare current activity with server confirmation and actual local presentation. Old responses never restore a dot for an already read version; new unseen activity remains unread. Temporary synchronization failures recover silently in the background, without blocking any user operation.

entries.title: Flower incremental live state
entries.summary: Floret owns canonical history/versions; Redeven authorizes one stream into ThreadCache. UTF-8 growth changes one item, never rescans history. Window/transport recovery preserves execution, prose and drafts. Retained DOM and scoped reads keep navigation and disclosure stable.

entries.title: Flower file edit preparation
entries.summary:
Flower shows candidate filenames while file-editing arguments are being prepared.
The existing Floret argument preview is display-only; actual tool results remain
the authority for completed changes. Progressive names keep long preparations
understandable while one stable activity row continues through approval and
execution.

entries.title: Flower timeline ordering
entries.summary: Flower renders Floret ordered facts using stable item, TurnID and RunID identities. Captured ordinary input appears immediately; only that draft is consumed. Queued inputs stay in the dock. Canonical request-key confirmation preserves mounted rows without duplicates, and summaries never author timeline detail.

entries.title: Flower terminal turn process disclosure
entries.summary: Floret owns turn outcome/timing. Terminal ordinary turns fold eligible process rows once, while pending controls, uncertain effects and inspected work stay visible. Explicit choices persist; user messages/finals remain mounted. Settled question/answer receipts fold with the process and reopen with complete content.

entries.title: Flower reasoning selection ownership
entries.summary: Existing threads display confirmed reasoning settings independently of runtime view versions; new drafts retain only explicit choices. Default is a configuration choice, never On or an inferred effort. Verified capabilities determine controls; unknown controls remain model-controlled. Failed saves preserve confirmed settings and active turns keep immutable execution configuration.

entries.title: Flower personal conversation preferences
entries.summary: Explicit model, directory and model-owned reasoning choices are remembered per authenticated namespace, endpoint and user. Loading/switching threads never writes defaults. New roots prefer explicit launch/draft choices, then personal memory, then configuration; existing threads and immutable turns retain confirmed settings.

entries.title: Flower model and navigation presentation
entries.summary: Flower separates Desktop/environment sources, unavailable models and first setup. Thread-owned model/reasoning choices remain authoritative. Navigation distinguishes visual intent from committed content and fences stale reads. Transient action failures use notifications; canonical failures remain in their timeline.

entries.title: Flower setup and settings
entries.summary: Shared Flower setup/settings serve Desktop and Env App. Empty unconfigured profiles offer explicit setup; configured new conversations offer editable starter drafts without launching turns. A retained modal form preserves saves/errors and makes covered chat inert without acknowledging reads. Existing recovery, model identity and permission owners remain authoritative.

entries.title: Flower provider configuration
entries.summary: Desktop, Flower and Env share one dialog. Hosts own persistence. Choose a brand, connect, then select models. Preserve navigation, focus and recovery actions after connection failures; reject stale responses. Kimi shares one brand while access methods retain separate credentials and models.

entries.title: Flower ChatGPT authentication
entries.summary:
The shared [Flower provider dialog](flower-provider-configuration.md) owns account
selection and authentication feedback. Signed-in accounts remain distinct from
previous connections, sign-out preserves a stable compact summary, and explicit
removal forgets only a signed-out local registration. The host retains verified
local admission and persistence ownership.

entries.title: Flower failure recovery
entries.summary: Floret owns outcomes, retry checkpoints and automatic historical migrations. Flower keeps accepted content readable with one failure/recovery surface; drafts, queue editing, Stop and navigation remain available. Transport uncertainty never proves success or permits replay. Readiness timeouts offer status refresh; deterministic migration failures remain explicit administrative diagnostics.

entries.title: Flower composer attachments
entries.summary: Flower owns connection-local attachment editing; host adapters authenticate staging, Redeven owns staged bytes/unadmitted commands and Floret owns admitted history. Select, paste, drop, retry, remove, preview and attachment-only send share one controller. Text above 50,000 Unicode code points converts only after successful staging, preserving IME and source text on failure.

entries.title: Flower file activity presentation
entries.summary: Canonical typed Floret Activity owns confirmed reads/mutations; output-progress owns provisional argument counts. Rows show user filename and added/deleted totals with matching unified diff. Protocol fields/private paths never become display metadata. Historical targets grant no read authority. Missing typed detail shows purpose/status without inventing a diff.

entries.title: Flower consecutive tool sequences
entries.summary: Desktop/Env App group consecutive tools with adjacent thinking. Active groups open; following prose or canonical turn end folds eligible groups, never temporary gaps. Explicit inspection survives; answered input splits settled work. This is ephemeral presentation over Floret facts, without canonical summaries or migrations.

entries.title: Flower activity disclosure interaction
entries.summary: Desktop and Env App share canonical Floret facts and one transcript viewport owner. Live changes cannot move pressed triggers/add hit targets before click completion. Cancelled gestures never activate tools; disposal releases all transient gesture ownership.

entries.title: Flower conversation sidebar
entries.summary: Desktop and Env App share one Flower sidebar with ThreadID-owned rows and endpoint-owned pin order. Selection, running work, unread attention and pending actions remain distinct. Live summaries preserve row/menu/focus identity. Resizing and pin feedback are ephemeral presentation over the canonical ThreadCache.

entries.title: Flower inline media
entries.summary: Assistant images, screenshots, video, audio and self-contained HTML render in shared Flower through released Floe media/HTML isolation. Redeven authorizes resource routing; canonical Floret messages remain the display source. Unavailable, forbidden, oversized or mismatched resources show local retryable errors without interrupting the conversation.

entries.title: Flower explicit long-thread qualification
entries.summary: Complete long-conversation content and responsive interaction are required product properties. Run this fixed-budget suite explicitly for acceptance/investigation, outside unified commit, integration and CI gates; it is not a prerequisite for each commit.

entries.title: Flower streaming stability
entries.summary: Indexed ThreadCache and published incremental Markdown apply actor-native changes only to affected text/DOM. Preserve history, code color, copy, focus, selection and disclosure. Semantic changes stay visible; malformed updates recover through the single live-state owner without suppressing output or adding lifecycle.

entries.title: Flower live queue CPU qualification
entries.summary: Ordered queues defer full-history snapshots; global facts and bounded root/child reading have separate owners. Local read failure preserves content/drafts without reconnecting. [Live-state contract](../ui/flower-live-timeline.md) remains authoritative.

entries.title: Flower request-history CPU qualification
entries.summary: Floret v7.79.0 reads canonical request facts once/execution, advancing bounded state after successful writes. Retry/restart reload; lineage validation remains. Redeven bounds sidebar previews and retains sequence members/observers. Three Service/Electron samples reduce median backend CPU80.3%, combined53.9%, allocations87.0%, preserving content/interaction.

entries.title: Flower received output progress
entries.summary:
Flower shows how long a dispatched model request has waited and how much output
has arrived. Edit rows show line counts while their arguments are generated,
then use the confirmed tool result. Published Floret v7.42.0 owns the generic
in-memory progress and preview lifecycle; Redeven interprets its own tool JSON
and presents the safe observations. No new journal records or schema changes
are required.

entries.title: Flower code highlighting
entries.summary: Flower owns committed Markdown lifetime; Floe enhanceCodeBlock owns visible tokenization/scheduling/color. Completed labelled fences receive colors in Env App/Desktop while source stays readable/copyable. Highlighting preserves geometry, focus and selection; unavailable or excessive work leaves plain code.

entries.title: Flower message appearance
entries.summary: Shared Flower uses published Floe colors for compact assistant/user reading and contrasting sent-message selection. Theme changes affect paint while preserving DOM, geometry and selection. Queued input stays quieter; forced colors use system roles. Media and resource cards retain canonical identity and never require an empty text bubble.

entries.title: Flower terminal activity presentation
entries.summary: Flower renders canonical Floret v7 Activity facts. Host-authored labels and descriptions explain the task; every terminal operation has safe expandable details, including writes and empty reads. Disclosure and output scrolling are local presentation state. They never create process lifecycle facts or expose stdin, private working paths, or effect internals. Actionable approval controls belong to the composer.

entries.title: Flower interactions and context state
entries.summary: Approval and waiting-user prompts are projections of Floret typed pending interactions. The bottom action mode is one mutually exclusive surface with fixed priority `input_request` then `approval` then `chat`, while the ordinary thread rail always remains interactive; decision surfaces never make a shared ancestor inert or install a pointer-blocking overlay.

entries.title: Asynchronous layout stability
entries.summary: Floe owns shared geometry; Redeven owns localized feedback. Request/copy/refresh/media completion cannot push adjacent content. Keep compact normal views without empty feedback rows; blocking errors stay visible, retained-content errors use existing-row disclosure. User navigation/disclosure/new records may change layout; async feedback cannot simulate them.

entries.title: Shared interface scale
entries.summary: Published Floe owns type, controls and responsive rows; Redeven maps semantic roles without root scaling or a separate density setting. Desktop uses 13px body/control, 12px supporting and 11px captions. Coarse-pointer fields and targets retain the published touch scale.

entries.title: Flower approval surface
entries.summary: Shared Flower renders canonical Floret approvals as a compact keyed list bounded by chat space with reachable header/footer. Runtime owns identity, permission and settlement; UI owns disclosure/submission feedback. Pending unavailable approvals stay visible with disabled decisions and reasons. Failures preserve content and keep Stop/navigation usable.

entries.title: Flower citations
entries.summary: Floret owns durable assistant sources with end-exclusive Unicode code-point ranges in exact message text. Flower renders provider markers as titled links and strips them on Copy. Only credential-free, whitespace/control-free HTTP(S) URLs are links; marker IDs cannot establish URLs. Missing historical facts remain explicit, while authored bibliographies stay ordinary content.

entries.title: Flower subagent detail window
entries.summary: The child detail window reads the complete canonical Floret `ThreadView`. HTTP and live updates share the selected parent-child identity, while Activity and queued-input controls remain attached to the same canonical child. The window preserves navigation and scroll state across updates without creating a second transcript or lifecycle owner.

entries.title: Flower subagent detail presentation
entries.summary: Floret parent-scoped ThreadRuntime.List owns membership; complete child ThreadView alone owns details. Open a stable immediate live window without polling/layout-changing sync UI. Routes use thread_id and explicit task_name, never inferred aliases. Malformed identity/contracts or parent-child mismatch fail rather than accepting legacy substitutes.

entries.title: Flower parent event timeline
entries.summary: Floret owns canonical child reports/events and admission; UI owns pages/bodies/disclosure only. Reports appear in the selected parent with canonical child avatars, without receipt/admission/preservation notices. Reading wakes neither task. Every full read rechecks recipient authority and canonical fixed-range paging.

entries.title: Tessiven Runtime discovery and operations
entries.summary: Runtime Tessiven service owns UI/Flower discovery and dispatch over existing registries/catalogs/executors. Discovery neither starts processes nor acquires business sessions. Path refs grant no permission. Lost authority, changed generations/identities or revocation stop dispatch. Lost mutation replies remain uncertain; inspect original operation/current state before deciding, never auto-replay.

entries.title: Tessiven Flower and operations
entries.summary:
Flower maps authorized code, configuration, and connected Runtime facts into
Tessiven versions through the `redeven-tessiven` system skill. Flower owns canvas
content editing as a core workflow. Resource actions
remain owned by the existing Managed Services and Containers managers. A
transport failure after a mutation is dispatched is terminal with an unknown
outcome, so the user must inspect the original manager before trying again.

entries.title: Authorized platform model gateway
entries.summary: Redeven AI uses the trusted control channel's platform lease and gateway origin to discover authorized models. The Runtime never receives a platform Provider API key. Floret continues to own thread execution, tools, canonical history, and recovery; the platform Edge owns authorization, binding, reservations, and final accounting.

entries.title: Model directory and selection
entries.summary: Runtime owns atomic metadata. Reads/send preflight use shipped/saved snapshots; refresh never blocks configured chat. Background refresh is disclosed, opt-in and excludes OpenRouter. OpenRouter/Ollama discover on addition; manual refresh remains available.

entries.title: Model web search
entries.summary:
Redeven owns provider and model search preferences. One backend resolver supplies
settings projections and Turn preparation; the final tool surface drives prompts
and wire declarations. Floret v7.40.2 validates hosted events against the actual
frozen provider request. Undeclared hosted execution remains a provider failure
because its remote effects cannot be assumed absent.

entries.title: Local ChatGPT plan authentication
entries.summary: OpenAI uses one API-key or ChatGPT-account method; omission keeps API-key behavior. ChatGPT uses public sign-in/Responses contracts, never Codex secrets/private backend. Floret owns engine/history/provider state; Redeven owns verified local admission, protected accounts/config/UI. Billing never silently changes; callers cannot obtain credentials. Canonical lifecycle reports failures.

entries.title: ChatGPT account lifecycle
entries.summary: The protected account store owns verified registrations/sessions; reuse unless explicit new-account/workspace intent. Email is no identity key. OAuth persistence is independent of connection editing; identity-only grants cannot infer. Retry refreshes OAuth inputs; renewal/logout serialize tokens. Cancellation/failed storage block credential use. Durable logout tracks interrupted cleanup; remote revocation remains separate.

entries.title: Provider configuration validation
entries.summary: Redeven owns configuration, credentials and Flower readiness across every settings entrypoint and provider-bundle save. Floret's public runtime contract is unchanged. Invalid saves preserve configuration and credentials; authentication/network failures remain execution errors.

entries.title: Provider API and catalog review
entries.summary: Runtime, Web, Desktop and iOS share one authenticated catalog. Official contracts and pinned models.dev inventory require released adapters and qualified limits, replay, tools, images and reasoning. Refreshes preserve configured model selections and stored conversation identities.

entries.title: Direct image reading and tool media retention
entries.summary:
image.read inspects authorized files/snapshots. Redeven owns bytes/authorization;
Floret owns history/membership. File references stay references; results use native
images, not browsers, temporary servers or Base64 result JSON. Original snapshots
remain available after model preparation.

entries.title: AI tool runtime
entries.summary: Redeven registers typed tools with product policy, presentation and effects; Floret owns admitted conversations, invocations, approval and history. This concept indexes focused tool, terminal, model, thread and subagent contracts. Detailed behavior belongs with its owner, without a duplicate implementation inventory.

entries.title: Flower storage ownership and migrations
entries.summary: Floret owns canonical Agent formats; Redeven owns product facts and uploads. Supported state upgrades through stable kinds, contiguous atomic migrations and public APIs while preserving history. Unknown, future, drifted or invalid state blocks Flower without resetting data or disabling the core Runtime.

entries.title: Flower backup and recovery
entries.summary: Readiness drains generations; storage owners snapshot/migrate their data and Floret ends old execution. Recover history/settings/read-state/uploads without stopping other surfaces. Freeze Flower writes during capture/replacement, verify complete collections and retain snapshots. Space, malformed data, migration or interruption blocks Flower while preserving recovery; no effect replay or binary rollback.

entries.title: Flower historical writer acceptance
entries.summary: Immutable fixtures come from locked released Redeven writers; current tests copy and verify them. Supported history must remain readable and continue after upgrade. Preserve source/module digests and public write paths. Fixture drift or upgrade failure blocks integration; database open alone is insufficient.

entries.title: Flower attachment resources
entries.summary: Redeven owns bytes/metadata, authenticated owner, quotas and retention; Floret owns turn membership. Upload once, send opaque attachment_id, display attachment://v1 locators and revalidate provider resources. Never expose paths or substitute product claims for canonical membership. Owner/quota/membership/metadata/digest/byte failures reject only the affected reference.

entries.title: AI tool permissions and dispatch
entries.summary: Redeven owns product visibility, policy, prompt and approval UI; Floret owns invocation and neutral tools. Current thread permission applies at the next boundary, while each admitted call retains its snapshot. Ordinary independent calls may authorize together; invalid authority rejects and dependent work waits.

entries.title: Computer and browser use runtime
entries.summary: ComputerUseRuntime owns targets, resources, control and script processes; Floret owns Agent lifecycle/effects/history. Prefer authorized commands for data, semantics for interaction and images for visual decisions. Missing target/permission/capability fails explicitly without selecting a substitute tab/window/device.

entries.title: Computer semantic snapshots
entries.summary: ComputerUseRuntime normalizes browser, macOS AX and Linux AT-SPI facts into bounded schema v2. Unsupported facts stay absent and relationships stay within the tree. Invalid observations are discarded while confirmed effects/output survive. Metadata grants no input authority and uncertain effects never replay.

entries.title: Computer script execution and semantic observations
entries.summary: One computer.exec is one Floret effect attempt. ComputerUseRuntime checks each controlled ui/browser/log operation in QuickJS. Same-target loops and navigation may compose; new target, permission or private input stops at the existing interaction boundary. Preserve confirmed progress without uncertain replay.

entries.title: Computer script read and validation boundaries
entries.summary:
Browser and native script reads return promised shapes or explicit errors.
Missing observations never become empty data, and invalid input never dispatches.
[Script execution](computer-use-scripts.md) owns the namespace and failure barrier.
Completed input stays recorded even when a later read fails.

entries.title: Optional built-in browser installation
entries.summary: Runtime owns one optional Chromium install. Enabled by default, it downloads only after authenticated user confirmation, never discovery/settings/tools. Disable persists, cancels install, closes managed processes and blocks use/prompts while retaining bytes/site data. Floret owns waiting/continuation. Failed verification publishes no partial package; offer explicit retry/source choice.

entries.title: Built-in browser Linux system preparation
entries.summary: Installation manager owns readiness; a short Runtime command performs the approved system transaction. Ubuntu namespace restrictions get explicit preparation, then version reuse. Preserve Chromium sandbox/global AppArmor; admit only catalog bytes at a fixed root-owned path, without API credentials. Dependencies, sandbox and unknown launch failures stay distinct; failed/cancelled publication preserves data.

entries.title: Browser and desktop settings
entries.summary: Desktop/Env App share one Browser and desktop dialog. Runtime capability, thread selection/grants and extension consent are separate authorities. Open/refresh/close never selects, grants, runs, installs or launches. Failed reads stay unknown; lost selections remain unavailable until recovery/replacement. Floret alone owns conversation lifecycle.

entries.title: Guided personal browser connection
entries.summary: Desktop and Env App share browser connection guidance over ComputerUseRuntime and Floret interactions. Users confirm Chrome installation and initial binding; later sessions restore the same environment. This bounded observation UI owns neither execution nor another lifecycle, and verified connections are reused.

entries.title: Chrome connection diagnostics and recovery
entries.summary: ComputerUseRuntime owns readiness/live handshakes; Desktop/Env App share host-specific guidance. Installed Chrome or accepted launch is not control readiness or task continuation. Resource, graphical-session, launch, status and continuation failures have distinct recovery. Only a compatible live profile enters Floret Respond; preserve guidance, never substitute browsers.

entries.title: Managed browsers and authorized Chrome tabs
entries.summary: ComputerUseRuntime owns connections/authorization/control. Managed Chromium, explicit CDP and Chrome extension share one restricted executor. Selected-tab authority excludes siblings/other devices. Disconnect/revocation/closed tabs/uncertain effects stop work without automatic replacement.

entries.title: Semantic desktop operations and explicit control
entries.summary:
`ComputerUseRuntime` owns desktop target execution. macOS targets an explicit
application window; Linux owns a private Xvfb and D-Bus session. Semantic actions
use native accessibility first. A foreground operation requires current task
authorization and respects explicit Stop and takeover. Platform permissions do not prove
that every application or action can run unobtrusively in the background.

entries.title: Computer target selection across threads
entries.summary:
The Computer Use Runtime owns discovery and selection over Redeven product
settings. Users describe work; Flower finds the browser page or application
window. The current selection is a working position, not a requirement to bind
resources in settings. Candidates never grant access. Stale, disconnected or
occupied resources fail explicitly without changing the previous selection.

entries.title: Computer use safety pauses and user control
entries.summary: Floret owns questions, answers and continuation; Redeven owns authorized computer effects and private media. Failures remain factual and blocked capture is not a screenshot. Answers pass unchanged without granting authority or replay. Fresh safe observation precedes further input; no second recovery lifecycle exists.

entries.title: Private browser observation and input
entries.summary: Runtime owns observer-bound private input/pixels; Floret owns takeover/continuation. Bind operations to current observer, revision, thread/run/target; never expose secrets or replay uncertain effects. Disconnect revokes input. Canonical answer starts a new Run with fresh observation; private input additionally waits for decoded matching observer/interaction/target pixels.

entries.title: Computer use media and visual requests
entries.summary:
Redeven owns authorized screenshots; Floret owns history/preparation. Flower
shows frames inline/in Stage. Durable frames and ephemeral samples have separate
lifetimes; tool success does not prove delivery. Model encodings never replace original assets.

entries.title: Flower computer viewer presentation
entries.summary: Floe owns Stage geometry/launcher; Flower projects canonical status and decoded media. Viewing, moving, closing or restoring grants no target/execution authority. Interrupted/private frames retain recovery and cannot borrow unrelated images. The media contract remains the sole authorization/sampling owner.

entries.title: Computer use product qualification
entries.summary:
Redeven qualifies Computer use through the actual product renderer, Runtime,
media decoder and target adapter. A passing scenario proves only its declared
target and provider scope. Fixture outcomes, decoded pixels and cleanup are
required evidence; successful HTTP responses or tool metadata alone are
insufficient. Failed input and uncertain effects must never be replayed to
manufacture a passing result.

entries.title: Computer use qualification evidence
entries.summary:
The production qualification runners establish scope-specific outcomes under
[the acceptance contract](computer-use-qualification.md). The following results
include September and October 2026 runs. A passing worktree run does not replace the exact-main
pre-push gate, certify arbitrary applications, or turn earlier failed runs into
successes. Private text and pixels are excluded from retained diagnostics.

entries.title: Browser and native drag timing qualification
entries.summary:
Browser drag timing is measured from actual input events, with all model and
assertion failures retained. [Script contracts](computer-use-scripts.md) define
behavior; [qualification](computer-use-qualification.md) defines the test lane.
Browser measurements certify only the tested browser paths and durations.

entries.title: Media contention and native read qualification
entries.summary:
The October 28 qualification validates cancellable media-write admission and
native node/subtree completeness. Production uses published Floret v7.88.0;
its existing cancellable inventory and write-gate contract need no upstream
change. Browser, AX and AT-SPI share the same completeness semantics.

entries.title: Computer use paired model measurements
entries.summary: Paired production Flower/Floret/model/browser fixtures compare visual primitives with semantic scripts on the same tasks. Keep all failures and reject missing, duplicate or unmeasured samples. Headless results do not certify native desktop or Chrome focus; those require separate product qualification.

entries.title: Codex computer and browser use design evidence
entries.summary: Versioned official documentation and installed app 26.908.40834/extension 1.26.901.11451 inform command-first routing, AX/script batching and compact observations. They expose neither proprietary implementation nor universal external-window isolation. Flower Runtime remains execution and authorization authority.

entries.title: AI tool approval and interaction runtime
entries.summary: Floret owns typed approval/input; Redeven authorizes and renders without a second lifecycle. Resolve commits canonical results before view publication. Since v7.26.0, unresolved interaction and active projection publish atomically; waiting clears run_progress, other active summaries retain it. Persistence failure stays unresolved; reject/cancel is row-local, not a global failure.

entries.title: AI terminal tool runtime
entries.summary: Redeven owns PTYs and bounded output; Floret v7 owns canonical tool calls, interactions, effect attempts, results and Activity. One adapter authorizes execution once and publishes current views. Product SQL stores no parallel terminal lifecycle or effect recovery.

entries.title: Model reasoning capabilities and transport
entries.summary: Published Floret owns reasoning choices, Ollama metadata and wire encoding; Redeven maps verified capabilities and settings. Default, Off, On, effort and budget remain distinct. Invalid selection rejects before dispatch; unknown controls retain model defaults. Active turns keep immutable settings through restart.

entries.title: Flower prompt and rule sources
entries.summary:
Flower's host-owned base system prompt contains its English introduction as
Redeven's general assistant, visual output guidance and local file-delivery rules.
Every run profile uses the same base prompt.
Runtime facts, tool definitions and native Floret guidance retain their own owners
and remain available independently of the product identity.

entries.title: AI model and context runtime
entries.summary: Redeven persists model/reasoning preferences, credentials and source selection. Floret owns provider context and opaque continuation. Desktop/environment sources stay distinct; typed observations drive usage/compaction. Token input/output limits remain separate and configuration merges preserve unrelated settings.

entries.title: Model provider surface and history
entries.summary: Floret owns the provider-visible history and render lineage for each Turn. Redeven supplies the current model surface, prompt, permission snapshot, and ephemeral overlays at the declared boundaries. Historical tool facts remain readable without reintroducing removed tools or rewriting canonical history; provider-surface changes create a new compatible lineage and never become a second continuation store.

entries.title: Model request recovery
entries.summary: Floret owns retry admission, physical-request deadlines and attempt identity. Redeven supplies protocol facts through one adapter and displays the authoritative current view. Frozen input, confirmed tool exchanges and user cancellation retain their existing authority across transport recovery.

entries.title: Model request measurement
entries.summary: Published Floret v7.70.0 owns one pressure calculation: a qualified native prefix plus an estimate of only the remaining frozen input, or the complete estimate when proof does not match. Redeven supplies protocol facts through optional public contracts.

entries.title: Model request reuse
entries.summary: Floret owns effective reuse decisions and canonical state. Redeven executes them through one prepared request and one Responses consumer. In-memory connections can optimize transmission only after the next canonical state and complete input agree. Failures return to normal turn recovery; supplemental context cannot enable reuse.

entries.title: Flower context compaction and Goal continuation
entries.summary:
Published Floret v7.74.0 owns compaction admission, installation, Goal continuation,
Stop, Retry and restart. Redeven authorizes and transmits the frozen intent and
presents canonical state. Pure compaction ends after installation or noop; Goal
continuation prepares context and continues work through the existing Engine and
current Goal review in the same execution.

entries.title: Model context usage and compaction
entries.summary: Published Floret owns context, compaction and usage; Redeven displays typed snapshots. [Compaction lifecycle](flower-context-compaction.md) owns intent through recovery; [qualification](../operations/flower-compaction-qualification.md) covers deterministic, historical-copy and real-provider checks.

entries.title: Flower context compaction qualification
entries.summary:
Compaction qualification uses isolated state and explicit test lanes. Production
threads are never continued by historical-copy inspection. The [execution contract](../ai/flower-context-compaction.md) owns intent and recovery; [usage presentation](../ai/model-context-usage-and-compaction.md) maps canonical observations.

entries.title: Flower Ollama context qualification
entries.summary:
The opt-in Ollama qualification uses the production Flower service, its model
gateway, and the published Floret thread runtime. Native provider usage must
agree with canonical Flower context and cumulative totals; compaction must
preserve facts through a real model-generated checkpoint and restart. Tests own
their temporary state and loopback recording proxy. A provider or assertion
failure fails the run; it never substitutes a simulated response or changes the
user's model configuration.

entries.title: Flower context distribution qualification
entries.summary: Floret 7.60.3 separates native tokens from same-request visible Unicode characters. Historical token categories/remainder attribution are superseded; current [presentation](../ai/flower-managed-model-context.md#presentation) is authoritative. Prior failed checks stay failed and unrelated prompt qualification remains 119/120.

entries.title: Flower Ollama task qualification
entries.summary: Explicit Ollama qualification uses the installed model, production Flower and published Floret. Verify real tool effects, files, processes, canonical views and streams. Failures remain failures without simulated substitutes or automatic reruns. Tests own cleanup and preserve source credentials/configuration.

entries.title: DeepSeek Responses
entries.summary:
Flower routes the DeepSeek provider to the published Floret v7.66.1 Responses gateway.
Floret owns `/responses` rendering, SSE parsing, reasoning, usage normalization,
function-call validation, and opaque provider history. Redeven only maps its
model DTOs and canonical dotted tool names to provider-safe aliases.

entries.title: Flower canonical thread queries
entries.summary:
Flower exposes two read-only tools for finding another readable conversation
and reading its content: `threads.query` and `threads.read`. The tool contract
is intentionally smaller than Floret's published general query API.
`threads.aggregate` is not registered or dispatched.

entries.title: Floret thread runtime integration
entries.summary: Floret v7 `ThreadService` is the sole owner of active and canonical thread lifecycle. Redeven authorizes endpoint ownership, resolves attachments and maps provider/tool effects. Send, Respond, Cancel, Retry, and the optional independent CompactContext return typed state before continuation. Canonical records prevent duplicates; drafts and execution tokens remain transient.

entries.title: Floret Redeven adapter and projection
entries.summary: Redeven's adapter is a thin typed boundary over published Floret. It authorizes endpoint and thread ownership, resolves resources, sanitizes Activity, maps typed views, native updates and failures, and projects live summaries. Floret remains the only lifecycle, persistence, migration, cancellation, and provider-state owner; Redeven never waits on provider work or mirrors a receipt, authority barrier, transcript, or execution projection.

entries.title: Flower subagent parent events
entries.summary: SubAgent reports and lifecycle events remain canonical Floret facts, visible to the direct parent without creating another handoff store. They do not wake idle parents; bounded waiting and explicit reads expose reports when the parent continues. Tool approval and user input remain ordinary child interactions, while questions and blockers can be reported through `report_to_parent` without ending the delegated task.

entries.title: Flower subagent runtime
entries.summary: Floret v7 owns each SubAgent as a normal canonical child Thread. Redeven exposes product tools and Flower mappings over the typed `ThreadRuntime` without a second child identity, result store, recovery projection, or child lifecycle table. Parent-scoped summaries are bounded status only; the canonical child current view is the only complete handoff authority.

entries.title: Flower thread fork coordination
entries.summary: Floret owns journal/destination identity; Redeven authorizes endpoint/source and adopts destination settings. One stable request optionally titles that returned destination only. No product fork receipt/saga/canonical copy. Invalid request, foreign source, Floret failure or conflicting settings fails explicitly, without a recovery coordinator or compensating canonical deletion.

entries.title: Flower thread deletion coordination
entries.summary: Floret owns canonical thread deletion and Redeven owns product settings, read state, execution authority, and attachment claims. One authenticated DELETE request performs those two owner operations in that order and returns success only after both complete. The operation is synchronous, idempotent, and retryable; it does not claim cross-database atomicity or persist a second lifecycle receipt.

entries.title: Flower plugin generation
entries.summary:
Flower can help users create plugins, but the generated-plugin flow is not a
second plugin platform. Redeven owns the user intent capture, prompt
orchestration, review UX, approval presentation, and product timeline
projection. ReDevPlugin owns templates, validators, package builders, lifecycle
APIs, runtime contracts, sandbox surfaces, and platform policy. Floret owns the
tool dispatch and approval lifecycle that Flower must use.

entries.title: Flower context action admission
entries.summary: Redeven owns selected context before admission; Floret owns admitted messages/references/context. One mapper validates authorization/privacy then emits durable ordered MessageReference and UserInput.Context. No product copy persists afterward. Malformed/unknown/forged or failed projection rejects admission while preserving editable draft/references.

entries.title: Redeven environment operations
entries.summary: Redeven environment lifecycle requests must go through the Redeven product surface, not through inferred container, SSH, systemd, launchctl, or process-manager commands. Flower learns this boundary through the standard `redeven-environment` system skill, not through a bespoke environment workflow embedded in the global prompt.

entries.title: OKF bundle lifecycle
entries.summary: Redeven builds its embedded OKF bundle from curated source files under the top-level `okf/` authoring root, verifies deterministic dist outputs under `okf/dist/`, and embeds the resulting bundle into the binary used by Runtime and AI features for local retrieval.

entries.title: OKF tool suite
entries.summary: Redeven exposes the embedded OKF bundle through read-only `okf.index`, `okf.search`, and `okf.open` builtin tools. Redeven projects bounded safe results into Floret v7.26.0 structured Activity rows, and the shared Flower surface expands those rows without reading raw OKF result JSON.

entries.title: Gateway v6 protocol
entries.summary: Gateway serves only redeven-gateway-v6, defined by spec/openapi/gateway-v6.yaml. Signed invitations carry admin-confirmed addresses; authenticated exchange returns the signed descriptor/all endpoints. Gateway owns paired Desktop permissions and Runtime-initiated membership. Mismatch/old config fails unchanged; old URL-profile/HTTP-forward routes are absent. Cloud v3 remains separate.

entries.title: RCPP v5 Cloud API
entries.summary: RCPP v5 separates Cloud authorization from network route. CloudRuntimeBinding owns environment, Runtime identity, Namespace, user or Namespace principal and generation. One Runtime ConnectionController handles direct and Gateway enrollment, registration, heartbeat, reserve maintenance and recovery. Desktop never creates a second credential recovery owner.

entries.title: Self-contained installer distribution
entries.summary:
Release packaging builds `redeven-installer_<os>_<arch>` for macOS and Linux,
AMD64 and ARM64, with CGO disabled. It renders `redeven-install.sh` from the
actual four binary digests and signs both the binaries and entry through
`SHA256SUMS`. No receiving-host Go, Cosign, Python, OpenSSL or package manager
is required. A standard shell, HTTPS downloader and SHA-256 utility remain
bootstrap prerequisites.

entries.title: CI and release gates
entries.summary: Focused development checks precede staged pre-commit and exact-tip main admission. Dependencies, generated assets, locales and OKF must agree. Long-thread, browser, Desktop and native acceptance stay explicit; release needs authenticated artifacts and same-commit historical data qualification. Windows remains internal-only.

entries.title: ReDevPlugin release artifact gate
entries.summary: Admit only the coordinated published ReDevPlugin release, binding artifacts to tag/source/target/digest/signer/receipt through registry readbacks, native evidence and closed inventory. Partial, mutable, Windows or target-mismatched inputs fail closed.

entries.title: Plugin integration gate
entries.summary: The plugin integration gate proves that the released ReDevPlugin Host and market contracts remain aligned with Redeven's authorization, placement, renderer, and Desktop lifecycle adapters. It uses the published package and isolated smoke profiles; copied platform paths, implicit grants, second bridges, and stale lifecycle projections fail closed.

entries.title: OKF release assets
entries.summary:
GitHub releases ship `okf_bundle.manifest.json` and `okf_bundle.sha256` together with CLI tarballs, desktop packages, and signed `SHA256SUMS`.

Release workflow publishes OKF verification assets alongside CLI and desktop artifacts.

The signed aggregate checksum remains the public integrity anchor for these standalone verification files.

entries.title: Automated service-template catalog updates
entries.summary: The template repository publishes immutable recommendations. Redeven daily/manual adoption pins public Go checksums, regenerates notices/OKF and passes normal integration checks. Failure retains published main and uncertain push requires ref inspection. Adoption never upgrades installed service instances.

entries.title: Flower managed runtime facts
entries.summary:
Flower consumes published Floret v7.47.1. One complete collector supplies four
stable partitions: execution environment, date/timezone, repository rule
sources, and available skills. Floret owns chronological admission,
semantic changes, user-role model-context messages, compaction and recovery.
The product owns collection and authorized presentation only.

concepts.summary: Redeven registers typed tools with product policy, presentation and effects; Floret owns admitted conversations, invocations, approval and history. This concept indexes focused tool, terminal, model, thread and subagent contracts. Detailed behavior belongs with its owner, without a duplicate implementation inventory.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
This concept is the stable overview for the subject.

Floret renders reference display content and snapshots into canonical model history for execution and compaction, preserving order across follow-ups.

Lease release follows the canonical terminal view, not the HTTP response or Desktop connection lifetime, so an existing session cannot admit hidden work after the final lifecycle snapshot.

concepts.title: ChatGPT account lifecycle
concepts.summary: The protected account store owns verified registrations/sessions; reuse unless explicit new-account/workspace intent. Email is no identity key. OAuth persistence is independent of connection editing; identity-only grants cannot infer. Retry refreshes OAuth inputs; renewal/logout serialize tokens. Cancellation/failed storage block credential use. Durable logout tracks interrupted cleanup; remote revocation remains separate.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Sign-in and registration
One `chatgpt.Client` owns bounded, five-minute in-memory attempts.

Interrupted logout is completed at startup; normal maintenance scans never clear a live logout.

## Renewal and credential coordination
[Account maintenance](../../internal/chatgpt/lifecycle.go) starts with the Runtime service, independently of AI readiness, connection bindings and open windows. Runtime shutdown cancels maintenance without signing out and never schedules OS background work.

Account updates use model_directory.changed and merge independently of drafts.

## Logout and connection changes
Sign-out first records intent and stops related tasks through Floret's existing immediate Cancel with descendants. The private Desktop model source observes current account facts once per second and passes confirmed account stop reasons to its owning Runtime; it never owns another task lifecycle.

The Runtime Service protocol, secrets schema, Floret public API and domain migration remain unchanged.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: This concept owns local registration and credential lifecycle. Connection configuration stores only account bindings; it cannot commit or roll back OAuth tokens. Cancellation cleanup may retain a verified signed-out registration, and remote revocation failure never becomes confirmed success.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Local host admission
The authenticated Runtime settings response publishes `auth_capabilities` with an `openai_chatgpt` availability, disabled reason and connection binding. Desktop identity, loopback URL text, renderer headers and client declarations cannot establish local access.

That source executes against the local account store; the remote settings page exposes no account login, credential transfer or account email.

## Account lifecycle
The [ChatGPT account lifecycle](chatgpt-account-lifecycle.md) is the canonical owner of registration, verified sign-in persistence, issued-client retry, local saved-account selection, renewal, cancellation cleanup and logout. Connection saves and explicit logout have separate results.

## Model and request contracts
The public account model endpoint's listed models preserve server order and are intersected with reviewed adapter capabilities. ChatGPT connections reject custom endpoints, API credentials and custom model declarations.

No error silently switches authentication or API billing.

concepts.title: Computer script read and validation boundaries

frontmatter.title: Computer script read and validation boundaries

concepts.summary:
Browser and native script reads return promised shapes or explicit errors.
Missing observations never become empty data, and invalid input never dispatches.
[Script execution](computer-use-scripts.md) owns the namespace and failure barrier.
Completed input stays recorded even when a later read fails.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Successful reads and argument counts
All guest methods, including image and download-cursor methods, validate explicit
minimum/maximum argument counts before dispatch. Existing type and option
validation remains authoritative; extra arguments return SCRIPT_ARGUMENT_ERROR
with a closed method and documented_arity diagnostic. Valid signatures do not change.

Runtime requires the promised result for semantic observations, node/text/collection/
attribute reads and condition waits. Missing or invalidated reads fail through the
existing observation-error boundary, seal the invocation and retain completed
input without replay. Empty arrays, empty text, zero counts and null attributes
remain valid data. Snapshot projection never fills absent observations with an
empty tree. A confirmed action may invalidate an old observation and still be
followed by an explicit fresh read. A documented wait timeout remains a result;
requireState turns it into CONDITION_TIMEOUT. Takeovers and target changes keep
their existing control boundaries.

The browser controller routes node/text/query/table/attribute/condition reads
through one observation boundary, including direct lower-level read exceptions.
It supplies the required semantic_read failure stage, retains the live source,
and uses the existing bounded read retry only; inputs never enter that retry.
A rejected read cannot become a malformed transport response that disconnects
the target. A later explicitly requested read can recover on the same page.

## Validated inputs and bounded browser reads
The browser adapter validates the complete operation before virtual focus,
scroll preparation or input. Invalid arguments retain a closed diagnostic with
phase, field, expected form and recovery; page errors and supplied secrets are
never copied into it. Keys use characters or documented names with
Alt/Control/Meta/Shift modifiers; physical codes such as Equal are not names.
Primitive computer.wait defaults to zero milliseconds and adds no settling
promise. Legacy waitFor retains its returned state. requireState throws CONDITION_TIMEOUT and seals later host operations, even if guest code catches the error. Earlier completed input remains recorded.
Its closed diagnostic retains method, requested state, timeout_ms and zero-based
operation_index, mirrored in failed_action/failed_operation_index. Matching text
and raw exceptions stay private. completed_actions records completed operations;
a completed wait operation does not imply its requested condition was met.

Browser locators expose query({limit,cursor}) over the authorized loaded AX
scope and an attribute allowlist. Results carry total, truncation, document and
cursor; changed contents invalidate pagination. Only returned page references
enter the bounded reference table. Each page is at most 200 items and 48 KiB of
items. Virtualized, unloaded rows are never counted as visited. href removes
credentials, query and fragment and must not be reconstructed as an action URL.
Browser rows reads a unique table/grid and returns header/data rows and cell roles,
with explicit loaded-tree scope. Pages contain at most 200 rows/48 KiB of item
content; each row is limited to 200 cells/44 KiB, each cell to 2,000 Unicode
characters. cells_truncated/text_truncated mark loss; exact totals cannot be
inferred from incomplete rows. Cursor identity includes full cell contents.
Nested tables are excluded. count reports loaded matches. attribute returns a
scalar safe attribute; linkSummary labels its redacted URL as non-actionable.
Native targets reject these browser reads inside scripts before adapter dispatch.

scroll_progress belongs to the scroll return value. It reports immediate
before/after measurements, with null or unchanged values remaining inconclusive.
Semantic wheel input uses the visible intersection of the target, not clickable-control
enabled state or its offscreen full-box center. Browser-native intersection geometry
owns ancestor clipping and transforms; document targets use their viewport. Existing
hit testing checks target ancestry and embedding-frame overlays before one wheel.
Scroll-into-view preparation remains separately reported when the wheel is rejected;
it can move the viewport. No alternative-point search or automatic input replay is
added. Immediate offsets do not select the next action for the model.

The core help demonstrates awaited node reads and logging the returned scroll
result; node and snapshot objects do not carry scroll measurements.

Repeated identical observations in the same script namespace/document/scope
receive a bounded advisory after two repeats. This never replays input, changes
target, adds a planner, or persists a second lifecycle.

Single-node detail does not enumerate a subtree. child_refs describes only
returned relationships; check children_truncated, use snapshot for a subtree
and browser rows/query/count for loaded collections.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Collection results describe only the authorized loaded tree; they do not certify
unloaded content. Native targets reject browser-only reads before dispatch.
Validation and observation recovery never replay completed input.

frontmatter.title: Managed browsers and authorized Chrome tabs

concepts.summary: ComputerUseRuntime owns connections/authorization/control. Managed Chromium, explicit CDP and Chrome extension share one restricted executor. Selected-tab authority excludes siblings/other devices. Disconnect/revocation/closed tabs/uncertain effects stop work without automatic replacement.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Explicit connection/tab creation in Browser and desktop selects the conversation target. Approval Required uses current target/URL through approval; temporary URL authority never becomes saved origin permission. This is not a model tool/second browser-opening path.

## Managed profiles

Both Flower carriers share /_redeven_proxy/api/browser/installation. Default profile lazily creates its first page; later selected-page loss fails explicitly.

Semantic clicks verify visible/enabled/stable geometry and actual session hit target, including parent overlays. Preparation is not completed input: blocked clicks report action_executed:false and fresh-observation demand after viewport changes. Bounded condition waits sample rendered CSS state. Labels use current safe observed titles, not discovery as account identity.

Same-document screenshot geometry may settle read-only for at most1s within invocation budget; check before/after every capture. Persistent movement returns capture/viewport_unstable without pixels. Cancellation/document changes/latched privacy guard remain authoritative. Never replay input to repair observation.

Frame inventory owns document identity. Child navigation/removal revokes its subtree, preserving unchanged parent refs. Root replacement/cancel/handback invalidates all. Snapshot/image revisions stay page-wide; ref resolution rechecks document after DOM/AX reads.

Locator keys require focusable elements; AX document roots use ui.key('PageDown'). Exact DOM.focus/document rejection returns ELEMENT_NOT_ACTIONABLE with focus/not_focusable, no key/connection retirement. Generic failures/lost focus or input acknowledgment/failed release remain uncertain, without replay. Expose safe stage/reason/fresh-observation demand plus warning and completed prefix.

Downloads use browser.downloadCursor() before input, sequential waitForDownload({after:cursor}), or exact known ID. Bounded page-local memory excludes old files; multiple new files are ambiguous. No replay/latest-file inference/durable ledger. Published SourceDownload is sole identity writer; raw CDP creates no duplicates. Same-named exports stay distinct; AMBIGUOUS_DOWNLOAD exposes bounded exact candidates.

readDownload(id,{offset,limit}) returns bounded base64/continuation from exact source; sequential chunks share a short-lived stream retired on cancel/idle/disposal. saveDownload(id) copies at most256MiB into task scratch with run-owned authorization/partial cleanup, validating offset/count/identity/available total each chunk. Guest cannot select destination/arbitrary paths; terminal/file tools process returned path and deliver finals.

Hit tests convert viewport CSS to owning CDP document coordinates, including scrolled frames. Cross-process input checks all embedding overlays. Protocol unavailability reports TARGET_OBSERVATION_UNAVAILABLE/observation_stage:hit_test, never fabricated coverage. Capture includes non-overlay scrollbars and derives immutable transform from actual dimensions with before/after stability. Scoped scroll verifies control-center hit target first.

## Chrome extension and explicit CDP

MV3 uses Native Messaging/chrome.debugger bound to exact tab. webNavigation creation events keep bounded popup-source facts; tab-group opener metadata is not action source. Remote Linux tasks use remote managed browser/private desktop, never silently local Chrome.

The Swift helper inventories regular and accessory application windows, reads AX roles, labels, non-sensitive values, supported actions and bounds, and exposes bounded subtree queries.

Application discovery reuses HostApplicationCatalog; exact candidate selection
uses NSWorkspace with current app/foreground permission. Launch completion is

Minimized windows are restored once and allowed to settle; zero/multiple windows

Secret fields enter the existing private takeover channel rather than model observations.

Snapshots declare source macos_accessibility and application_provided coverage.

The Xvfb owner starts a private session D-Bus and AT-SPI bus. The executor rejects socket or environment paths leading outside that private desktop; it never discovers or attaches to another logged-in user's session.

Product target preferences and canonical historical results follow their existing owners.

- Missing, changed or unauthorized bytes fail explicitly. No unrestricted URL fallback.
- [Image reads](image-read-and-retention.md) share immutable Computer storage;
  computer:// identities and retention stay intact.
- Safe results include target, location, summary and safety. Semantic/script
  operations include images only when requested.
- All authorized model images use published Floret PrepareModelImage: JPEG quality
  85 and a 2560-pixel longest side, without upscaling. Uploads, image.read/crops,
  browser/native screenshots, MCP images, summaries and historical replay share
  this policy. Alpha remains PNG; EXIF orientation is applied and ICC retained.
  An animation stays byte-identical when it fits; oversized animation fails
  explicitly without flattening frames. An unchanged smaller original may be kept.
- Canonical original bytes, hashes, locators and visible history never change.
  Model notices report source/model dimensions and bytes; fine text can be read
  through an original-backed crop. Preparation never fetches arbitrary URLs.
- Preparation precedes estimation/freezing. Transport retries reuse exact bytes;
  Desktop RPC carries validated derived metadata to prevent lossy recompression.
  Encoding revisions invalidate provider state. No durable derivative cache exists.
- Flower caps JSON/base64 at 32 MiB independently of tokens: product policy,
  not a provider limit. Remote DTOs share the cap; services own final rendering.
- Media dimension/count/byte failures retain typed actual/limit/stage through
  Desktop RPC and canonical failure projection. Published Floret v7.94.0 recovers
  aggregate count/total-byte failures through safe historical compaction even
  with low token usage. Individual invalid/dimension failures remain terminal;
  neither class aliases token overflow. UI provides numeric
  diagnostics and input/model guidance without unchanged Retry or secret payloads.

## Screenshot coordinates
A model screenshot returns frame_geometry with its computer:// identity, original
image dimensions and model_image dimensions. Browser geometry also carries CSS
visual viewport scale/offset. Screenshot handles use model_pixels plus frame and
document_id; explicit browser image_pixels retains original pixel semantics.
Default browser CSS and native window coordinates keep their existing units.
Native window screenshots support model_pixels with a transient window anchor.
Full-page/cropped arbitrary images do not establish an input mapping.

Each controller holds one model anchor. Viewer sampling cannot replace it.
Changed target, document, viewport, bounds or observed native accessibility state
rejects stale input. Input and takeover invalidate the anchor. Known-change
checks cannot eliminate arbitrary dynamic layout races; semantic locators remain
preferable for moving controls. The final attachment supplies after_frame when
several screenshots were taken.

## Browser observation and private input
The shared browser controller enforces visible password fields, structured
one-time-code input semantics, secret-change latches and explicit permissions in
each frame, including shadow roots. Native adapters enforce platform secure-field
roles. They do not classify ordinary labels or page prose as CAPTCHA, OTP or
instruction attacks. Observed content is untrusted data, never authorization.
The model decides task meaning and whether human help is needed; it never receives
confirmed protected values or pixels for classification. Unmarked secrets are not
guaranteed detectable by accessibility; native apps must expose secure fields and
users retain explicit takeover control. An unreadable frame stops the observation
without inventing a human requirement. Unknown read failures are not retried;
only measured viewport instability has a bounded same-target resampling window.

Redeven qualifies Computer use through the actual product renderer, Runtime,

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Evidence and isolation
Use built product renderer, Runtime, decoder and adapter. Keep canonical results, fixture events, decoded frames, exact source/artifact hashes and cleanup. HTTP/code/model prose/Activity alone prove neither effects nor pixels. Separate assertion, model and product failures, retaining originals; never replay uncertain input or repeat until green. Native/provider/foreground suites remain explicit outside ordinary/exact-main gates.

Result-encoding recovery uses a real task Service/public UI: one counted effect followed by invalid optional result. Browser/native semantics share cancellation/revocation-before-input and terminal unknown acknowledgements.

## DeepSeek lane
TestComputerReliabilityDeepSeek uses production Service/Floret, configured deepseek-flash (local V4.1 Flash 1017) and catalog-installed Chromium, without substitutes. Require REDEVEN_COMPUTER_RELIABILITY_E2E=1, absolute REDEVEN_COMPUTER_CONFIG_ROOT/EVIDENCE_DIR and REDEVEN_BROWSER_TEST_INSTALLATION. Command: GOWORK=off go test ./internal/ai -run '^TestComputerReliabilityDeepSeek$' -count=1 -v -timeout=22m. Repetitions 1..5 (default 1); browser-only may use -parallel 3. Native requires REDEVEN_COMPUTER_NATIVE_E2E=1 and released Swift helper, serialized desktop access; absolute REDEVEN_COMPUTER_NATIVE_TEST_HOST may select a baseline. Preserve provider/secret hashes and user threads.

Use default tools except explicit legacy-wait case. Cover bounded text/limits/budgets, confirmed prefixes, pre-focus validation, paging, image identity, delays/titles/staleness/options, scroll facts, conditions/natural tasks, timeout/below-fold input, exact asynchronous content, landmarks/reset, scripts/downloads/app entry. Canonical ThreadToolResultReader must decode Floret ERROR and host envelope. Require data.script_error for script diagnostics; pre-dispatch rejection is distinct. Final prose/logs cannot replace execution. Completed waits remain confirmed after guest failure.

| Case | Required effects/evidence |
| --- | --- |
| capture/refs | Four PageDown then fresh screenshot; parent ref survives child navigation |
| options/waits | Exact unsupported field, failed index and safe condition facts |
| stale/image | STALE_REFERENCE and zero pointers / one pointer after image |
| visual/form/table | Vary position/labels/size; screenshot before actual visual click; exact values/totals |
| batch | Three page reads, >=two transitions in one script, screenshot; totals checked separately |
| download | One export/save identity, exact bytes and terminal-created project file; no anonymous reads after acquisition |
| native entry | Discovery/confirmed selection, exact text, one click/screenshot |
| optional/caught | Zero/timeout may branch; failed unique lookup cannot resume input even when caught |
| output loss | Prior explicit output retained; one fault/zero later input; actual method without invented code |
| drag | Independent press/release/moves/endpoints/duration; invalid integer_0_5000 rejects before input |

Also cover >2,800 nodes, complete totals, account/tab separation, older same-name download and save followed by diagnostic failure without replay. Retain wire IDs/errors/history/events/answers. Scope success proves neither weights nor universal reliability.

## Browser/native boundaries
Semantic scroll verifies document/tall/clipped/covered cases, counting wheels separately from scroll preparation: one valid dispatch, zero on rejection. Real extension CDP/AX faults retain method/code, zero input and explicit same-ref recovery. Managed frames/shadows/transforms and malformed reads use actual zoom/DPR.

Maintained batch/download examples run QuickJS→Runtime→Chromium with exact multichunk bytes/one export/ID, page values and screenshot. Native entry verifies zero/one/multiple/minimized windows; native script checks actual Swift scrolling/screenshots/focus restoration, invalidated by external input.

AppKit drag receiver verifies 0/1/500/5000 ms plus interrupted 5000 ms, one press/release and early canceled endpoint, using independent timestamps. Fixture key-window changes require factual pause/balanced release/explicit recovery, never replay. Real-model timed/invalid/zero/focus-change cases use production receipts. Browser node tests cover both hosts/image/timing/cancellation but cannot qualify native timing.

## Product carriers
Built Desktop uses isolated exact provider config and rejects missing/overridden identity. Observe preload workspace stream; Linux Webtop may passively copy CDP. Missing decoded native/browser frame fails that scope. Name all unqualified platforms/native/connected-Chrome lanes.

checkDesktopSystemBrowser.mjs combines built Desktop/Runtime/extension/Native Messaging with deterministic provider: canonical help before target binding, then continuation after verified connection. Existing media/takeover owns private previews. Delete owned fixture threads/servers and exact process trees; verify ports. Late decoding, expired interactions, queued input, selection and close remain separate deterministic boundaries.
