## Execution
`computer.observe` reads bounded semantic information, with an optional image.
Inside `computer.exec`, `await ui.observe({emit:false})` returns a local object with
`observation.nodes`; script reads receive the full observation. The `full:true`
option controls the emitted snapshot instead of the default diff.

See the [adapter result contract](floret-redeven-adapter-and-projection.md).

## Platform adapters
The [browser contract](computer-use-browser.md) covers managed profiles, explicit CDP tabs and same-device Chrome extension bindings.

Stage viewing uses its independent bounded sampler; those samples never enter model history. See [Computer media](computer-use-media.md).

## Task access
Each computer invocation receives the permission snapshot established at its tool authorization boundary. Opaque origins never become origin grants.

Target selection chooses where work runs; it is not another confirmation of an already authorized action.

## Packaging and compatibility
Browser execution JSONL and Native Messaging use protocol 6 for Runtime-owned pause control, explicit page selection, reveal, popup progress and confirmed progress on observation failure.

Native window capture continues to respect Desktop-window exclusion and never substitutes an unrestricted display capture after failure.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Authority
computer.exec is one Floret invocation/effect attempt. QuickJS exposes ui/browser/log only; Runtime rechecks target policy, grant, cancellation and control per operation. One canonical turn retains target; live sampling may interleave. New target/permission stops with confirmed prefix. Private input/approval uses existing interaction, temporary approval bound to current target/URL/lease.

Unrestricted turns discover targets/select_target/exec under current permissions. Explicit/saved primitive consumers retain discovery, including read-only callers. Retry asks public canonical APIs for only source-Turn primitive names/current grants; Floret prepares missing metadata once before requery. No unrelated expansion/history store. BatchExclusiveGroup rejects conflicting prepared target calls before authorization/input; inventory/unrelated tools may coexist. Cross-batch gates apply. Rejection grants no replay, alias or rebinding.

## Guest and output
Require target, code, readable description. Bound each call to 30 s/50 operations and eight active namespaces; ui.budget/results expose remaining budget. Sequential awaits/loops/same-page navigation may compose; image judgments require returned screenshot/model review. No timers. const/let are call-local; globalThis survives healthy turn/target namespaces only.

SCRIPT_NO_PROGRESS means unresolved script without pending supported work; STALE_REFERENCE means invalid observed identity. Neither implies interference or permits replay/retargeting. Any failed host operation seals the call even if caught, retires namespace/dormant Promises and returns context_reset with confirmed effects. Unique missing/ambiguous lookup fails; optional query/count returns zero and waitFor timeout is data.

Closed diagnostics carry phase, known method/field, expected form, safe example and available source position/symbol. Keep raw interpreter text private; echo only known unsupported option names. Shared guide/help(read/visual/downloads/legacy) owns signatures: string names, numeric deltas, supported waits, validation before dispatch. CDP preserves actual correlated method and supplied signed code. Lost/malformed mutation exchange is helper_exchange/response_unavailable with unknown effect; diagnostics authorize nothing.

Limits: canonical snapshot 256 KiB; complete response 512 KiB; explicit UTF-8 logs 64 KiB. Stream logs before later operations. Retain earlier explicit output after read/navigation failure/timeout/uncertainty separately from current observations. Failed reads discard their data/pixels and stop later calls/logs; private pause discards invocation content. One bounded prefix buffer, no ledger/replay.

Only snapshot/observe/locator.snapshot accept emit; collections require log, screenshots/help always emit. emit:false preserves identity/budget. Default automatic snapshot is 32 KiB with opaque refs/parents; omissions are unknown/truncated. Full/node detail retains 2,000-code-point fields/flags; detail-mode change resets diff baseline. Failure uses the same bounded projection.

## Input
ui.type inserts, fill replaces. Native doubleClick/scroll keep parity; scroll centers the window and scrollAt selects coordinates without clicking. Semantic selector scroll is separate. Browser waits accept text|value, equals:string and optional timeout, read visible textContent/value without new input; native rejects these conditions. Completed waits survive later guest failure.

Drag duration_ms is integer 0..5000; straight held path, zero adds no delay. Monotonic scheduling avoids accumulated waits, not transport overhead. Cancel/takeover/document invalidation stops and releases only owned input at last confirmed position. Unknown replies never replay. NativeInputSequence starts timing after acknowledged down, retains authorization/cancellation and event receipts. Independent AppKit qualifies native timing; browser results cannot.

## Reads and identity
[Semantics](computer-use-semantics.md) owns schema v2; [read contract](computer-script-read-contract.md) owns strict shapes, branchable absence and bounds. getByRole(role,{name?, exact?, root_ref?}) uses canonical roles; snapshots/nodes/subtrees are direct, legacy observe/read wrappers remain.

locator.text reads one explicit unique HTML innerText through fixed isolated-world code: <=12,000 Unicode characters, rendered_element scope and truncation; no hidden/unloaded text or arbitrary DOM script. Document/text/SVG reject TARGET_CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE before reading, without substituting parent/body. Attributes are string|null, rejecting >2,000 code points. Method/capability/choose_supported_read facts survive all layers. Unknown reads stop but preserve valid refs; model may explicitly choose another supported read.

Image input handles bind immutable frame/document/image; editable metadata cannot retarget. Download results always include downloads and immutable cursor-bound wait. After export inspect existing ID instead of clicking again. Screenshots accompany results, never require paths/PNG export.

One needs_observation value drives execution/output. Safe snapshot (even emit:false) or screenshot clears it; input, staleness, failed reads or unknown effects require fresh observation. observation_status requires current safe evidence; title is insufficient. Private takeover excludes pixels/observations from model history.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Snapshot and node identity
Observations include `semantic_schema_version: 2`, `document_id`, `roots`, `nodes`, `truncated`, optional `focus_ref`, `total` and `execution_mode`.

Browser role resolution scans the complete authorized AX scope independently of the bounded model observation. A unique control after node 1000 remains resolvable; a duplicate beyond the presentation boundary remains ambiguous. References still require document revision and fresh DOM/AX identity validation.

`children_truncated` marks exported nodes with omitted descendants, including Runtime byte pruning. It is not evidence of empty rows or virtualization. Agents can read a row or table subtree through `root_ref`; completeness claims require checking the returned truncation facts.

Single-node reads use the same bounded observation path on browser, macOS and
Linux. child_refs only links returned nodes; an omitted child is not an empty
subtree. Native child-list read failures stop observation rather than becoming
empty arrays.

Name, description and string value have a 2,000 Unicode code-point budget.
name_truncated, description_truncated and value_truncated are true only when
the adapter omitted part of that field; snapshot truncated continues to describe
omitted nodes. Runtime validates these flags and preserves them in compact,
detailed, diff and single-node output. A detailed read does not remove field limits.
Browser query items also carry name_truncated when needed.

References compare the full native name through a bounded SHA-256 digest, never
the displayed prefix. Changed names receive different tokens so a fresh observation
cannot rebind an old reference. Browser collection cursors include complete-name digests
for every match, including items outside the current page. The existing reference
table and cursor owner remain authoritative; no additional lifecycle or replay
state exists. A failed or malformed DOM/AX identity read is observation-unavailable,
not proof of a stale reference. Preserve the observed token and sanitized protocol
method/code, reject input before dispatch, and require successful validation on a
later explicit call. Only confirmed identity changes invalidate the token. Semantic selectors match full names, including on native adapters.

Both directions of every parent/child edge must agree. An observation describes the bounded returned tree, not an exhaustive view of every application node.

## Roles, states and relationships
One Runtime alias inventory owns normalization and canonical selector expansion.
Standard landmarks including navigation, main, banner, contentinfo and
complementary, plus supported structural/live-region roles, round-trip through
this inventory. Unknown `other` remains reference-only, never a wildcard. Invalid
canonical selectors return safe field/expected/recovery diagnostics before dispatch.
Browser references are opaque bounded hashes of controller, document revision,
frame, native node identity, role and complete-name digest. The existing reference table remains their sole
owner; no second alias registry exists.

An ignored or truncated target has no invented reference; a platform-computed name or safe description may still be available.

Confirmed actions survive an observation failure; failed content never enters model history and input is not replayed.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Discovery and selection
`computer.targets` lists browser profiles/pages and application windows without a preselected target. Explicit system/personal-browser tasks use `system`, which excludes managed and native window candidates and never starts a managed profile.

Set application to a name or bundle ID for bounded installed-app discovery,
including apps not running. Discovery never launches. Selecting an application
candidate opens/restores that exact catalog entry; one accessible window is
selected, while zero or multiple windows return launch facts and window candidates.
App and foreground grants, current target ownership and private pause boundaries
are checked before launch. Launch uncertainty never authorizes automatic replay.

A changed title/URL requires fresh discovery rather than a silent substitute.

## Default work and explicit switching
For `current`, the Runtime reads the thread's `computer_target_id`. An existing selection must still resolve to that exact resource.

Empty, failed and pending inventory reads retain cancellation, return and close controls.

## Persistence and fork
The migrated product store remains the only selection store.

A lost task page fails until an authorized candidate is selected. Deleting product settings removes the selection and grants; a later bind never recreates a deleted thread.

## Binding contract and observation identity
Selection returns version 2 with exact backend availability and the shared core
script guide and one bounded initial observation through the normal runtime gate.
Observation failure retains selected:true and needs_observation; private pauses
retain selection without leaking content. Confirmed app opening remains
action_executed:true. ui.help discloses read, visual and download details on demand.
The earlier verbose capability fields are superseded by this model-facing guide;
there are no product consumers of those fields. It is not a new registry or authorization source. Native adapters reject
browser-only query, attribute and image-coordinate operations before dispatch.

discovery_name is the discovery label. target_name comes from this call's
observed title, or the stable target ID if no title was observed;
observation_status distinguishes current observation from no new observation.
A failed or zero-operation script must not present an old about:blank label as a
current page. Flower activity shows localized validation/preparation/confirmed or
unknown-effect guidance from returned facts. These facts do not create retry authority.

## Observation
Floret supplies ThreadFactsSource, ThreadWindowSource and canonical body readers. v7.87.4 includes bounded text, lazy fields, startup reuse and single-mutation title summaries from <=16 KiB canonical prefix, without detail/index writes. Blank-module adoption verifies released historical continuation/restart. Floret alone owns cadence, versions, buffers, Activity reduction and reads.

Root/child/command receipts share bounded windows containing canonical Summary in the same baseline. No separately sampled preparation/watermark. Authorized history POST installs interest on the ordered observer; item POST expands only published frozen-live/manifest/hash-verified locators. Recheck endpoint/user/namespace each read. Workspace facts preserve equal sidebar cache identity. Each observer has two cancellable slots: conversation and child. Malformed metadata cannot replace classification. Empty prefix proves no absence of effects; invocation completion is not task success. Model chooses authorized observation/work; never replay tools. Actual interactions/cancellation/dispatch/uncertainty retain authority; failure to encode safe result is infrastructure failure. Persisted questions keep canonical answer/cancel after restart, without host migration/auto-answer.

request_key remains send idempotency for transient browser outbox, not invocation identity. ask_user supports write and select_or_write; fixed choices always include custom text even without write_label. concepts.title: Flower Agent Plugins
concepts.summary: Flower loads Agent Plugins 1.0.0 as environment-scoped Skills and MCP extensions. This domain is separate from native `.redevplugin` packages, their SDK and marketplace. A manifest identifies a package; it does not register a marketplace listing or grant execution permission.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Ownership and supported format
Redeven owns distribution/admission/state/credentials/UI; published Floret owns invocation, approval, effects, history/recovery; official MCP Go SDK owns wire/sessions. No local dependency copy or second lifecycle.

Root plugin.json declares https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json; validate 1.0.0 locally, diagnosing unknown top-level fields and ignoring foreign namespaces. Skills are immediate skills/<name>/SKILL.md children. mcp.json declares the matching canonical MCP schema. Isolate invalid entries; malformed MCP disables that component type. Support stdio/Streamable HTTP; diagnose/skip legacy SSE. Do not interpret hooks, commands, postinstall or private formats.

stdio accepts executable tokens or ./ package paths, not shell expressions. Expand PLUGIN_ROOT (managed snapshot) and PLUGIN_DATA (persistent installation data) once in args/env/cwd only; cwd stays contained. Do not inherit parent secrets. HTTP headers are literal; generated protocol/auth fields win and redirects are denied.

## Discovery and distribution
Administrators select readable local directories, public GitHub repository/ref/path, or explicit HTTPS catalogs. Resolve refs to immutable commit receipts before bounded download; local directories become snapshots. Flower catalogs use schema_version flower.agent_plugin_catalog.v1, id, and plugins containing id plus {type: github, repository, ref, path} sources; this is outside the Agent Plugins standard.

Catalogs only recommend GitHub: no local installation, enabling, credentials or execution. Ship no default market/address/automatic search. [Catalog integration](flower-plugin-catalogs.md) owns opt-in sources/metadata. Admit explicit ASCII HTTPS/valid ports; reject private resolved targets, unsafe redirects, archive links/duplicates and Windows drive/stream paths. Before extraction count files/directories, allow at most 32 separators and use pinned os.Root writes. Materialize contained local symlinks; reject escapes. Limits: 4,096 entries, 16 MiB/file, 128 MiB/package/archive, 1 MiB/manifest/catalog.

## Review, persistence and recovery
Preparation owns at most four workers, two minutes each, without executing commands. Review source/components/entry points/changes before commit. New installations default disabled; new update components require selection. MCP configuration changes clear corresponding credentials; every update clears discovery.

Under <stateDir>/ai/agent-plugins/: registry.sqlite kind flower_agent_plugins/schema 1 has readonly preflight and atomic revision-CAS; packages/<sha256> stores snapshots, staging/<operation UUID> preparation, data/<installation UUID> retained data. Digests bind paths/bits/bytes. Unknown/future/drifted databases fail unchanged. One registry owns installation/component/discovery state.

Namespace/endpoint/user scope operations; request identity plus reviewed digest bind commit, and changed-selection replay fails. Ready operations expire at 30 minutes but survive disconnect/resume. Restart fails interrupted preparation. Shutdown cancels/drains workers; cleanup removes only unreferenced packages/stages, never retained data. Conversation snapshots/restores omit extension configuration/data/credentials and never construct another manager.

SecretsStore schema 4 stores immutable write-only references; no values in listings/operations/audit. Replace/clear invalidates discovery; empty objects clear and omission preserves. Uninstall retains data by default; explicit permanent deletion validates UUID/pinned root, rejecting escaping replacements. Snapshot stat/read/link inspection also uses rooted handles.

GitHub automatic checks default enabled as an explicit preference, run at most every six hours, and record availability only. Applying updates always repeats preparation/review; checks never download/apply/enable/execute.

## Projection and authorization
Project package Skills/MCP into existing managers without standalone copies. Skills bind plugin name/installation UUID/name; MCP binds installation/digest/component/revision/credential/schema. Reject namespaced standalone writes. Readers inspect; authenticated administrators manage; stdio checks additionally need write+execute.

Each skill read/MCP call resolves current authority and leases the resource. Digest mismatch fails closed. Update/uninstall cannot retire leased installations; disable prevents new dispatch immediately. Recheck MCP configuration after connecting and before dispatch. Floret retains in-flight/unknown-outcome semantics without replay. Explicit connection checks discover tools without bypassing conversation permissions.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Managed snapshots and containment checks are not an OS sandbox. Enabled local commands run with the runtime user's privileges and may access resources allowed by that process. Native plugin markets and signed `.redevplugin` runtime admission are unchanged. Private GitHub authentication, OAuth onboarding, legacy SSE and external marketplace publication are outside this implementation.

concepts.title: Flower attachment resources
concepts.summary: Redeven owns bytes/metadata, authenticated owner, quotas and retention; Floret owns turn membership. Upload once, send opaque attachment_id, display attachment://v1 locators and revalidate provider resources. Never expose paths or substitute product claims for canonical membership. Owner/quota/membership/metadata/digest/byte failures reject only the affected reference.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Identity and provider preparation
Redeven product threadstore v1 owns generated attachment ID, authenticated user hash, private relative storage name, detected/sanitized media metadata, exact size/SHA-256, optional strict UTF-8 code-point/line counts, source/state/idempotency and retention claims. Floret ResourceRef is content-addressed; display locator is attachment://v1/<attachment-id>/<encoded-name>. Retention never authorizes canonical reads.

Admit files independently of model modalities/tools. Preserve recognized text/image/PDF types; other files, including Office and non-UTF-8 documents, keep original bytes/name as application/octet-stream. Active UTF-8 uses text/plain; pasted long text requires strict UTF-8. Queue/admission enforce owner, staging, count and byte bounds, not a model MIME allowlist.

Capabilities affect presentation only. Supported modalities receive native content; otherwise the owning user message/tool result receives a factual manifest: name, media_type, size_bytes, locator, content_included:false, content_trust:untrusted. It adds no system message, tool-selection instruction or generic failure advice. Tool definitions own access guidance; manifest implies neither extraction, tool availability nor parser installation. The model chooses tools or explains its limitation. Switching models never rejects retained attachments/images; verify canonical descriptors/digest before the same manifest fallback, preserving native rendering for capable models.

## Reads and copies
Historical reads revalidate membership and bytes. Upload/image lookup uses current-path public Floret windows (50 items, 128-byte previews), one authorized subscription and page/stable-leaf correlation; no full hydration or retention-inventory authorization. Resolved handles prove ownership/metadata only. Hash during materialization; provider/text/image consumers verify their exact snapshots and downloads verify before returning paths. Avoid prehash plus reread. Bound size/cancellation; corrupt bytes never publish a copy.

Floret v7.51.1 exposes user and confirmed tool descriptors canonically. Retention distinguishes tool media from uploads; never parse image refs as upload rows.

attachment.materialize requires current execution/canonical authorization, RWX and normal write policy. Create a unique regular scratch copy using cancellable 32 KiB streaming with exact size/SHA-256; image locators retain bounded validation. Failure deletes private staging, repeated names never overwrite edited copies, and output exposes only the work path.

## Lifetime
Cleanup removes work copies, never original inputs/images. Retained references permit rematerialization after cleanup/restart/compaction/parent deletion. Historical Fork inherits refs only through its canonical cut and separately copies current scratch/staging. Product settings/claims publish transactionally without another admitted-message map.

Files derives input/media pages from public windows with current product authorization. Last-reference inventory includes inactive paths/queued inputs but grants no read authority. External files/deliveries retain destinations and survive cleanup. Existing upload/media backup scope excludes disposable task files.

sections.body: Redeven does not inspect or migrate Floret storage, persist message ordering, expose a filesystem path, accept a client owner, authorize by locator, or infer canonical membership from its claim table. Neither transport embeds bytes or a URL identity in a turn JSON body.

concepts.title: Flower backup and recovery
concepts.summary: Readiness drains generations; storage owners snapshot/migrate their data and Floret ends old execution. Recover history/settings/read-state/uploads without stopping other surfaces. sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Preserved snapshots
Ordinary startup, binary changes and transactional migrations do not create full snapshots. A damaged old snapshot cannot block healthy live data.

Abandoned task staging is removed only after any durable replacement completes and before a new generation opens; an unclosed generation prevents that path.

## Administrator recovery
Settings and the Flower maintenance action expose backup time, source build, size and protection.

Old unfinished Turns become terminal, old interactions become resolved and non-executable, and queued input remains canonical readonly `RestoredInputs`.

Diagnostics use the existing sanitized export and do not include conversations, credentials, database contents or uploaded files by default.

sections.title: Contract

## Compaction and continuation
[Manual compaction](flower-context-compaction.md) defaults to explicit continue_goal intent. Retry and restart use canonical preparation and confirmed tools. Redeven forwards intent and renders state without a second execution coordinator.

## Goal ownership and execution
User and model updates enter Floret's shared journal writer with request identity and expected version. An existing unfinished Goal remains authoritative across continuation and context restoration.

Stop cancels execution and reflection; deletion only cancels future Goal checks.

## Interaction and recovery
Selecting or entering /goal opens an in-composer command chip.

Each popup opening confirms detail through the existing read coordinator before showing canonical text.

A failed binding leaves the draft available for retry; no cross-thread target validation is relaxed and no attachment is uploaded twice.

Skill rediscovery uses one authoritative catalog and deterministic text; disabled or newly restricted skills cannot reuse an activation cache. Loaded skill instructions remain historical model facts.

## Skill catalog and explicit reads
The automatic skill catalog contains current available names and descriptions in stable priority/name order.

Disabled, deleted, restricted, unreadable or invalid skills cannot return older instructions as current content.

Whole-request wire bytes and body tool-result bytes are reported separately by the regression tests; these are byte measurements, not tokenizer counts or production change rates.

## Snapshot lifecycle
UserInput.Context retains ordinary submitted facts and references. Automatic facts use ModelContextSnapshot, never historical free-text parsing.

No new thread, storage migration, historical text parsing, or product-owned snapshot is required.

Authorized canonical reads and the existing workspace subscription carry the same snapshot, record location, changed/removed keys and latest request use.

Subtask details use the same component and bounded detail cache.

## Presentation
One confirmed request supplies native input-token usage, visible Unicode character counts and recent cache rate as independent measurements. Missing historical values remain unavailable; visible characters never estimate or explain token differences, and no provider history is reconstructed.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Optional runtime configuration
REDEVEN_AGENT_AI_PLUGIN_CATALOGS is a runtime-process JSON array of {id, name, url}; unset/whitespace/[] means none. Example:team/Team extensions/https://catalog.example.com/plugins.json, never a default. Restart applies config. No official URL, startup fetch/search/remote switch/automatic enrollment.

Limits:16sources,1 MiB, IDs plugin-name syntax≤128characters, names nonempty single-line≤128Unicode, unique IDs/URLs. HTTPS host required; reject userinfo/query/fragment/unknown fields/malformed config explicitly. Network checks occur only when browsing through bounded public distribution.

Configured sources use configured:<id>/managed:true and memory only. User UUID/CAS sources retain independent 16 limit. Configured URLs take display precedence without deleting user records; removal reveals retained source. User APIs cannot delete configured sources. Config changes do not revise installation registry or alter snapshots/credentials/data. Desktop/Web use authenticated runtime routes; renderer-only environment has no effect.

## Directory document
flower.agent_plugin_catalog.v1 contains directory id/plugins; entry{id, optional display, source{type:github, repository, ref, path}}. IDs follow plugin-name syntax≤128; unique entry IDs. Limits 128entries/1 MiB, reject overflow rather than truncate. Empty[] valid; missing/null arrays, unsupported schema, trailing JSON/unknown top-level-entry-source fields reject. display alone allows discarded additive fields:single-line name/author≤128Unicode, description≤512. Render text only, no HTML/badges/credentials/configuration. Incompatible changes need a new schema.

Existing public-GitHub normalizer validates repository/ref/commit/path (default .). Different repository paths stay independent installs. Catalog identity/removal never changes installed identity/state.

## Browse and install boundary
Browse reads bounded JSON only, no archive/preparation/process/enablement. Install invokes the existing manual-GitHub preparation:resolve exact revision, snapshot package, validate real manifest/components. Preview uses actual metadata, not directory claims; commit binds reviewed digest/explicit selection. Listing/topic/manifest is no endorsement.

Fetch failure exposes Retry, not empty success. Unconfigured/unavailable/removed discovery cannot affect installed management/execution. [Extensions](../ui/flower-extensions.md) owns UI; [Agent Plugins](flower-agent-plugins.md) owns snapshots/permissions.

concepts.title: Flower plugin generation
concepts.summary:
Flower can help users create plugins, but the generated-plugin flow is not a
second plugin platform. Redeven owns the user intent capture, prompt
orchestration, review UX, approval presentation, and product timeline
projection. ReDevPlugin owns templates, validators, package builders, lifecycle
APIs, runtime contracts, sandbox surfaces, and platform policy. Floret owns the
tool dispatch and approval lifecycle that Flower must use.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
A Flower-generated plugin flow is a sequence of approved product actions over released ReDevPlugin APIs.

A plugin-generation handler may run already-approved local steps and call released ReDevPlugin adapters, but it must not perform its own approval wait, bypass Floret dispatch, mutate Flower activity rows directly, or convert plugin audit rows into Flower timeline state.

If a generated plugin needs a platform capability that does not exist in released ReDevPlugin, the requirement is recorded upstream instead of hidden behind a Redeven-local helper.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Flower must not write plugin registry rows, mint bridge tokens, place plugin UI assets directly under Env App routes, bypass package inspection, signature assessment, explicit confirmation, or trust policy, grant storage/network/ runtime access outside ReDevPlugin brokers, or call a business adapter before ReDevPlugin has built the request context.

A requested approval remains waiting until Floret resolves it.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
`internal/ai/prompt_builder.go` is the sole source of the base system prompt.

Visual output uses the existing [inline HTML preview](../ui/flower-inline-media.md)
contract when it communicates better than text; ordinary nonvisual answers remain
text. Existing direct WebGL guidance remains unchanged.

Delivering a created or confirmed local file requires a clickable Markdown link
with a clear file name or title and the full absolute path. Plain text or inline
code cannot be the only delivery entry point. Destinations containing spaces or
parentheses use angle brackets, such as `[Report](</workspace/report (final).html>)`.
Paths must not be invented and links must not use `file://`. Paths inside commands
and code examples may remain code. Existing authorized file previews own opening;
this prompt rule does not change historical messages or file authorization.

Discovery checks symlinks and Git boundaries; incomplete discovery and context overflow fail admission rather than silently clipping facts.

[Agent Plugin skills](flower-agent-plugins.md) join the existing skill catalog with installation-qualified selectors and current-authority checks. Packages do not rewrite the base system prompt or install a separate rule loader.

There is no separate social or creative prompt path.

Deterministic tests require the exact base prompt across all 18 permission, profile
and allowlist combinations, pin reviewed tool-definition hashes, check file-delivery
requirements and bound the prompt to 2,000 bytes.

Synthetic receipts never execute proposed tools; the Service lane runs inside disposable state. Skipped paid runs are not new model qualification, and historical scores do not establish quality for this prompt.

The base prompt adds one short execution strategy: use the most direct tool/API/CLI,
batch known steps with scripts, inspect UI state as needed, and use reported
effects/current state after interruption. This stays within the existing 2,000-byte
budget; it does not add a procedural checklist.

Default discovery still has three computer entry points. Definitions allow loops,
conditions and multiple pages within the existing budget. Selection/help responses
own exact signatures, snapshot shape, document-bound refs, automatic image output,
backend-specific coordinates and download handoff. Historical primitive consumers
retain executable contracts under current permissions.

concepts.title: Flower storage ownership and migrations
concepts.summary: Floret owns canonical Agent formats; Redeven owns product facts and uploads. Supported state upgrades through stable kinds, contiguous atomic migrations and public APIs while preserving history. Unknown, future, drifted or invalid state blocks Flower without resetting data or disabling the core Runtime.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Storage owners
Redeven consumes the exact published Floret version in go.mod with `GOWORK=off`.

Floret owns bounded startup recognition and background per-thread migration. Each validated dependency closure publishes atomically; retained sources retire only after complete verification. The oldest v2-v5 snapshots reserve historical identities through a resumable scan before new-thread admission. Segmented stores admit new threads immediately. Redeven uses public status, thread preparation and per-thread media contracts and never decodes upstream records.

Published Floret v7.87.0 removes hidden Activity field preparation from ordinary startup, retains summary metadata on large activity admission, batches explicit locator writes and skips same-value SQLite upserts. Its recent manifest cache is bounded, memory-only and owned upstream. No new host indexes, full-text indexes or duplicate conversation storage are introduced. First disclosure may still prepare the selected complete activity once; this is not a claim of field-granular cold preparation.

Cancellation, shutdown and execution-context settlement resolve canonical control records through Floret. The host keeps the original Stop request and does not read or reconstruct upstream conversation bodies to settle it.

A read-state failure cannot become a core Runtime constructor failure or a synthetic read record.

Redeven also owns the [Agent Plugins registry](flower-agent-plugins.md), snapshots and installation data. Its schema-1 SQLite store is separate from canonical conversation history; credential references resolve through SecretsStore schema 4. Neither owner decodes Floret records.

## Readonly checks and owner transactions
`sqliteutil` owns WAL-aware readonly preflight, integrity checks and complete SQLite snapshots for product and read-state owners. Inspection never creates missing data or runs a migration.

Required upgrade snapshots precede Floret space maintenance and all migrations, as specified by the [backup and recovery contract](flower-backup-and-recovery.md).

## Frozen historical queue conversion
The migration-only `pendinginputlegacy` package owns the complete interpretation of historical queue bytes: session identity, options, context shapes, default values, resource metadata and normalization limits.

The v4-to-v5 product transaction imports canonical pending inputs through Floret's public idempotent import API, records necessary product authority and removes retired source tables before commit. The upgrade operation contains only target build, original snapshot identity and completion; owner versions and canonical records remain the progress authority.

## Resource and authorization retention
Product upload references retain resources for every canonical thread that contains them, including ordinary forks, nested forks and restored inputs.

After activation, product recovery pages settings, retains each thread's complete descriptors and promotes eligible admitted input. Failures retain the cleanup gate while independent threads recover. Tool-media collection keeps its complete global inventory, write gate and idle constraint.

Bounded keyset maintenance and compaction stop and drain with their owning generation.

concepts.title: Flower working files and deliverables
concepts.summary: Flower stores intermediate files in Runtime state and final files at the user's destination. Redeven owns filesystem policy, bytes and UI; Floret owns canonical results/identities. No artifact index, transcript copy, new upstream API or domain migration.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Placement and authority
Runtime owns <StateDir>/task-files/<ThreadID>/{scratch, staging} for intermediates. Final files use the requested destination or selected project/worktree, independent of temporary cwd. Admission/provider context publish identical absolute roots. System placement overrides skill suggestions without filename heuristics or permission changes. Source/tests/builds retain normal locations. Terminal children receive FLOWER_SCRATCH_DIR/FLOWER_STAGING_DIR, never FLOWER_OUTPUT_DIR; cwd/HOME/cache/TMPDIR keep normal semantics and OS temp its lifecycle. Long thread paths cannot become TMPDIR.

The private writable root grants no sibling/project authority. All file/patch tools share registry policy; patch cwd resolves relative paths only. Reject sibling roots and escaping symlinks. Authorized external/detached roots need no additional whitelist; [editing policy](tool-permission-runtime.md) applies.

## Fork
One action copies current scratch/staging even for historical conversation cuts; files are not historical snapshots and projects/finals remain shared. Exclude new source admissions/cleanup, drain admitted work cancellably and reject unreaped processes. Rooted bounded copying preserves executable bits, checks identity/size/time/final tree, rejects unsupported types/external links/hard links, and renames only complete private staging into the new ThreadID.

Publish settings and validated canonical upload-retention claims transactionally after copying, retaining the source-deletion gate. Failed/unadmitted work stays invisible. Canonical Fork replay finishes preparation without recopying admitted edited/cleaned forks. A source marker supports interrupted publication/context only; cleanup preserves it, deletion removes it. Recheck ownership before removing failed/canceled unadmitted copies.

Startup/periodic recovery scans 50 names per batch, skips in-flight target/staging gates and removes private stages/marked forks lacking settings. Explicit orphan operations share the target gate. Retry retains canonical identity with a fresh independent copy. Context maps ancestor suffixes to the new root and instructs inspection/repair of hardcoded paths, including nested forks; never rewrite history. Ancestor cleanup cannot delete descendants.

## Delivery and discovery
file.present verifies an authorized regular file outside application state, hashes cancellably with identity/size/mtime consistency, and returns path/title/MIME/size/SHA-256/mtime/endpoint plus canonical thread/turn/run IDs. It never moves/uploads/deletes bytes; failure preserves originals.

Files reads authorized successful canonical Floret results: 50 records/page, 32 KiB/record, preserving Fork/restart provenance without a crawl/second ledger. Available means accessible and unchanged size/mtime, not rehashed history. Hashes describe delivery-time bytes; changed/missing/unavailable are observations, not hidden versions.

Files defaults to deliveries/uploads. Process files separates canonical tool images from Temporary files; grouping changes no ownership/retention/provider history. One dialog controller discovers 50-item windows with 128-byte previews, advances at viewport end/through empty windows/during search, and declares completeness only at cursor end. After independent initial sources, requests serialize; repeated cursors expose Retry. Temporary navigation/child preview pauses discovery. No full View/retention scan.

Same-owner refresh retains successful rows/equal identities; append preserves focus/scroll. Thread/runtime changes invalidate content; close/change aborts discovery/previews/download reads and fences late responses. Partial failures preserve other rows. Floe Dialog owns child placement, focus/Tab/Escape and row restoration; closing preserves query/filter/scroll. Successful folder handoff closes the dialog. Env App supplies rich renderers; shared Desktop supports image/PDF/text, Markdown and opaque-origin sandboxed HTML. Unsupported formats offer Download.

loadTaskFile uses existing endpoints/common validation: reauthorize each 256 KiB, reject version/offset drift, cap previews at 20 MiB and stream downloads. Desktop permits exact thread endpoints/query keys with IPC cancellation. Browser Blob sinks retain their memory cost; reads never publish/relocate originals.

## Download ownership
Enqueue downloads in the existing Shell manager before destination selection. Env App uses its top-bar Downloads owner; Desktop full/companion share one manager. Deliveries/temporary files use validated authorized chunks; uploads/images use the attachment reader. Retry closures bind original thread/source/runtime; metadata stores neither attachment URLs nor Blobs.

Only the manager owns progress/destination/cancel/failure/retry/completion. Closing previews/lists or switching threads stops previews, not admitted downloads. Reopened lists consult active thread downloads before cleanup. Cancellation remains terminal after late destination/read/write settlement; finalization cannot cancel. Native destinations expose Reveal/Open; browser handoff is identified. Records last until Shell ends or Clear finished; prior OS/browser history is not imported.

## File panel presentation
Use published Floe controls/icons/theme tokens. Header: title/close; body: search/refresh. Files/Process files exposes source filters only for multiple known kinds, resetting vanished selections to All. No ambiguous totals, empty headings, collapsed images or manual paging. Delivered files labels only file.present results. Same-name images retain names and show existing timestamps.

Rows provide keyboard preview, compact origin/size, lazy thumbnails and exceptional availability, without success badges/MIME parameters/endpoint IDs/absolute paths (including tooltips). Paths remain action inputs. Localized names wrap beside accessible download/folder/source actions at phone widths. Temporary files appears only when present, with Back/preview/separate confirmed cleanup; Process files has no blanket cleanup. Return restores focus/scroll; protected work/downloads disable cleanup.

Action feedback preserves controls; page failures offer Retry without hiding successful content. Stable responsive viewport scrolls body only, retaining header/close. All locales are explicit; [loading continuity](../ui/page-loading-continuity.md) applies. Browser tests cover themes/phone/search/partial failure/cancellation/routing/focus/cleanup. Real layer-4000 hit-testing covers foreground previews, keyboard, temporary reads, same-name images and HTML/Markdown in both carriers.

## Cleanup
List at most 200 files after inspecting at most 10,000 entries, disclosing truncation/lower bounds. Confirmed RWX cleanup pins each owned scratch/staging directory from Runtime state, rejects symlinks and checks opened identities. Paths grant no deletion authority. concepts.title: Flower canonical thread queries
concepts.summary:
Flower exposes two read-only tools for finding another readable conversation
and reading its content: `threads.query` and `threads.read`. The tool contract
is intentionally smaller than Floret's published general query API.
`threads.aggregate` is not registered or dispatched.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Find, browse, read

- `threads.query` defaults to `object: threads`, listing recently updated
  conversations first. Optional `title` is one literal, case-insensitive title
  fragment. Optional `thread_id` selects one exact conversation.
- To browse `messages` or `tool_calls`, provide one `thread_id`. Records are
  chronological; there are no model-controlled sort keys or detailed filters.
- `limit` defaults to 50, with a maximum of 200. Continue with `next_cursor` and
  unchanged input. Pass a record's `ref` to `threads.read` for complete content,
  following its cursor until no continuation remains.
- Nested `filter`, message-body matching, argument/result matching, keywords,
  phrases, time/role/tool/status predicates, grouping and aggregation are not
  accepted by the tool schema or handler. Unsupported inputs fail explicitly.
- Reasoning, secrets and private provider state remain excluded. Tool arguments
  and confirmed results are available only through authorized content reads.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
## Authorization owner

Authenticated session authority supplies read permission, user, endpoint and
namespace identity. Redeven reconstructs the readable scope for every page and
read. Tool parameters and returned references never grant authority. Changed
scope invalidates frozen cursors; a new query starts under current permission.
The adapter uses published Floret public APIs and never reads Floret SQL or
reconstructs canonical records.

## Historical results and presentation

Saved query/read results remain previewable after restart and after their
original refs expire. The historical aggregate result renderer remains solely
for immutable already-saved tool exchanges; it cannot dispatch aggregation.
Private query contents are not added to Activity snapshots. The intent label
and explicitly opened, bounded result preview remain the presentation boundary.

## Storage and execution

The canonical owner stores source locators and metadata. Flower requires no
full-text index and schedules no startup or background indexing. Metadata-only
browsing requests one thread's ordered records; canonical full content is read
only as needed. Floret's retired optional indexing declarations are not a
product capability. The engine's published query API may retain compatibility
filters without exposing those filters to Flower's model tools.

frontmatter.title: Direct image reading and tool media retention

concepts.summary:
image.read inspects authorized files/snapshots. Redeven owns bytes/authorization;
Floret owns history/membership. File references stay references; results use native
images, not browsers, temporary servers or Base64 result JSON. Original snapshots
remain available after model preparation.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
- File mode accepts file_path and optional target_id; locator mode requires a
  canonical media:v1 locator, excludes file_path/target_id, and reuses original
  bytes without reopening the source. Default behavior remains unchanged.
- Every permission mode checks image capability, CanRead, filesystem scope and
  ToolTargetPolicy. Unavailable explicit targets fail without device fallback.
- File reads retain their 10 MiB bound; Computer snapshots retain 16 MiB.
- Locator-only crop accepts integer x/y/width/height within original image pixels,
  never clips, and saves a new lossless PNG with source_crop metadata. It uses
  fresh canonical authorization. Image pixels differ from CSS action coordinates.
- image.read stores original snapshots, while every model input (including crops
  and summaries) uses [default model preparation](computer-use-media.md). Original
  locators remain available for detail crops; no durable derivative cache exists.
- Floret preserves every image in ordered summary batches; capacity failures shrink
  the same unconsumed batch. Current user images remain exact. Tokens and JSON bytes have separate
  limits; indivisible overflow fails.
- Switching to a text model preserves all images and presents verified metadata and
  locators through the [attachment manifest](flower-attachment-resources.md), without
  blocking selection or claiming that the model has seen pixels.
- toolMediaStore retains immutable images in computer/keyframes across source
  changes, Retry, restart, Fork and compaction.
- Previews check ownership/canonical membership directly. Markdown images stay unchanged.

## Maintenance and interactive writes

One in-process media gate protects writes and the complete canonical inventory
through deletion, following Floret's published retention contract. Maintenance
skips a held gate or queued writers. An interactive write cancels a running
maintenance scan and waits for that scan to settle; its own wait honors caller
cancellation. Partial or failed inventory never authorizes deletion. No second
membership ledger, detached scan, speculative unlock or input replay is used.

concepts.title: Flower MCP runtime
concepts.summary: Redeven configures MCP and adapts the released official Go SDK, which owns stdio/Streamable HTTP sessions. Floret owns invocation, approval, one-shot effects, history/recovery. Add no second execution queue/lifecycle/retry authority. Unknown call outcomes are terminal and never replayed; invalid persisted config fails without changing bytes.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Configuration and protocol
Standalone configuration lives at `<stateDir>/ai/mcp.json`, with schema version 2, one monotonic configuration revision, and server revisions for optimistic edits. Persistence failure leaves the in-memory catalog unchanged.

Catalog limits are 32 servers, 128 tools per server, 32 KiB per schema, and 4 MiB total persisted configuration.

Package-owned connections project from the [Agent Plugins registry](flower-agent-plugins.md). They use the same SDK/session and Floret invocation paths, with separate credentials and explicit discovery. They cannot be edited through standalone MCP writes.

## Standalone identity
Creation accepts an omitted local ID and display name. The runtime generates a cryptographically random lowercase ID with an mcp_ prefix, independently of the name or connection address; duplicate explicit IDs are conflicts, never replacements. Edits require the saved ID and revision. Missing IDs with a nonzero revision fail without creating another connection. Existing IDs and exact-ID Skill dependency matching remain unchanged.

For new unnamed connections, use the HTTP hostname or local executable basename, then prefer serverInfo.title followed by serverInfo.name from the existing successful initialize exchange. Automatically selected names are trimmed, limited to 120 UTF-8 bytes without splitting a character, and reject control characters. Explicit names win. Edits with an omitted name retain the saved name, and checks never rename a connection. Disabled creation uses connection-derived names without starting a command or contacting the server.

Typing or opening a form does not probe connections. Failed discovery/persistence does not create a saved identity; retry remains an explicit user action. The persisted schema and credential-preservation rules do not change.

## Presentation icons
Save and explicit Check read `serverInfo.icons` from the existing SDK initialize result. Connection-preserving disabled edits retain icons; changed connection settings clear stale discovery.

Rejected sources receive the generated identity described in [the shared UI contract](../ui/flower-extensions.md#entry-icons).

## Execution and dependencies
Enabled, previously discovered tools join the dynamic tool surface before the existing permission filter. Their identity binds the exact server configuration and tool schema, so a changed or disabled configuration cannot execute through an old invocation name.

Enabled, checked configuration satisfies the catalog indicator; it does not promise current network reachability or bypass approval.

## Image results
Typed ImageContent and image EmbeddedResource blobs become immutable tool-media
attachments before the text display limit. Ordered text placeholders retain each
image's attachment index, original dimensions and canonical locator. Arbitrary
strings, structured JSON and resource links never trigger image downloads.
Admission bounds each original to 10 MiB/32 megapixels and each result to 64
images/32 MiB; HTTP SSE events allow 48 MiB for Base64 and metadata. The released SDK
retains its 16 MiB stdio frame bound; transport rejection is explicit and never
authorizes replay. Provider delivery uses the shared [model policy](computer-use-media.md).
If image retention fails after CallTool returned, the result records confirmed
invocation completion and unavailable output. This does not authorize tool replay,
including when retention observes cancellation. Already retained attachments stay
paired with the completed result.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
MCP tools are conservatively mutating and open-world regardless of server annotation claims. An MCP handler cannot run directly without that proof.

Server tool errors and known connection failures remain distinct from an unknown execution outcome.

Redeven passes model output capability as Floret ModelMaxOutputTokens, and only an explicit per-request limit as MaxOutputTokens. It never maps capability to a fixed output reservation.

The comparison logs are /tmp/redeven-budget-desktop-failures-focused.log and /tmp/redeven-budget-desktop-main-baseline.log.

Model reasoning capability, stream fields, history replay, and immutable thread settings are governed by [model reasoning capabilities and transport](model-reasoning-runtime.md).

Unsupported transports reject non-empty state before HTTP.

Hosted-turn diagnostics record the selected wire mode, and Floret lifecycle audit events carry batch index, batch size, event type, and observation time so operators can distinguish model serialization, provider single-call output, approval wait, dispatch, and completion without feeding diagnostics back into scheduling.

## Prompt and repository rule sources

## Related context usage

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Evidence and projection
Lifecycle evidence may retain frozen trigger candidates, pressure and validated replacement. Floret installs complete actor-owned context before publishing its version. Changed context bypasses text cadence; equal snapshots coalesce text in bounded queues. Redeven neither accumulates usage nor reconstructs lifecycle facts, invents budgets or infers capacity from weights.

## Independent capacity evidence
Published Floret v7.94.0 supplies optional typed request-byte and image-capacity evidence alongside
compaction decisions. Host preparation failures include exact actual/limit byte
counts; server HTTP 413 carries no guessed counts. Both can occur while the last
measured token ratio is low. The indicator retains that confirmed ratio, while
the divider explains the independent capacity cause and message-text estimate.
Cause-only events, reloads and Desktop RPC retain this distinction. Historical
records without this evidence remain unknown; no error-text inference is used.

Aggregate image evidence carries exact image counts or decoded bytes, with
preparation/response stage; counts never occupy byte or token fields. Desktop
RPC v5 reconstructs the typed upstream cause before Engine recovery; older peers
are rejected at the version handshake. During recovery
the inline divider says “Organizing image history…” in every shipped locale and
shows measured cause details. Token utilization remains independently measured.

Floret owns bounded recovery, complete ordered image-summary batching, protected
current inputs and replacement validation. A failed/cancelled summary never
installs a partial checkpoint, and completed tools are never replayed. Schema 34
migration belongs exclusively to Floret; Redeven never patches upstream records.

## Timeline
One row between short separators uses a compact surface-owned tooltip without expansion or reflow. Success labels canonical message text estimates explicitly, never as full provider-request input. Localize missing-count, running and cancelled explanations. Wrap original errors without clipping; localize the fallback only when absent.

The tooltip follows the active surface and global theme outside chat. Prefer above, or below near the top boundary. Delay pointer-exit dismissal for hovering/selection. Escape, Tab, blur and outside clicks dismiss it; the visibility owner closes it on process collapse. Retain keyboard/touch access and independent retry.

## Native web-search observation
Responses hosted search requests include web_search_call.action.sources for canonical Activity URLs. Qwen keeps its tool shape.

## Provider surface and history
Published Floret v7.92.2 PrepareResponsesHistory owns API-key OpenAI, compatible Responses, Qwen and ChatGPT native replay: search receipts, encrypted reasoning and function items survive local tools. Activity is no replay source. Disabling searches retains evidence; completed events supply output omitted from terminal snapshots. Confirmed incomplete Responses retain snapshots for length continuation; interrupted/failed streams install none. ChatGPT rejects incomplete responses; content filtering never advances history.

Preparation estimates full native input. API-key OpenAI uses response-ID/suffix continuation only with explicit responses_continuation and Engine permission; others send full input. Freeze selection/request across retries. Rejected IDs never trigger evidence-dropping retries; explicit configuration can select full replay. ChatGPT retains namespace/OAuth/WebSocket/published state.

Historical ID-only OpenAI states retain opt-in continuation; absent bytes cannot be recovered. New states store complete upstream envelopes. Reader removal needs a future-major domain migration, never within v7. Changed canonical prefixes discard stale suffixes/IDs; Floret isolates model/account/secrets. Manual Retry/Fork retain canonical facts/tool results but clear source state; transport retries preserve frozen requests. Acceptance covers provider modes, streamed-only output, suffixes, immutable retry, Goal review, truncation/restart.

Floret v7.37.0 owns append-only canonical history and lineages keyed by provider/model/reasoning/prompt/local-hosted tools/adapter/context policy/state compatibility. Flower reads persisted Activity or uses neutral presentation without unknown JSON/arguments.

## Provider rendering and estimation
Floret v7.26.0 EstimateRenderedRequest owns Responses, Chat Completions, Gemini signatures, Moonshot and Anthropic. Verified mappings use official vocabularies; unknown models use an explicit multilingual BPE proxy. Server rendering may differ; no host calibration ledger/network preflight.

## Anthropic Messages
Floret v7.95.0 owns HTTP/SSE, frozen cache hints, authorized attachments and native signed output. Flower maps controls/content/usage/events through public Gateway; retire the SDK route. Endpoint brand/intermediary does not select behavior. Engine policy allows at most four ephemeral markers and separately controls opaque state. Cache-off retains permitted signed history; secret isolation clears both reuse paths.

Completed output survives continuation/restart. Retry/Fork/compaction retain canonical facts and clear source state through Floret. Never fabricate signed historical reasoning or recast it as answer text. State stays opaque. Frozen transport retries resolve no attachments and carry new attempt IDs.

Usage separates uncached/cache-read/cache-write. Measured request input needs complete partitions and excludes service-transformed hosted/signed input; unsupported evidence remains estimated. Failed streams retain billing without advancing state. Diagnostics preserve public structured HTTP errors and exact byte limits.

model_gateway_anthropic_test.go covers final wire/usage/state/cache-off/secret isolation/frozen identity. Service regression retains signed/redacted blocks across two turns with separately typed public thinking. Shared argument/attachment/cancel/prepared-request tests remain; no qualification resumes production threads.

Floret v7.79.0 owns [measurement](model-request-measurement.md), frozen-prefix pressure and schema 28; Redeven adds no pressure policy/store.

## Provider request recovery
[Recovery](model-request-recovery.md) owns Engine retry budgets/deadlines/attempt diagnostics/current feedback, without another history owner.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Capability and transport
OpenAI-compatible Chat reasoning is capability-driven. Redeven reads only response fields named by that result, emits their fragments as reasoning without trimming provider whitespace, and never treats reasoning-only output as assistant body text.

Budget-only and fixed-thinking models never acquire synthetic effort names or a toggle merely because another model supports one.

## Default selection
Default asks for the model's own reasoning behavior. Thread creation, Thread
edits, and every Turn canonicalize it once, in
`config.CanonicalAIReasoningSelection`: on a model without verified reasoning
controls a budget-free Default is the omitted selection and is neither stored
nor sent. Default with a budget, Off, On, and named efforts remain explicit
intent and are rejected for such a model; personal memory keeps no reasoning
choice for it. Clients may send Default without knowing the model's capability
and must not drop or rewrite it themselves.

## Settings ownership
Thread model, reasoning and permission settings are Redeven product state. Execution authority records admission permission for historical attribution only, never as live tool authorization. The configured `current_model_id` initializes future threads only.

## Automatic titles
Published Floret v7.26.0 owns title reasoning and output limits. They never change the thread's saved reasoning choice or the main response policy.

The [live timeline contract](../ui/flower-live-timeline.md) owns canonical title status, persistence, and workspace-summary presentation.

concepts.title: OKF bundle lifecycle
concepts.summary: Redeven builds its embedded OKF bundle from curated source files under the top-level `okf/` authoring root, verifies deterministic dist outputs under `okf/dist/`, and embeds the resulting bundle into the binary used by Runtime and AI features for local retrieval.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
`build_assets.sh` invokes `build_okf_bundle.sh`, which runs `cmd/okf-bundle` against explicit source and dist roots. The builder emits the bundle, manifest and checksum deterministically. Summary and section bodies are embedded as structured data; Evidence remains in its source file but is omitted from ordinary concept opening unless requested. `okf/dist/*` is generated from source and is never an authoring surface.

## Quality gates
Report mode exposes layout, indexing, summary, evidence, duplication, lifecycle and budget issues without blocking cleanup. Strict mode fails structural and source-integrity violations, overdue reviews, and source totals above the hard cap. Final integration runs strict content quality after source integrity and before verifying the generated bundle.

## Source budget
Count Unicode characters in every source Markdown file under `okf/`, including the index and log, after CRLF-to-LF normalization; exclude `okf/dist/`. The report shows total, remaining capacity and index/concept/log usage. Exceeding 900,000 warns; strict quality accepts exactly 1,000,000 and fails above it. A per-concept `quality_exception` cannot waive this hard cap.

## Review and log lifecycle
Every concept declares `lifecycle` and `reviewed_at`: review contracts every 180 days, active measurements and operational evidence every 90 days, and retained history every 365 days. Retained history also needs a concise `retention_reason`. Report mode warns and strict mode fails on invalid or overdue metadata; expiry prompts review and never deletes a document automatically. Keep `log.md` to compact summaries from the last 30 days after durable knowledge moves into its concept.

## Index and retention
Keep categories and concept links in the index; the parser derives each retrieval summary from the concept's `# Summary`. Prefer an existing concept, preserve only decision-relevant historical conclusions and counterevidence, and remove obsolete detail from the current tree so Git history remains the recovery path.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: The bundle remains auditable only while OKF Markdown concepts are the sole authoring surface, source and lifecycle budgets are enforced through the shared parser, and `okf/dist/*` stays a generated verification artifact set rather than hand-edited truth. A `quality_exception` may document a justified per-concept length exception, but it never waives the source cap or other quality checks.

The `subagents` tool supports spawn, send input, wait, list, status, inspect, close, and close all.

Display timestamps, duplicated IDs and counts, and UI action flags remain outside that projection. Spawn and wait do not repeat task descriptions; list and explicit inspect retain them. Complete handoff bodies bypass generic output caps. Explicit event reads retain their full page contract. Parent reports, lifecycle events, bounded waiting, and the compact event panel are described in [Subagent parent events](subagent-parent-events.md).

item without creating a second parent confirmation. Child requests remain
blocked at their own authority boundary. The parent model can use completed
handoffs, perform independent work or explicitly ask for a dependency decision.
Unchanged attention is neither a timeout nor new progress. Parent UI activity

concepts.title: AI terminal tool runtime
concepts.summary: Redeven owns PTYs and bounded output; Floret v7 owns canonical tool calls, interactions, effect attempts, results and Activity. One adapter authorizes execution once and publishes current views. Product SQL stores no parallel terminal lifecycle or effect recovery.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
[Task-file placement](flower-task-files.md) supplies thread scratch/staging through
child-only environment variables while preserving project cwd and OS temporary
path conventions. Cleanup waits for owned terminal processes to be reaped.

PTYs use Floret execution/effect identities. `terminal.exec` waits 5 seconds when `yield_ms` is omitted or zero; positive values cap at 30 seconds. Yield returns a running process ID without stopping the command.

On macOS/Linux, one exit worker observes command exit without reaping, kills its process group, retires numeric signaling, verifies no live members within 2 seconds, then reaps and drains output. The unreaped root pins its PID through cleanup. Child cleanup preserves shell exit codes; only confirmed Stop termination means cancellation. Stop, input failure, the 30-minute limit and Service shutdown share this worker. Unconfirmed cleanup reports a runtime error and retains workload admission. Settlement stops the watchdog.

Long-lived commands stay foreground under the yielded process ID. Backgrounding and `nohup` cannot transfer ownership; escaping the PTY group/session is unsupported. Independent services need a managed lifecycle; previews use the managed browser. Names, CPU use and age never establish ownership.

`terminal.read` observes output after the caller's sequence for up to 60 seconds, returning early on output/exit. An expired observation retains process ID and cursor and reports `wait_expired`/`wait_ms`; `timed_out` means command timeout. Continue with the same ID and returned `last_seq`, without sleeps or command restarts.

Normal expiry uses Floret `BoundedWait`; Floret measures handler time and owns repeat protection. Immediate, failed, canceled and early reads gain no exemption, nor do neighboring repeated effects. No extra retry counter, clock, wake or durable ledger exists.

Reads are read-only effects: cancellation preserves process and cursor, then confirms the canceled result after observation returns. Execution/input retain shell-effect uncertainty rules. `terminal.write` bounds stdin; `terminal.terminate` kills the owned group and waits for reap/output drain. Thread Stop policy governs cleanup.

Read results contain incremental output, status, cursor, wait and exit facts. Command, cwd and timing remain in canonical Activity without repeated model echoes.

Browser payloads exclude local working paths, stdin, authorization proofs, and effect internals.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: No authority barriers, admission receipts, recovery handles or projection-cursor waits exist. Reads never retry settlement. Open-detail polling refreshes bytes, never canonical status or provider dispatch.

sections.title: Contract

- `tessiven.runtimes` / `GET /_redeven_proxy/api/tessiven/runtimes` returns   independent source availability and exact target paths. - `tessiven.runtime.inspect` / `POST .../runtimes/inspect` reads status,   bounded public diagnostics, or the original Desktop operation. - `tessiven.runtime.action` / `POST .../runtimes/actions` requests connection   or one supported `start`, `stop`, `restart`, or `update` process operation. - `tessiven.inspect/action` retain the canonical canvas version, bound instance,   and resource identity checks for Managed Services and containers.

No sibling module, replacement SDK, or product lifecycle queue is introduced.

Desktop registers its Tessiven host through owner-authenticated private Runtime control. Web Service, CodeSpace, nested frame, unrelated-origin and worker requests cannot declare a native source;

Ambiguous references fail closed.

## Connection and business access
Explicit connect reuses saved configuration and existing connection leases.

It cannot carry claimed permission flags, an arbitrary URL, another Runtime reference, or a process-lifecycle action.

Member removal and replacement retire the transport; no local or alternate route is substituted.

## Native lifecycle handoff
Process actions use saved direct Desktop placements and the existing [Desktop lifecycle owner](../desktop/desktop-runtime-process-lifecycle.md). The model cannot choose a download URL or release version; the existing release selector owns updates and post-operation verification.

Unknown connection outcomes require checking the selected connection in its native owner rather than retrying.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Identity and execution

Discover Docker/Podman independently, one service/engine, no inactive-context scan/fallback. Each has a shared two-second command budget; reuse selected endpoint inventory for health. Resource readiness stays separately bounded. Docker Desktop requires selected desktop-linux/desktop-windows context or exact endpoint alias; installed plugins cannot claim other engines. Validate with docker desktop version --format json, never slow desktop status. Resolve Podman Machine ownership before health.

Known Desktop management/health errors retain ID, implementation, config sources and supported actions. Missing CLI/permission/timeout/unknown failures never mean stopped. Start requires stopped; Stop/Restart running. Save-and-restart requires known state before writes; plain save remains available.

Typed lifecycle actions share two minutes across steps, separate from ten-second query/two-second discovery; parent deadlines/cancel apply. macOS Start uses /usr/bin/open -g -b com.docker.docker then bounded endpoint polling; Restart stops first under that deadline. Other platforms/Stop use official CLI. LaunchServices receives only identity/home/PATH/temp/shell/locale/timezone/proxy/certificates, excluding Redeven metadata, Electron/Node controls, CLI overrides and secrets. Explicit empty env stays empty; CLI/probes retain theirs. Launch acceptance is not success; reload final state while locked. Never elevate, sudo/pkexec/polkit, alter groups/socket permissions.

Read-gated GET /_redeven_proxy/api/container-resources/services exposes mode/source IDs; one failure cannot hide another. Migration maps legacy state→engine and client_proxy→docker_cli.

## Interaction

One preflight confirmation shows service name, localized risks/impact counts and action; no retyped name/extra review. Client binds name; server checks identity/authority/request+plan hashes. Cancel creates no operation; duplicates stay locked. Hide hashes/raw prose; history resolves names/localized errors.

Settings entry warns. Header aligns outlined square Back/title independently of description; narrow target≥44px. Refresh retains cards, animates only indicator and uses inline errors. Known Desktop/unknown health retains disabled Start/guidance; revalidation enables it. Active divider section replaces normal controls with elapsed/cancel/secondary history. Failure exposes recovery/revalidation. History never auto-opens; unmeasured work has no percent. SSE/poll completion reloads service/runtime facts.

Observed health leads; active work retains locks/feedback. Terminal start/restart failure leaves card on running; stop failure leaves on stopped. Unknown/config failures retain recovery; completed/cancelled records stay in history. Current running never rewrites restart result. History keeps original result/error/duration apart from current state, no empty errors or historical time as live progress.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Admission and serialization
The operation key contains engine, opaque endpoint ID, resource kind, and canonical identity.

Reusing a request ID with different hashes produces an idempotency conflict instead of a second operation.

## Execution, cancellation, and events
The service owns an operation context from queued state through reconciliation. Cancellation is an explicit API action; closing Activity, Workbench, an inspector, an event stream, or the browser never implies cancellation.

Terminal errors use a small public taxonomy for storage, registry availability, rate limiting, not-found, and access denial; the drawer maps known codes to localized guidance alongside the durable timeline. Unknown codes use a localized generic failure; codes and backend messages remain diagnostic evidence, not visible UI copy. Timeout guidance acknowledges that host work may still be in progress. Desktop service cards direct users to its native application for setup/startup recovery and expose status revalidation. Service history shows state transitions without generic execution stages or a synthetic percentage bar.

## Authoritative terminal observation
After engine execution returns, the service reloads the exact endpoint-bound resource or relevant bounded inventory.

The operation is never replayed, regardless of whether the resource appears present or absent.

## UI observation
Inventory requests and streams are fenced by source runtime, endpoint, resource view, and request generation. A superseded response cannot replace current data.

Mobile and desktop expose the same state and cancellation authority. Service lifecycle feedback stays on its card; history is secondary. Polling terminal transitions refresh authoritative service/runtime facts even when the event stream was lost. The portaled history drawer owns its responsive container and independent scrolling. Desktop uses a history sidebar; narrow drawers place a horizontal history strip above details. Rows use stable operation IDs and pressed selection; polling preserves focus and detail nodes. Details separate identity, live cancellation, duration/current health and timeline. The active final timeline step uses a pending indicator, never a completed check.
