File preview defaults to the main surface. Chunked history remains one atomic snapshot with canonical dimensions. Compound controls use Floe CSS.

## Terminal workspace placement

Published SplitWorkspace owns splits, presets, docking, swaps and accessible resizing. Splitting creates a backend view; later placement edits update it. Users manage independent named views through thumbnails, rename/delete and creation above Directories.

Each session has at most one owning view. Selecting a member activates its owner and focuses the pane, including from another view or standalone session. Unowned sessions display alone. Cross-view dragging moves membership atomically and leaves the source slot vacant. Pane and sidebar close buttons terminate the named session; they never delete a view or collapse its geometry. Only the view action deletes a view, releasing its sessions without closing them. New views create fresh sessions. Layout selection only rearranges the current saved view: it preserves all members (including temporarily unavailable sessions), visual reading order and focus. Only published presets matching its slot count are offered; standalone, single-pane and larger custom views disable that menu. Adding sessions requires explicit splitting, dragging or creation in a vacant slot. Explicit splitting uses the target group and verified local cwd or group startup directory. Group membership and cwd remain independent.

Desktop starts at pane headers, with preference-controlled Workbench activity indicators. Its footer retains presets, search, clear, settings and creation. Groups retain scoped creation; overlays keep toolbar/drawer controls.

Split creation/attachment never covers existing panes with global loading. Environment/view changes fence async placement. Mobile shows active-pane tabs without rewriting desktop trees. There is no pane-maximize mode; Alt+Shift+Left/Right cycles panes.

Pane chrome follows terminal foreground/background, never ANSI blue; sidebar follows shell tokens. Compact 14px session tiles use fine contrasting borders and subtle theme-neutral fills; pane headers are 28px high. Rename opens with the existing name focused and selected through Floe overlay autofocus. Idle hover uses pointer; only active drags show grabbing. Sidebar close appears on hover/focus and stays available on touch. Placement previews use terminal foreground borders with background isolation and a contrasting fill. Shared geometry notices are absent.

## View projection

One environment provider batches affected source/destination views in revision-checked atomic saves. Edits survive acknowledgment; conflicts retain drafts for explicit reload/discard. One lifecycle resets scope/access before loading; unchanged permissions preserve readiness/drafts, and retired connections cannot publish. Layout edits wait for readiness.

Active view stays local per panel. Legacy v1 local splits import unowned members once and clear after backend acknowledgment. Missing sessions render as vacant slots without pruning saved geometry. Closure persists fresh vacant identities; even an entirely vacant view remains selected. Each vacancy offers localized session creation and accepts a dragged session into that exact slot. Moving within a view leaves the source vacant. Slot creation shows local progress and recoverable errors; failed close restores the session. Empty-view selection never falls back to an unrelated session. Views do not restart PTYs.

CodeSpace, Web Service and service-template catalog modules own their styles.
Vite loads feature styles with their lazy page chunks. Resource presentation
components import their shared header stylesheet; the root stylesheet does not
duplicate these imports. Every document retains the enforced 122 KiB gzip

implementation or suppress model output to keep input responsive.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## One session and one request path
Product subscriptions call the Shell-bound session event reader. Floe Webapp's acquisition lifecycle opens a logical HTTP stream on the current Flowersec session and parses SSE with its shared bounded parser.

Session multiplexing removes those event requests from the browser HTTP pool; changing request priority alone cannot do so.

## Authority and resource lifetime
Local session issuance declares only Env App API and plugin API paths plus the plugin CSRF and expected-management-revision headers. Remote issuers must declare the same plugin request authority and upload cap in their signed scope.

Product code must not reset a successful response while its bytes are still being consumed.

## Observation and recovery
Flower maintains one workspace stream; thread selection never reconnects it.

Its transport and cancellation regression coverage remain intact.

Carrier failure clears the cached proxy runtime.

HTTPS or a trustworthy local origin is still required where the browser restricts those APIs; product code does not mark an insecure network origin as trustworthy.

concepts.title: Cross-platform host application behavior
concepts.summary: Viewing, sharing, closing windows and ending processes are distinct on every OS. Ordinary actions preserve unsaved work and app cancellation; only confirmed Force quit bypasses saving. Backend facts drive supported controls. Session/display policy remains authoritative and unavailable recovery cannot silently relaunch.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
| Operation | macOS | Linux |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Close outer Desktop window / browser popup | Release this client lease; app survives | Same |
| Network loss, reload, second viewer | Reconnect same live app; stale input is revoked | Same |
| Release this client lease | End this capture/route; other clients and app survive | End this proxy/route; other clients and app survive |
| No window for more than 40 seconds | Waiting, with native menu/reopen | Waiting, reconnect same process without relaunch |
| Close last window | Viewer closes; app decides whether its process exits | Same |
| Cancel normal close/quit | Preserve application and save dialog | Same; ordinary control is Close all windows |
| Explicit Force quit in library | Confirm loss warning; exact AppKit instance | Confirm loss warning; exact owned backend and descendants |
| Orderly Runtime shutdown or process exit | Native app remains discoverable | Private display survives; new Runtime verifies/reconnects it |
| Running list | Regular apps in the logged-in OS session | Caller-owned Redeven instances, including detached/windowless apps |
| Host reboot / display server destruction / OS cleanup | No survival guarantee | Same; Runtime cgroup cleanup may also end its virtual display |

## Accepted operations and visible state
Quit and force-quit requests are asynchronous. The Host Applications surface must close the confirmation dialog after acceptance and show a per-application pending state until the authoritative running snapshot confirms the target instance is gone.

The first Force quit action only enters that state; only its final confirmation sends the destructive host request.

Neither backend can preserve an application after its OS or display environment has been destroyed.

## Waiting and process lifetime
A running process without its first shareable window remains attached indefinitely; there is no first-window termination deadline. Releasing the current client lease during this wait ends that sharing lease normally; missing pixels do not turn a lease release into a launch failure. An unexpected helper exit is a failed sharing session, not evidence that the host application ended.

## Window evidence
The window registry distinguishes present, unknown and confirmed-empty inventories. No first-window deadline is introduced.

## Capture and recovery
Capture availability is independent of lifetime. AX identity survives a capture-surface replacement while the input generation is renewed; retired callbacks cannot update the replacement. Failure to launch and unexpected helper loss remain failures; missing pixels do not change a confirmed process exit into a failed launch.

## Terminal state
Terminal state retains the native end reason: `application_exited` confirms the bound process exited, `windows_closed` confirms its last shared window closed, and `sharing_stopped` confirms detachment. Closing windows and stopping sharing never claim the process has quit. The [lifecycle validation matrix](../operations/host-application-lifecycle.md) separates automated recovery evidence from OS/application compatibility limits.

concepts.title: Plugin background entries
concepts.summary: ReDevPlugin owns headless Worker lifecycle and durable intervals. Redeven supplies environment permission policy and presents verified status through ordinary plugin management. No hidden surface, host scheduler, replay endpoint or second Worker protocol is involved.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
A plugin may declare runtime_start, on_demand or interval. The first two use the platform background manager: starts are idempotent, scoped to the installed instance and environment, and independent of visible Activity or Workbench surfaces. Interval requires background.method.v1 and background.interval.v1, an explicit method and parameters, an environment-scoped job Worker, synchronous execution, no confirmation or preflight, a 1,000–86,400,000 ms period, and a 1–300,000 ms execution budget not exceeding the period.

The platform persists and claims each due invocation before dispatch. One instance runs at most one interval invocation; separate plugins remain independent. The first run waits one period, then each next run follows completion plus the period. Missed periods coalesce. Restart preserves completed plans; an unfinished claim becomes unknown and is never replayed. A later period is new work, not proof of the earlier result. Disable, uninstall, package replacement and revocation fence and cancel exact current work. Host close drains execution before closing state. ReDevPlugin owns contiguous control-store migration and unknown-outcome handling.

Redeven's background policy snapshots the validated runtime LocalMax intersected with the Env App application cap, then applies the existing method-effect rules. It does not depend on an online session, borrow a user's cached authority, or apply a per-user override to an environment-owned job. Admin and unknown effects are denied. The platform separately verifies owner, installed package trust, current grants, revisions, runtime admission and the durable claim. This policy grants no filesystem, process, secret or network resource: adapters requiring a live user session continue to reject background access. Selected-file and connection approvals retain their existing lifetime and owner rules.

An explicit install/enable action authorizes the declared environment lifecycle through the ordinary product review and platform APIs. Permission removal blocks future dispatch without changing the user's enabled intent. The existing disable action stops work. No separate scheduling switch is introduced.

sections.title: Presentation
sections.body: Installation review shows the localized cadence for interval entries. Method identity, exact period and execution budget remain inside existing expandable technical details. Installed details consume the authoritative background_interval projection: scheduled, running, stopped or blocked, with next-run time only while scheduled. A prior failed or unknown result remains visible without a retry button that could replay effects. A previous background diagnostic cannot override current interval status; separate process diagnostics remain available. Refresh uses the existing owner-scoped inventory path.

## Ownership and isolation
Every session binds plugin instance, user scope, environment scope, plugin invocation/session, and client key. Start requests contain an executable and argv array; ReDevPlugin never parses an implicit shell command string.

Secret references are resolved by the Host adapter and values do not cross the UI, error, audit, or diagnostic projections.

For one owner and client key, ReDevPlugin reuses only a field-equal launch request. Redeven delegates this decision to the platform.

## Streams and lifecycle
The first contract supports non-PTY stdin, stdout, and stderr only. Each output stream has an independent cursor and bounded ring buffer.

The platform removes the session after close and prevents access after owner revocation.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
- Upstream owns validation/hashes/trust, inspection and registry state, permission/confirmation, tokens/assets, sandbox/bridge, settings/intents, Executions/Events, storage/network/secret brokers, supervision/IPC/WASM, quotas/revocation, control storage, generated clients/errors/schemas and release metadata.
- Go/npm/runtime/machine artifacts form one coordinated release; frontend cannot downgrade independently. Current pins live in manifests and are checked by the dependency-contract test.
- Local bootstrap keeps its bounded credential admission before session readiness. [Package lifecycle](redevplugin-package-lifecycle.md) owns inspection/install/cache/readiness; [Redeven adapters](redevplugin-redeven-adapters.md) owns host modules and presentation.

## Product availability

Plugin subsystem readiness is never a prerequisite for Runtime readiness or
ordinary host sessions. A plugin market, package, runtime, storage or initialization
failure is diagnosed locally and leaves files, terminals, Notes, Workbench and
other non-plugin services available. An unavailable subsystem exposes the released
`PLUGIN_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE` failure without dispatching plugin effects; rejected
mutation requests report `not_committed`. Plugin Center localizes the failure
inside its own view rather than replacing the product shell. The launcher never
claims an unreadable inventory is empty, and automatic subsystem failure does not
interrupt unrelated work with a global toast. Initialization has a ten-second
budget; cancellation rejects late results and closes any acquired integration.
Caller-owned construction resources unwind on errors and recovered initialization
panics. This boundary does not mask cancellation of the host's own startup.

Host channel authentication and plugin execution admission are separate facts.
A failed or panicked plugin generation binding grants no plugin authority and cannot close
the host channel. Plugin request panics release their admission while the HTTP
server contains the request failure. Platform storage remains opaque: isolation
must not delete, rewrite or silently reauthorize incompatible plugin state.

## Host network policy

ReDevPlugin 3.12.0 separates host-selected routing from package verification and
plugin network authority. Redeven supplies single-hop transports for market,
package and release-document downloads. They follow explicit environment proxy
settings, current macOS system proxy/PAC configuration, and OS DNS/VPN routing.
VPN synthetic addresses, enterprise DNS and private package sources are not
rejected merely for belonging to a non-public address range. The platform still
validates each URL and redirect, exact allowed release origins, byte limits,
cancellation, hashes and signatures. Downloads do not grant plugin execution.

For granted HTTPS hostname connectors without explicit private-prefix binding,
Redeven registers the released transport factory. The platform checks target,
method, grant and revision before dispatch, and owns pool identity, quota and
revocation. Explicit private-prefix connections, literal addresses and other
protocols retain their released address-bound contract. Network configuration
resolution happens only during requests, never during Runtime construction.
Failures remain inside the plugin boundary.

## Retained package history

ReDevPlugin 3.11.2 owns the bounded read-only projection of signed pre-Web v9
installation records and version history. Normal migration retains their exact
canonical manifests, hashes, signature facts and data generations. Their current
Host action state is incompatible; they are manageable but cannot execute or be
enabled. A user may explicitly update the same installation to a current Web
package without deleting its history. No VNode renderer or fabricated Web
declaration exists. Redeven consumes released inventory and action state without
parsing or rewriting platform-owned records. Unknown or corrupt state remains
unchanged and unavailable only within the plugin boundary.

## Ordinary Web surfaces

The released platform owns Web application admission, package-local ES module assets, sandbox bootstrap and the authenticated surface bridge. Redeven supplies an origin-allocation adapter and mounts the released Web surface handler. It does not translate DOM events or render a platform-specific VNode tree. Each surface receives an independent origin; parent credentials never become ambient authority inside that origin.

Plugin data conversion and exact historical data binding remain released Host responsibilities. Redeven displays verified review evidence and calls the existing update APIs; it does not interpret converter code, copy generations, migrate the platform database, or retry uncertain writes.

Durable interval scheduling, claim fencing, restart recovery and unknown-outcome handling remain ReDevPlugin responsibilities. Redeven registers an environment/app permission-cap adapter and renders the released summary and inventory status. It does not retain a user session for background authority, implement timers, or access platform scheduling tables.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Package sources and lifecycle
Production obtains catalog entries from the validated latest-only market snapshot. Publisher, plugin, version, hashes, signatures, revocation evidence, source policy, and Host requirements must match before ReDevPlugin changes the registry.

A GitHub source without an administrator-entered tag resolves the latest eligible Release on each new inspection; the previously resolved release tag is evidence, not a new durable user pin.

## Retained plugin data

ReDevPlugin 3.9 owns target-filtered discovery, exact inspection, one-shot recovery commit and read-only reconciliation. The source is an uninstalled instance with compatible retained data; the target must be explicitly disabled. The Host verifies owner, publisher, plugin identity, data shape, generation, management revision and active fingerprint. Its atomic transaction swaps data references while retaining both generations. It does not restore grants, secrets or enabled state.

Redeven passes published SDK DTOs unchanged. Discovery, inspection and status require environment read permission; commit requires write permission; disabling remains an admin action. An uncertain commit is never replayed. Reconciliation uses the exact inspected plan; a confirmed pending result permits a new explicit review, while unknown status remains read-only. Host restart recovery remains upstream-owned.

## Plugin data upgrades

ReDevPlugin 3.10 owns package-declared conversion, isolated input/output generations, quotas, cancellation, and the atomic package/data/history transaction. A converter matches an exact predecessor version and data shape. Failed or cancelled conversion keeps the old package and data; committed or unknown outcomes use the existing update reconciliation path and never trigger automatic replay. Downgrade restores the exact historical package's last data generation. The platform migrates its control store before opening it; Redeven never reads or writes that schema.

Redeven consumes the verified data-upgrade declaration from the released security summary. Review presents one concise saved-data notice before approval; method, predecessor identities and resource limits remain in expandable package details. Added, changed and removed declarations use the existing security-difference projection. Review omits empty release-note placeholders and generic instructions; inspection-binding facts stay inside expandable evidence, and unchanged permission grants appear only once. No second migration wizard, converter dispatcher, durable job or product-owned data copy is introduced.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Host modules and external packages
Redeven constructs the released Host with explicit core, official-release, runtime, connectivity, secrets, capability, and external-package modules. Redeven supplies session, authorization, web-security, trust, official release-source, observability, secret, external source, and business adapters; it never edits registry, inspection, token, lease, revoke-epoch, or plugin-data state directly.

The official signed-release module remains the stricter release-ref path.

## Network adapter

The product-owned hostnetwork package implements current host routing without
network I/O in its constructor. HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY use explicit
upper/lowercase environment settings, including explicit empty values for direct
routing; NO_PROXY is evaluated with the standard hostname/IP/CIDR matcher. On
macOS, requests without applicable environment policy use CFNetwork system
settings and bounded cancellable PAC resolution. Linux uses environment proxies
or normal OS routing. Remote Runtimes use their own host network environment.

The adapter respects the ordered configured routes. A bodyless GET/HEAD may try
the next configured route only after a dial failure before an application
connection exists. It never invents a direct fallback. TLS, protocol and unknown
outcome errors do not change routes. Writes use fresh HTTP/1 connections and are
not automatically replayed, including when the application supplies an idempotency
header. Read and write requests share a bounded eight-request limit per transport;
read pools retain at most two idle connections per origin for thirty seconds.

Market services own their default transport. The plugin integration closes its
caller-owned package transport on failure or shutdown. Each granted connector
receives an independent transport managed by the upstream pool lifecycle. TLS
verification and system trust roots remain enabled; proxy credentials stay on the
proxy hop and never become origin or plugin credentials.

## Surfaces and interaction ownership
The product Shell owns one released `PluginPlatformClient`, authenticated transport, and shared surface scope.

The application-method receiver (`surface.methods`) uses the same read authorization as opening and preparing its surface. Redeven uses them for host placement behavior, never as identity, authorization, or permission evidence.

A recovery presentation may explain or retry the Host snapshot, but it is not a second open gate and owns no catch-up identity state machine.

Redeven derives a plugin origin only from a trusted product entry origin and the released surface origin key. Local UI and AppServer route child requests to the released Web surface handler after removing parent credentials. Ordinary HTTP loopback Local UI uses the same isolated resource handler as

on the exact listener port. This is a resource route, not an additional public
management authority or a private-bridge fallback.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Env App inventory and permissions
Env App owns one authenticated fetch adapter, one released client, one shared scope, and one placement coordinator. Every mutation carries its current management and applicable policy/revoke revisions; committed and unknown management outcomes rely on Host revocation followed by the SDK's scope teardown, then refresh state without a second slot-close path or blind mutation retry.

Generic review and confirmation copy names the exact permission id instead of substituting an official-plugin label.

## External lifecycle changes

Each surface's first terminal error refreshes the shared owner-scoped inventory
once. It does not replay an execution or automatically retry the same revision.
A user retry retires the failed slot, awaits an authoritative inventory read,
and opens only while the original component and authenticated owner remain
current. Failed reads never authorize reopening from a cached revision.

The product container's keyed lease owns replacement when management revision
or generation changes. The retired component cannot open a duplicate slot after
that replacement. Disabled plugins remain disabled; their explicit Enable
action first refreshes inventory and writes only if the current instance is
still disabled, using its current revision. If another client already enabled
it, the refreshed inventory restores the container without a second mutation.

Workbench and Activity use the same refresh callback. Shared inventory updates
Plugin Center as well as surface placement; refresh does not remove layout,
replay Agent/file writes, or revoke sibling surfaces. A failed inventory read
retains a healthy cached lease; it is not evidence of revocation. The failed
surface still requires a successful authoritative read before retrying.
The projection reads the resource's latest owner-bound snapshot during refresh
so background inventory requests never suspend and detach the Workbench DOM.
Detaching an iframe would reload its already-consumed entry ticket and destroy
otherwise valid sibling application state.

Visibility and theme/context delivery can race with SDK retirement or document
navigation. A synchronous delivery failure enters the same first-error path
for that exact slot, refreshes inventory once, and retires through the SDK. It
must not escape into the Workbench error boundary or close sibling placements.

## Installation-bound runtime recovery

Startup recovery results describe the exact Host-checked installation: instance
ID, active fingerprint, installation timestamp, and management revision. The
released SDK compares that identity with the current enabled inventory record.
Env App preserves those fields in both official and external inventory projections
and displays only matching observations. Updates, reinstalls, disabling, and
uninstalling invalidate an old observation without deriving readiness or starting
another recovery pass. A current failure on a sibling installation stays visible.

Explicit retry loading, success, failure, and rejected requests remain bound to
the installation and authenticated session captured when retry began. A delayed
response cannot overwrite a replacement installation. Product copy localizes the
released reason code; a catalog instance ID or a raw unknown code is not the
user-facing failure message. Inventory action state remains the launch authority.

## User close and forced revocation

When a narrow Plugin Center replaces a card with details to confirm uninstall,
dismissal returns focus to the surviving detail heading after modal presence
ends. The hidden card trigger is no longer a valid return destination.

User close requests use the released surface request-close contract. A plugin may report unsaved work; Redeven presents one localized Floe confirmation and preserves the slot if canceled. Forced lifecycle invalidation still revokes without waiting for user consent. A successful request-close is recorded as already closed so subsequent placement disposal cannot send a second close.

Management teardown may preserve the product layout while the SDK clears the document to `about:blank`, removes same-origin authority and closes the bridge. An iframe remaining in the layout is not evidence of retained application authority; a fresh authorized slot is required before reopening.

`/_redeven_proxy/api/remote-desktop` is independent from application launch. Every session and forward belongs to the authenticated user; renderer-supplied identity never authorizes a route.

The same policy fences new admission under the manager lock, so an HTTP request authorized before revocation cannot recreate the removed desktop.

## Platform boundary
macOS uses the exact remote Swift package in the existing Runtime helper.

The canonical official Alpine source remains the final fallback; every download still checks the expected size and SHA-256 before atomic cache publication, and a failed archive download can move to the next trusted source.

Capability normalization also applies to a retried connection after accepting or declining takeover, so a removed display cannot return through the stored request.

## Media and office interaction
Control and media travel through separate Flowersec native proxy streams bound to the same product attachment. Cancellation retires the selection and releases held keys; lock-screen input cannot use that text path.

Native session and frame authority remain governed by this concept.

Compatibility epoch 35 requires both Desktop and Runtime to understand explicit reasoning `on` alongside the existing default, off, effort, and budget choices. Epoch 59 pairs Runtime authorization requests with the shared Desktop and Env App OpenAI account picker. Epoch 65 requires the model directory's backend-owned default_fetch_source field in provider search policies. See [model web search](../ai/model-web-search.md).

concepts.title: Web Service management recovery
concepts.summary: Registry owns lifecycle records/transactions; Manager observes resources and available actions; Renderer presents current state, last result and next step. Unavailable inspection is not absence; historical failure is not current state. Destruction requires fresh ownership/explicit cleanup. Authorized detach works with an offline engine but preserves resources and claims no process stop.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Facts and actions
`ServiceFacts` separates presence, ownership, runtime state, inspection completeness, resource references, and check time.

Frontend code never substitutes Retry or Restart for unavailable Start.

A failed Host maintenance hook may be bypassed only through an administrator's reviewed plan, and only for verified resources.

## Review and execution
`GET /managed-web-services/{id}/inspection` requires read permission, is non-cacheable, and uses the same factual backend projection as the list.

Existing unrelated lifecycle transactions cannot be overwritten by recovery.

Instance-scoped allocation and legacy resource boundaries are owned by [Service resource ownership](service-resource-ownership.md).

## Uninstall transaction
Uninstall uses `runtime_manifest_json`, the existing operation coordinator, and the existing event stream.

A resource recreated under the same name cannot acquire the previous deletion authorization.

Detachment remains available while it is unresolved.

## Management archives and access
Registry version 4 adds `active`, `detached`, and `uninstalled`. Only active records participate in template uniqueness and must own an authorized Forward.

Names, ports, or cached reachability never prove ownership.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: The contiguous `portforward_registry_v2` 3-to-4 migration preserves bindings, configuration, private-file references, operation history, and existing resource locations. Failed migration rolls back completely; unknown versions and structural drift remain read-only failures. Desktop/Runtime compatibility epoch 15 covers these management contracts.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Identity and version matrix
Current authors use `redeven-service-template.json` with fixed `kind: "redeven.service-template"`, source `schema_version: 4`, author `template_id`, `service_family_id`, positive `revision`, `default_locale`, and `locales`, followed by the full display and execution declaration.

| Entrypoint | Source document | Execution input | Effective execution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `template.json` | 1 | TemplateSpec 3 | TemplateSpec 7 |
| `template.json` | 2 | TemplateSpec 4, 5, or 6 | TemplateSpec 7 |
| `redeven-service-template.json` | 3 | TemplateSpec 6 | TemplateSpec 7 |
| `redeven-service-template.json` | 4 | TemplateSpec 7 | TemplateSpec 7 |

The branded filename requires the branded document.

## Adaptation and execution ownership
The reader strictly decodes the historical document, applies consecutive data transformations, validates current TemplateSpec and passive resources, then returns the current typed definition. Historical syntax never grants extra privileges.

The npm SDK publishes the corresponding types, schemas, and GitHub acquisition contract; it does not execute services or migrate databases.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:

[Database migrations](database-schema-migrations.md) retain their exact lineage, shape checks, rollback, and read-only rejection rules.

concepts.title: Tessiven canvas contract
concepts.summary:
Tessiven is the Runtime-owned library of immutable service canvases. Each
canvas stores a complete `redeven.io/tessiven/v1.1.0` YAML document and every save
creates a new version. The Runtime is the single owner of canvas data; the
Desktop Welcome surface and the local Env App render that same library. A
failed validation or version conflict leaves the last saved document intact.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
- A canvas document contains stable IDs for Runtime nodes, visual groups,   business services, instances, external resources, relations, and evidence. - Every service has at least one instance on an existing node. A missing   placement fails validate/save at the service ID with a source location. - A service kind describes its primary responsibility independently of its   product name, instance role or deployment format. The [DSL versioning contract](tessiven-dsl-versioning.md)   owns version selection, read projections and write upgrades.

The `tessiven_canvas_library` SQLite lineage starts at schema v1. Canvas identities, archive state, immutable YAML versions, and idempotent request results remain intact.

A fresh v2 library and an upgraded v1 library must both reopen successfully.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: The local Runtime owns the SQLite canvas library and immutable version documents. Canvas references never authorize resource actions; the [Flower and operations contract](../ai/tessiven-flower-and-operations.md) owns that boundary. Tessiven does not deploy services, discover targets in the background, or synchronize libraries between devices.

sections.title: Contract

## Read And Negotiation
Under `/_redeven_proxy/api/tessiven`, `GET /presentation-contract` returns `formats` and `capabilities`. Unknown well-formed capabilities are ignored rather than treated as authority.

The initial optional `group_layouts` capability enables authored group packing; without it automatic layout preserves the same memberships and relationships.

## Compatibility And Authority
The frozen schema is independent of the DSL registry. Existing display meanings must not change in place.

Resource requests continue to read the original version, check exact bindings and enforce current permissions.

concepts.summary: Runtime owns schema selection and explicit v1→v1.0.0→v1.1.0 migrations. New documents use redeven.io/tessiven/v1.1.0; each edge changes only its version scalar, preserving legacy automatic layout. sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Version Identities And Releases
DSL identities use stable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` strings, for example `v1.2.3`.

Paths must be unique, acyclic and complete, with source validation, target validation and semantic checks. Do not introduce a schema-only registry entry without its executable migration and fixtures.

## Read Compatibility
Validation selects the exact source schema, applies the explicit upgrade chain, and validates the current shape and cross-object contracts. Returned `document` is canonical current data.

The [canvas contract](tessiven-canvas-contract.md) owns those semantic rules.

Native rendering uses the independently frozen [canvas presentation contract](tessiven-canvas-presentation.md), not the current DSL identity. Every DSL release must verify its explicit mapping to the oldest supported display contract without rewriting source or granting resource authority.

Ordinary edits valid in the original schema continue to upgrade automatically; no historical YAML is rewritten.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
## New Snapshots And Failure Boundary
Creation, imports, full save and exact edits write the current DSL. Existing history is never bulk-rewritten.

The [canvas storage contract](tessiven-canvas-contract.md) continues to own atomic startup database upgrades independently.

concepts.title: Independent Web Environment Center
concepts.summary: Desktop combines an environment center with its existing local Runtime lifecycle. Web Center deploys independently; Runtime never requires Center or Desktop to start. Both hosts share Contracts/Core/Controller/UI. Web Center has one administrator, with no registration, users, roles, organizations or user ACL service.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Shared behavior and host ownership
Shared desktop/src/envcenter owns routes/search/filter/recovery/order/cancellation/Gateway lists. Desktop adapter calls existing lifecycle/windows; Web calls Center HTTP/browser tabs. Shared code imports neither Electron/Node filesystem nor Web auth. Desktop never contacts Center or changes Welcome/navigation/preparation/shutdown. Config/secrets do not sync. cmd/center-contracts generates exact DTO/TS/schema bounds.

Labels/hostnames grant no trust. Revisions/sequences fence observations; late completion cannot navigate canceled pending tabs or cancel open route owners. Refresh reads authority, not new intent.

## Server entry
Portal, Env and each child use distinct HTTPS origins under one registrable domain/port with matching TLS. Bookmarks are direct. Clipboard denial/absence retains descriptor/manual localized selection; announce success only after actual write.

Center pairs as access-only Gateway after fingerprint confirmation. Runtime independently persists consent through redeven web-binding apply --stdin --yes, binding RuntimeID/origin/clientSPKI/scope/revision. Published Flowersec mutually authenticated TLS1.3 pins signed Runtime service; no inbound app TCP listener.

Operations bind device/route. Browser nonce/exact origins/bounded redemption/single-use code complete handoff; response-loss same-request retry recovers one outcome. Host-only cookies never replace Runtime password/MFA. Logout/security/source/route revocation cancels derived admissions/streams.

## Runtime and child applications
webbinding owns consent, webconnector pinned TLS, environmentcenter admin/directory/proxy. Deployment requires separate stateless Connector via Unix socket with exact peer UID before credentials. Worker holds admitted route credentials only; Center retains admin/factors/master key. Direct adapter is test-only, never deployment fallback.

Control connection owns worker lease; Center loss/logout/revocation closes all streams. Connector restart loses leases; next request requires fresh valid admission. Never replay business HTTP. Systemd/Compose use distinct unprivileged identities; Connector cannot read Center state/TLS keys. IPC preserves bounded permission/capacity/compatibility/offline codes; Runtime payloads cannot invent worker errors. Published controller retries only explicit transient Gateway admission conflicts; invalid/denied/revoked proofs terminate.

Services/editor/graphical viewers use resource origins; trusted proxy retains parent credentials. Editor pins running instance. Graphical access requires scoped Flowersec. Child framing follows authenticated Runtime policy for editor workers; Portal denies framing.

## Plugin application origins
Authenticated parent operations prepare/revoke origins under shared pending/active capacity. Duplicate pending origin is busy; failed/canceled probes release reservation. DELETE fences pending work so late probes cannot revive/replace generations. Each child binds parent route/Runtime admission and cannot call management APIs. Gateway certificates/CONNECT enforce exact namespace/target. Desktop credentials attach only to trusted parent frame.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Center is trusted with plaintext application traffic. This is not browser-to-Runtime encryption against Center. Forwarded headers, loopback, SSH tunnels and browser-supplied headers cannot create management authority.

Web v1 does not implement Desktop SSH/WSL/local preparation, Cloud aggregation or local account/model delegation. Existing Desktop capabilities retain their owners. Remote terminal/files/Git/monitoring/container/Flower and graphical capabilities retain ordinary Runtime permissions and platform conditions.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Collection
Header, launcher, toolbar, and collection share a centered axis.

Rows have a 64px minimum, never a fixed height.

The bounded status cell isolates asynchronous progress and explanatory feedback from neighboring rows under the [layout stability contract](../ui/asynchronous-layout-stability.md).

## Opening restrictions
When Open is unavailable and the backend selects an executable Start action, Start uses the primary button style within existing management permissions.

Long explanations wrap inside the visible boundary in either theme.

## Review and focus
One overlay drawer contains a concise service conclusion, compact resource facts, and recommended actions. A newer known inventory check may replace older inspection facts; unknown checks preserve the last known facts.

Older or unknown targets retain the stop-first flow and require a second explicit update after stopping; an initially stopped service remains stopped after update.

sections.body:

Specific entrance errors remain readable; failed Open never prevents another attempt.

The shell retains only collection and loading-presentation styles; management and version-review styles load with the product page rather than the initial document graph.

concepts.title: Native Desktop CodeSpace access
concepts.summary: Desktop owns each CodeSpace window, browser profile, protected loopback listener and selected route. Runtime owns editor generation, permissions and AccessGate. Editors use native HTTP/WebSockets without privileged preload or transport injection. Closing a window, revoking access or stopping an instance ends its connections. Route failure and occupied saved ports fail visibly without transport substitution or request replay.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
- Only the trusted environment root submits `loading`/`open` with a DNS-safe CodeSpace ID. [Window status surfaces](../ui/window-status-surfaces.md) owns presentation.
- One window owner controls loading, navigation, readiness and cleanup. Theme refresh never focuses it. Navigation and route failures use separate localized diagnostics without credentials, raw exceptions or error URLs.
- Profiles hash stable environment/resource identity, including control-plane/user identity where applicable. An occupied port never causes contact with its occupant or a replacement profile origin. External navigation uses the system browser.
- Native/placement sessions reuse their private Local UI bridge and token. No extra Runtime, SSH forward, public Local UI fallback or certificate bypass is allowed. Passwords remain ephemeral, outside editor storage, URLs and logs.
- Descriptors resolve only running CodeSpaces and return the generation and Runtime-owned `access_cookie_name`; full effective read/write/execute permissions and AccessGate are required. Flowersec owns HTTP/Duplex adaptation. Redeven owns routing/authorization and never replays requests or terminal input.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Compatibility remains defined by the current protocol and published manifests, not historical dependency pins. Electron qualification covers document handoff, readiness, redirects, Workers, Service Workers, WebSockets and unauthenticated rejection. HTTP tests cover generation, authorization, bytes, upgrades, cookies and origin conflicts.

Descriptor acquisition uses the real environment Electron session and its [private bridge request policy](../security/plugin-platform-integration-security.md), including the global request hook. A mocked `fetch` or raw socket route alone cannot qualify this boundary.

sections.body:
## Resource intent and route ownership
After starting the selected CodeSpace, Env App submits `mode: browser` and its CodeSpace ID through the same root-frame-only IPC used for built-in editor windows.

The system browser never receives a private Local UI `/cs/<id>` URL, an environment credential, or a raw gateway header.

Runtime accepts only this shaped loopback origin or the built-in numeric-loopback origin as presentation metadata; that metadata never selects an upstream dial target.

## One-time entry and browser session
Only main can mint an entry from the gateway object.

Runtime and editor traffic never carries the browser cookie; upstream responses cannot set the reserved cookie name.

An OS-open failure closes the newly acquired gateway and route.

sections.body:

No upstream package, public listener, SSH forwarding process, editor injection, or Web Service authorization change is required.

concepts.title: Desktop development sessions and bundles
concepts.summary:
- Authority: launcher owns Desktop, local Runtime, saved Gateways and bundles.
- Outcome: run current source, stop together, prune old bundles.
- Invariants: preserve data, identities, unrelated services and recent/selected/live bundles.
- Failure: preparation cleans up; incomplete inventory prevents pruning.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Source and build identity
scripts/dev_desktop.sh captures HEAD and tracked/nonignored source; mutation fails. Generated OKF/ignored assets are outputs; authored OKF/builders/Go embeds are inputs. Reuse requires identical source, dependencies, tools, target/settings and verified Desktop/immutable Runtime bytes. Missing/corrupt/incomplete output rebuilds; failure never launches old bundles. Only pinned Rust installation may change tools. --rebuild forces build; REDEVEN_AGENT_FORCE_INSTALL=1 reinstalls all three JS packages once. Manifests select pnpm/npm and their locks, not compatibility-lock installers.

## Network and caches
macOS preparation reads enabled static HTTP/HTTPS system proxies once. Any explicit HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY (including lowercase/empty) or REDEVEN_DEV_SYSTEM_PROXY=0 disables discovery. Preserve explicit NO_PROXY, otherwise add loopback/compatible exclusions. PAC/SOCKS-only needs explicit policy. Never log credentials or weaken TLS/artifact checks. Remove only inferred variables before launching services.

Official Node checksum/archive transfers each get three attempts, 1/2-second backoff for transport or HTTP 408/429/500/502/503/504; permanent HTTP/certificate errors stop. Separate CONNECT/origin status from bytes. Retry the same official URL/policy; resume only this build's partial archive, verify complete checksum, delete failed partials. Cached archives still need fresh official checksums.

Development may reuse Cargo registry/target caches but freshly stage exact locked public crates and regenerate verified digest/execution/consumption evidence. Complete caches work offline; incomplete caches acquire explicitly. Corruption/compiler errors cannot switch paths. Release directories remain isolated. Source changes rebuild the whole product, without component/watch mode.

## Scheduling and lifecycle
Desktop compile overlaps Runtime preparation. Runtime assets/Go, plugins and Computer resources own separate outputs. Env App typecheck overlaps bundling under checkout lock. Development builds skip notice freshness; staged/main gates own admission. Sequential release builds check notices after asset tasks. Go waits for embeds; publication waits for complete outputs and unchanged inputs. Three dependency workers overlap probes with serial-equivalent digests/order. Supervisors preserve errors and stop owned descendants on cancellation/failure.

Saved local Gateways reuse intact compatible installs; source changes do not force upgrade. Service owner repairs missing/damaged packages; explicit Update selects current build. Archive cache keys include dirty source; changed inputs discard old cache generation, absent keys create a session cache. Package owner validates archives.

Dev gzip1/Brotli 4 retains identical decoded bytes; normal/release compression stays maximum. Profile is part of identity. Gateway source copies exclude other worktrees/native caches. Log dependency/verification/Desktop/Runtime/Gateway durations. Qualify rebuilt and reused launches with a saved local Gateway, exact Runtime commit and cleanup; empty-profile warm measurements alone are insufficient.

Exit/preparation failure/signals stop only owned services. Electron resolution outputs only its path, logs to stderr, propagates errors and rechecks executable after dependency builds.

## Credentials and retention
Unpackaged development uses AES-256-GCM with a random retained 0600 profile key: plaintext protection, not protection from the same user. Other launches use Electron system storage without constructor probes. Legacy Keychain offers explicit recovery; never read preferences/system secrets implicitly. Each file migrates atomically only after user action. Failure retains credentials/retry/quit; corrupt keys never reset accounts/Runtime/Keychain.

Publish complete bundles under <development-state-root>/desktop/bundles/<manifest-sha256>. Retain newest three, selected/reused and all live bundles. This bounds inactive verified count, not total bytes; active/unverified entries may grow.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Runtime state identity
Each Runtime state directory owns an immutable Ed25519 seed in `access-identity.key`. Invalid or symlinked existing material fails closed and is never replaced.

Existing TLS, Gateway trust and Runtime authentication remain authoritative.

## Observation and grouping
Main-process observations bind an entry ID to its configured connection and verified identity.

Runtime membership summaries use the Gateway pairing fingerprint: SHA-256 of the canonical, trimmed Ed25519 SubjectPublicKeyInfo PEM, encoded as unpadded base64url with `SHA256:`.

Existing registrations, Gateway member and Cloud binding authority remain in their respective stores.

## Explicit default and one-time opening
The existing main Open button uses the saved default. Implicit defaults use stable registration / first-observation order, never probe completion order or a newly rebuilt Gateway catalog timestamp.

[Gateway access sessions](../gateway/gateway-access-sessions.md) owns transport isolation and same-route session reuse.

## Membership discovery and migration
Members are discovered from the signed v6 directory and matched to trusted Runtime membership summaries.

Existing Cloud-only Runtime configurations must rejoin and cannot silently gain the new member delegation. [Gateway Cloud access](../gateway/gateway-cloud-access.md) owns proof-based preservation of a formal environment ID.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Desktop shares host-neutral environment contracts, projection/controller and Gateway list UI with [Web Center](../architecture/web-environment-center.md). Existing lifecycle/window owners and user interactions remain authoritative; no Center login/service dependency is introduced.

This contract owns display association and route selection. Proof observation never upgrades those permissions.

[Gateway Desktop interactions](../gateway/gateway-desktop-interactions.md) owns the explicit environment connection, invitation and confirmation steps and the independent management, invitation and local consent boundaries; recovery reuses the original Runtime lifecycle owner.

Each perspective selects an explicit route without granting authority or falling back. Snapshots retain nodes, selection and focus; owner removal invalidates submission but retains open sessions.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
[Interaction continuity](desktop-interaction-continuity.md) owns authority, drafts, visibility and stale completions. Card controls stay single-line; long progress-panel action labels wrap within their buttons.

## Window actions
All perspectives use **Open window** for unopened environments and **Show window** to focus an existing session. Labels preserve readiness, authority, lifecycle and session ownership.

Settings, progress, recovery and titles use Environment, environment window or Redeven. Env App is internal, never a label or brand. All shipped catalogs explicitly translate this copy.

## Alignment
The four new-environment entries form a complete equal-column 2x2 grid, without a spanning last entry or vacant cell. Progress-panel Copy log and Close use the same Floe outline treatment, equal widths and row height; longer translations remain readable without overflowing.

Center visible content within the primary button, excluding the menu toggle. Idle text reserves no icon space. Submission shows a loader/shimmer, exposes busy state and blocks repeat clicks; completion restores centered text. Keep geometry fixed and meaningful icons grouped with labels.

Batch health refresh owns only the header refresh control until the batch settles. Each card's refresh icon follows its own health observation or explicit refresh request, so completed and failed probes stop independently. Observation never turns every card's primary action into a pending submission. Starting a card action cannot release the batch refresh control, and batch completion cannot clear that card's pending action.

## Perspectives and platform
Linked cards place Runtime, Redeven Cloud and paired Gateway tabs in the standalone badge slot. Cloud authorization or sync failure never disables Runtime actions. [Center navigation](desktop-welcome-navigation.md) transitions preserve card layout and do not restart on snapshots.

A bundled original-color OS mark beside the Runtime name reflects trusted platform data. Unknown platforms use a device mark; recognized Linux distributions use brand marks, otherwise Tux. Keep the slot fixed.

sections.title: Contract

## Sections and authority
Local opens Access & security and has no connection editor. Access management uses existing WSL authority only after discovery confirms that exact distribution is running; opening settings or automatic loading never starts a stopped distro.

Current process password constraints remain distinct from saved next-start configuration.

## Opening, drafts and saves
One opening owns the committed connection baseline, connection draft and lazily loaded access baseline and draft. Background health revalidation preserves the observed running summary, connection nodes, expanded listeners, address filters, selection, scroll and QR panels; it never reloads access, certificate or security configuration.

Starting a save invalidates older reads; late failure from a closed opening is a notification, never an error in the next editor.

## Access tasks and recovery
Access opens a task overview for current connection, browser access, sign-in protection and HTTPS certificate.

Recovery-pending protection must be restored before that change.

concepts.title: Desktop runtime process lifecycle

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Ownership
Keys combine host authority, exact container engine/id and normalized Runtime root. Native Local keys use the actual canonical state directory, resolving symlinks without equating parent and child. [Scoped Runtime operations](../ai/tessiven-runtime-operations.md) recheck source/target authority before this coordinator admits a handoff.

## Execution
- Start reuses one verified healthy Runtime. Stop succeeds on empty inventory and verifies termination.
- Restart stops the observed Runtime, starts the installed binary and verifies readiness.
- Update prepares/verifies its package before modification, starts even a previously stopped Runtime and verifies it.
- Refresh observes directly without mutation. Reinstall follows [its recovery contract](desktop-reinstall-operations.md).

The current binary supplies temporary exact inventory and best-effort stop. Builds, downloads, archive preparation, upload and extraction belong to package progress, never process discovery. Desktop exit/update retires WSL Bridges without stopping WSL Runtime.

## Actions
Direct targets retain lifecycle and Provider Connect/Disconnect actions in every diagnosis. Conflicting actions stay visible but disabled, naming the active operation. Access-only targets offer Open/Connect/refresh-access without lifecycle or management fallback.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Direct readiness
Native Local Environment is available on macOS/Linux; Windows uses registered WSL Environments. A newly published listener without final status remains pending within the startup deadline. Desktop update warns that Desktop and Local Runtime restart and interrupt Local sessions; Later changes nothing.

WSL, SSH and container observations use the saved channel. Unknown/failed health offers Refresh with its real diagnostic. Pending refresh retains prior diagnosis/startup age but withdraws live Presence; completion replaces it. Main retains credential-free `observed_runtime_control_status` until probe failure or management-configuration change. Gateway failure affects only that route.

A completed probe preserves missing-control diagnostics even when it publishes no Presence. Unknown or unauthenticated status must not become an observed stopped Runtime. Missing diagnostics may guide recovery but never grant live management capability; only current Presence can do so.

Direct lifecycle actions remain available in every diagnosis. Failed nested recovery names the actual operation and retains structured diagnostics; raw stderr appears only in technical details.

## Access and Flower
[Verified access routes](desktop-environment-access.md) owns association/defaults. Gateway directory presence, membership and application probing are distinct; failure never changes routes or starts Runtime recovery.

[Runtime Flower access](../../desktop/src/shared/runtimeFlowerAccess.ts) checks actual protocol/epoch for commands, subscriptions, frames and attachments. Desktop restart does not prove Runtime changed. Welcome admits Flower only with compatible openable Runtime and AI `ready`/`degraded`; transitional states show preparation with a return action, while missing/blocked/unavailable facts cannot admit requests.

concepts.title: Desktop SSH runtime operations
concepts.summary: Desktop manages SSH-host and SSH-container Runtime only through the saved connection and placement. One process-local lifecycle coordinator, Launcher Operation, transport lease and temporary helper serve Start, Stop, Restart, Update, Refresh, Open recovery and Reinstall. Gateway/Provider credentials never substitute for SSH authority. The target stores no Desktop lifecycle lock or supervisor state.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Authentication and transport
Keys bind normalized destination/port, authentication, SSH executable and credential scope. Preserve failure without substitution/replay. macOS/Linux use ControlMaster; Windows bounded native OpenSSH plus one child/private Bridge, never WSL/ControlMaster. Cancel only owned children.

Omitted passwords reuse exact private scope; explicit changes reject during leases and never cross scopes. Without password, explicit connections try configured keys/agent in batch mode even for password registrations; passive status may defer. Never send empty retries. Start/Restart/Update carry transient credentials through access/certificate checks, preparation and verification without saving; observations reject passwords.

Connect Timeout bounds probe/inventory/readiness; startup/packages have distinct deadlines. Windows x64 askpass accepts password/passphrase, rejects host-key prompts, writes only private stdout and preserves OpenSSH trust. Missing helper fails; no secrets in args/files/logs. Bounded includes exclude wildcard/negated picker aliases, not explicit destinations. Save exact root/container engine+ID separately from label.

## Execution
One operation reuses transport and probes platform once. Only inventory/stop prepares the small helper; Start/Stop never build full bundles. Update verifies before mutation with visible acquisition/upload/build. Use public dependencies and install Desktop deps before Env assets.

Archive bounds: 256 MiB compressed/512 MiB expanded including Runtime/Computer/signed plugins, enforced before writes and parsed once. Upload progress has its own stall deadline; command timeout resumes after final write. Stall/cancel/loss stops owned command; pipe bytes prove no receipt. Password prompts have no upload deadline.

Private slots: runtime/managed/bin/executables 0700, stamps/evidence 0600 independent of umask. Failed normalization preserves live slot; upstream owns executable admission. Host targets require confirmed user/root, containers exact saved identity. Start/Restart/Update/Reinstall may start container; Stop never does and accepts empty inventory. Signal only verified scope; retain before/after. Wipe-reinstall may tolerate helper inventory/stop failure only when direct access can isolate root.

Remote snippets perform bounded probe/stage/inventory/stop/install/start/verify/isolate/cleanup. Desktop owns order/deadlines/cancel/progress/retry; no target lock/heartbeat/supervisor.

## Progress and results
Use generated signed GitHub latest/download/redeven-install.sh with selected tag, no Portal duplicate. One Launcher Operation measures actual upload/download/acquisition bytes. Parse complete Downloading Redeven: N% records; stderr diagnostics, stdout stage path. Companion output cannot reset Runtime progress. No additional parser/process/poll.

100% transfer proves no activation/readiness. Freeze measured progress on failure/cancel. Acquisition/staging/upload/unpack are preparation; only activation changes live slot. Create operation before first SSH command. Distinguish connection/engine/preparation/command/readiness errors with technical stderr. Empty successful report stays pending to deadline; nonzero read is command failure, valid blocked report Runtime failure, only nonempty malformed report invalid. All lifecycle paths share interpretation.

concepts.title: Desktop transport recovery
concepts.summary: Each placement bridge owns HTTP/2, immutable recovery generation and registry identity. Its owner replaces stdio/session once, verifies process/Runtime, rejects late callbacks and disposes resources at one terminal boundary. Health observers or individual streams cannot independently restart transport.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Recovery presentation
Recovery uses an unboxed layout within the existing shell, with generous whitespace, semantic theme colors, standard buttons, and fine separators around the authoritative countdown or active phase.

A 30-second stalled-app timeout shows an actionable failure instead of an endless loading surface.

## Mechanism
Each established bridge owns one immutable transport-recovery snapshot with a monotonic `generation` and `revision`, the real `waiting`, `connecting`, `paused`, `ready`, or `failed` phase, completed attempt count, known retry and recovery timestamps, a structured failure, and explicitly allowed actions.

Lifecycle generation fencing cancels matching Opens so a late response cannot recreate the old session.

Terminal transport failure may preserve the renderer window for diagnosis and navigation, but every previously loaded Runtime surface remains non-interactive until a fresh session is explicitly opened.

concepts.title: Desktop WSL runtime operations
concepts.summary: Windows 11 x64 runs Electron only: no native Local, Windows or local-container Runtime. Register initialized Linux x64 WSL2 distributions independently; manage only exact distribution/user Runtime. Windows owns WSL installation/lifecycle/removal. Missing/WSL1/uninitialized distributions, commands, damaged packages or lost Bridge fail visibly with explicit recovery.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Discovery and registration
The main process publishes one immutable platform-capability snapshot. Renderer surfaces consume it and never infer the host operating system.

UI recovery copy may show Microsoft WSL commands for the user to run.

## Linux Runtime lifecycle
WSL and SSH host operations consume the same managed-Linux probe, uploaded install, atomic activation, startup report, inventory, exact stop, and verification scripts.

Runtime installs under the Linux user's home-backed `~/.redeven`, never under `/mnt`, and does not require `systemd`.

Only the Environment Stop action stops it.

## Private Bridge and failure behavior
`desktop-bridge` remains a foreground `wsl.exe` child carrying the shared `redeven-desktop-placement-h2/1` HTTP/2 session over private standard input and output.

Multiple registered distributions have independent target ids, processes, Bridges, update state, and lifecycle coordinator keys.

## Package and update boundary
The Windows Desktop bundle uses `managed_wsl_archive` and contains one verified `redeven_linux_amd64.tar.gz`; it must not contain or execute `redeven.exe`.

Public Windows assets remain forbidden until Authenticode signing, signed NSIS update metadata, signing receipts, and a real signed n-1 to n update are enabled together.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Windows and WSL 2 remain separate authorities. No boundary may be hidden by a native Windows Runtime, SSH-shaped WSL compatibility path, public port, localhost-forwarding dependency, system service, or second lifecycle state machine.

The [preparation contract](../architecture/host-application-preparation.md) owns those boundaries and pending application opening.

After explicit preparation, waiting and checking have unknown cache/download totals and no percentage.

## Layout
The first-party host-application bootstrap places its controls in one 40-pixel Desktop titlebar, alongside platform-owned traffic lights or caption buttons. Empty header space drags the window when no toolbar popover is open; buttons and popovers explicitly reject dragging.

The control is unavailable until its selected target has decoded pixels.

## Appearance and language
The bootstrap consumes published Floe `standalone.css`: primitive sizing and fonts, all 26 shell presets, shared floating material and input focus rules. Local CSS owns only viewer layout and maps control states to upstream semantic tokens; it must not maintain a second light/dark palette.

The inline assets add no request or connection wait.

## Backend commands
The shared toolbar and picture-preset presentation do not own backend state. macOS retains native menu, window-generation, frame credit and capture-quality semantics.

It never sends server shutdown or force-kills the application. macOS quit retains its existing application-wide confirmation. These distinct actions must not be collapsed into one destructive command.

concepts.title: Gateway access sessions
concepts.summary: Desktop opens a joined Runtime over its existing outbound Flowersec connection to Gateway. Gateway forwards bytes to the Runtime's fixed application entry; it has no Runtime URL to dial. TLS terminates in Desktop and Runtime. Password, MFA, Host/Origin checks and application authorization remain Runtime-owned. Access artifacts limit initial redemption; no Gateway timer shortens established business sessions.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Reverse application streams
After local consent, Runtime redeems its invitation with its own identity and initiates a persistent Flowersec session to the member TLS endpoint. Gateway opens a reverse ByteStream on that Runtime's connection and relays both streams with bounded buffers and cancellation.

TLS, WebSocket, streaming responses and secure cookies retain their original semantics.

## Application and management separation
A reverse stream enters the original public Runtime handler. It never acquires a trusted Desktop management marker.

The catalog alone does not authorize service or Runtime process operations.

## Limits and revocation
The shared budget admits at most 32 business connections per member and 1,024 in total, including pending opens. One member exceeding a limit cannot consume another member's allocation.

Cloud closure receipts and partition limits are owned by [Gateway Cloud access](gateway-cloud-access.md).

concepts.title: Gateway client access
concepts.summary: Gateway exposes two fixed paths: verified host administration and environment-only URL access. Clients cannot choose roles or persist management authority. Runtime lifecycle and application authentication remain independent; Cloud operations still require Cloud authorization.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Host administration
Local, SSH, local-container and SSH-container connections acquire management only after actually reaching the target Gateway and verifying its private host credential. It never exposes the credential to Renderer, URL connections, Runtime channels or logs.

Removing a Desktop connection does not stop or delete the Gateway service.

## URL enrollment and reconnection
Administrators create client access codes through POST `/gateway/v6/clients/access-codes` or `redeven-gateway clients access-code`. An identical completion retry returns the original result after response loss; other clients cannot consume that code.

A client access code neither enrolls a Runtime nor grants Gateway administration.

## Client visibility and revocation
Host administrators list clients through POST `/gateway/v6/clients/list` or `redeven-gateway clients list`. The display name is a recognition label, never identity evidence.

Revocation survives restart.

## State and compatibility
Trust schema 3 retains Gateway and client keys, preserves previously allowed environment access and removes legacy management grants. A handshake mismatch requests a Gateway/Desktop update, not identity replacement or state reinstallation.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Independent approval and membership
Joining a Gateway establishes local membership only. A directory cannot obtain Runtime credentials.

Namespace authorization, local egress permission and batch-enrollment delegation are separate decisions.

## Required network path
Runtime control registration, independent recovery, data transport and enabled official-platform requests use the explicitly selected route. Gateway outages and denied egress never trigger a direct Internet fallback or global proxy environment variables.

Ownership changes require separate authorization.

## One recovery owner
Registration, heartbeat and credential replenishment share one connection controller and independent credential source.

Unknown results resume that operation.

Each route operation can be queried after an unknown result; cancellation reports a committed operation truthfully.

## Management notifications and closure
Each Gateway has one authenticated HTTPS notification owner. Reconnection starts with an authoritative snapshot.

No short data lease is introduced during ordinary control outages.

concepts.title: Gateway Desktop interactions
concepts.summary: Desktop enrolls managed Local, SSH, WSL and container targets through one app-owned session. Runtime management, invitation verification and local consent remain separate authorities. Membership appears only after joining; observations preserve drafts, while confirmed faults require explicit recovery. No Runtime URL enrollment form exists.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Enrollment and authority
One app session serves creation and card actions for managed Local, SSH, WSL and container targets. Creation offers Not now or Add Gateway access after setup. Each opening leases the exact sender/target Env App bridge and connects before verification/consent; prior opening is no current proof. Env App closure retains the lease, while cancel, navigation/destruction and authority changes retire it. Admitted writes retain transport until settlement; reject late requests.

Try saved management authentication first, including available SSH/OpenSSH credentials. Passive auth_required or missing saved passwords cannot preempt it. Only a current typed authentication failure exposes focused, Enter-submittable temporary credentials and stops credential-free retries. Distinguish authentication, Gateway and engine failures; unknown status is not rejection. Temporary passwords belong only to scoped status, never verification/consent; do not save preferences. Carry them unchanged through the admitted action/access verification, then clear on completion/failure/closure. Startup observations cannot race clearing or interrupt the action.

Proven stopped targets offer explicit Start. Start/restart/update share the lifecycle owner and request credentials only after typed SSH failure. Connection loss stops submissions/polling but retains drafts. Explicit recovery, authority change or Settings suspension revokes verification/consent; resume with a fresh connection/lease. Preserve step/code drafts and use inline feedback. Observations cannot cancel admitted actions.

## Gateway selection and invitation
Saved/manual tabs keep separate drafts/input nodes. Select enabled registration ID, never address or connectivity. Retain endpoint-less entries with setup guidance. Use confirmed member_endpoints, otherwise only a URL registration's canonical HTTPS origin; SSH/listener coordinates are not substitutes. Reject changed trust, invalid/Host-rejected origins and remote loopback without hiding registrations. Inventory cannot overwrite typing; removing a selected usable address revokes verification.

manage_members uses update_gateway_endpoints without changing listeners/restrictions. Retain authoritative IPC values only until catalog change; never restore removed addresses. Enrollment needs explicit invite_gateway_runtime or pasted code plus Runtime verification/consent. Saving/selecting/issuing alone never enrolls. Access-only users receive administrator guidance. Close/suspension/authority changes fence late responses; success consumes code and reopening clears consent/code.

Unknown submission queries exact membership without resubmitting. Positive membership completes; authoritative absence clears uncertain/consumed material and returns to verification. Checks consume no code. Done restores the originating control.

## Welcome and management
Keep toolbar, horizontal Environment/Redeven Cloud/Gateway navigation, search/filter and bottom bar. Responsive compact cards become one column when narrow. Name/Manage opens an in-shell page: Overview, Clients, Runtimes, Network, Redeven Cloud, Service maintenance. Localized All Gateways restores search/scroll/focus. Global navigation suspends owners and reopening preserves drafts.

Cards group identity/management, equal full-row Connect client/Runtime actions, and observed status/refresh/recovery footer. Manage/More share Floe control geometry and touch sizing. Access-only cards omit enrollment. Shared Dropdown offers local Edit, Enable/Disable and confirmed Remove, explaining retained remote membership/service. Clients/Cloud initialize independently; URL access inherits no stale administration. One action owner survives filtering, without a hidden maintenance card.

Creation separates existing service/new deployment and URL pairing/host transport. Save returns the exact registration and opens its overview/status/next action; it proves neither deployment nor connectivity. Connect Runtime distinguishes Desktop-managed targets from another administrator. Managed enrollment reuses the app session, including stopped/unopened targets. Other-admin uses the existing invitation issuer; missing addresses link to Network. Wait for outgoing modal presence. Hiding preserves admitted work/drafts; resume through card actions with fresh management/consent, without another issuer or banner.

Only active sections contribute scroll extent; visited sections stay mounted. Floe navigation wraps below 768 px. Dialogs own edit/enrollment/service tasks and keyboard return. Ready empty cards show counts without banners. Use semantic tokens and explicit locale catalogs. Compatible installed Gateways are reused; build/commit inequality cannot invent start/update requirements or reinterpret pairing rejection. [Service compatibility](gateway-service.md) owns readiness.

Runtimes owns members/Cloud overrides/recheck/removal; Cloud owns global policy; Clients owns listings/revocation. Client enrollment prepares editable HTTPS, then explicitly issues code/expiry/address with individual/combined copy. Observations retain addresses/codes/drafts. Shared Dropdowns own choices; refresh failure preserves data. Settings/import grants no Runtime/Namespace authority. [Network](gateway-network-settings.md) owns validation/restart.

Translated panels stay viewport-bounded with shared keyboard/focus behavior and border-only focus. All locales supply hostname:port, listener/Host examples and plural timers. Localized member recovery keeps raw/future codes in details; policy feedback pairs action labels with hook IDs.

## Service actions
Card/service/network-restart actions share admission, foreground ownership and progress. Confirmation names action/target/affected sessions and title-row close. Pending replaces controls until authoritative progress. Closing cannot reopen or redispatch. Show observed steps/state/elapsed time, never fabricated percentages. Raw details collapse beneath timeline; failure retains recovery. Hide restores focus without canceling; reopen retains timing, and reconnect adopts current work before another confirmation.

## Configuration ownership
`POST /gateway/v6/network-settings` requires current verified host management proof and saves one bounded settings object.

Desktop Settings shows the saved listener bindings separately from active addresses. A pending restart exposes an explicit review action using the same Gateway lifecycle confirmation and progress as card maintenance. Saving never restarts the service.

A runtime-selected ephemeral port is reported as an active address rather than replacing the configured `:0` binding.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
## Request Host restriction
The default empty list accepts all request Host names. Forwarded headers cannot expand the list.

The separate native host administration listener retains its request-bound host proof and browser Origin rejection.

## Durable upgrade and recovery
Member state v4 appends `allowed_hosts` to the existing endpoint state. Future versions and invalid network shapes fail read-only. Atomic state replacement owns the save boundary; a write failure cannot install partial network settings in memory.
