concepts.title: Gateway service
concepts.summary: redeven-gateway owns durable membership, one-time invitations, client grants, policy and restricted forwarding. Runtime verifies address/code, previews signed enrollment then explicitly joins. Gateway never scans/dials Runtime addresses or manages Runtime lifecycle. LAN needs no Cloud; Gateway loss affects its paths, not independent management authority.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Membership authority
An administrator verified through the Gateway host creates a ten-minute, single-use invitation code and shares an administrator-confirmed Gateway address. Gateway never obtains Runtime Cloud credentials from its directory.

Desktop display association uses the trusted Runtime management membership summary and the paired Gateway key; public health proof remains a separate observation and grants no authority.

## Policy and executable hooks
New installations deny Cloud by default.

Programs use an absolute executable and argument array, never a shell. Desktop member management and `redeven-gateway members reevaluate --member ID --version N` check the current member version before applying the same reevaluation.

## Own-process management
The separate Gateway archive and state root contain no Runtime lifecycle data. Saving, refresh, pairing or member management never starts a stopped service implicitly.

Cancellation still stops development startup and exact owned-process cleanup remains required.

## Compatibility and updates

Gateway release tags and source commits are diagnostics, not admission gates. Desktop validates the installed binary against its own installation stamp, then observes service readiness and the actual Gateway wire/authority contract. An unrelated Desktop or Runtime release never forces Gateway replacement. Start/restart reuse an intact installed package; explicit Update validates the staged archive against the selected release and commit before activation. Package corruption, stopped service, pairing failure and protocol incompatibility remain distinct diagnoses; authorization rejection never implies an outdated build.

Gateway v6 owns its authority epoch independently of Runtime Service. The existing value 69 is preserved so deployed services remain compatible; change it only for a reviewed Gateway authority break. Runtime metadata versions do not gate membership. Preserve signed identity, consent, permissions, freshness and current protocol validation; best-effort compatibility does not accept unknown security contracts. A feature failure affects that operation, not unrelated members or Runtime lifecycle authority.

## Address changes and upgrade
[Gateway network settings](gateway-network-settings.md) owns atomic network configuration, next-start listener changes, request Host admission and its persistent migration boundary.

If all fail, the membership stays intact and reports Gateway unavailable.

Optional Cloud publishing remains a separate flow.

concepts.title: Flower explicit long-thread qualification
concepts.summary: Complete long-conversation content and responsive interaction are required product properties. Run this fixed-budget suite explicitly for acceptance/investigation, outside unified commit, integration and CI gates; it is not a prerequisite for each commit.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Execution and evidence
Run node scripts/check_flower_long_thread.mjs --fast for focused regressions; omit --fast for browser/sustained acceptance. Require frozen published Desktop/Env dependencies and visible composited Electron; unavailable prerequisites fail. Unified gate manifests exclude this explicit suite.

Record exact source/tree/cleanliness, tools/dependencies, metrics and supervised cleanup. Changed product/dependencies invalidate performance evidence; policy-only changes may cite prior unchanged-product evidence separately, never relabel an unmeasured tip. Nonzero/interrupted runs, missing tests/metrics/tools or failed cleanup fail. Preserve negative 110 ms latency/21 commits-per-second regression and profile-exclusion test. No workload/threshold override or waived failure.

## Correctness
Fast checks cover indexed records, queues, windows, turn/disclosure identity, block invalidation, keyed disposal, local thinking, structural/mutable dependencies, sealed bodies and incremental Markdown. Each sequence entry has one mounted owner; classification stays stable while live fields and first-prose boundaries update. Removed owners dispose. Title identity classifies once, visibility only on admission/claim; grouping never rescans completed bodies. Restored titles stay static. Cover 600 retained rows and actual browser arrival.

Per-group disclosure observers update only changed blockers; removed groups dispose. A 600-group case forbids repeated historical folding. Body growth cannot advance restoration provenance; full hydration retains its boundary. Root/child regressions preserve fresh motion through history scans. Correct anchors synchronously on loading completion, not byte growth. Structural batches publish membership once after records are ready, without per-replacement rescans. Parent intervals own coverage independently of text; immutable turn facts add no per-field subscriptions. Cover history/reconnect/selection/input/approval/terminal state.

Sustained fixture creates 500 canonical turns, 1,000 messages and 1,000 tools through real Service/published Floret/fake providers, verifying all admitted content. No paid provider, user state, raw DB writes or product fallback. Produce mixed text/reasoning/Markdown at 80 updates/s, one tool per 60 updates and initial 32 KiB body independently of UI; accumulate >=120 seconds in one active turn.

After canonical terminal observation, use actual history/disclosure controls to compare every generated prose/reasoning item and exact code blocks with canonical content/full Markdown. Enter reading mode and reveal parents before children; never force hidden clicks/change disclosure state. Draft/focus/selection survive drag. Synthetic floating output does not qualify terminal emulation.

## Responsiveness
Sample idle/early/late/repeat on the same visible production UI with two PersistentFloatingWindows, >=12 monotonic seconds each. Cancellation, button release, blur or hidden document invalidates samples. Dedicated nonfocusable Electron host installs pointer isolation before showing, preventing native keyboard input while retaining real composition, CDP input, DOM focus and interruption checks. Assert both drafts before and throughout sampling.

Read counter before press; one CDP session performs press/move/release with no intervening backend calls. Use Chromium monotonic timestamps. Independent 60 Hz producer cannot await dispatch: offer >=55 events/s and require >=45 position commits/s and >=80% idle cadence.

Fixed budgets: presented drag P95 <=75 ms; work-minus-idle <=25 ms; >=95% prose markers with P95 <=250 ms; frame P95 <=25 ms; reactive apply P95 <=12 ms/max <=50 ms; no main-thread task >=100 ms. Known regressions do not relax them; they are requirements, not universal/photon claims.

Pair complete MOUSE_DRAGGED async spans by process/identity/scope with compositor presentation. Report coalesced/unpresented separately and require >=30 presented samples/s. Healthy rAF cannot prove input responsiveness. No profiling/screencast during timing.

A report's `pass` describes that scenario only; the Go process exit status is authoritative for the complete run.

Required cases:

- Stop generation or owned terminal: preserve confirmed effects, prevent delayed writes, accept later work; cancellation is not failure-retried.
- Queue optimistic edit/stale rejection/order/delete, exact executed user order, Send now cancellation/promotion and conflicting duplicate keys.
- Stop/restart at generation/approval/Ask User; stale answers cannot execute, retained queue promotes once. Queue edits during approval preserve this boundary.

- Two interrupted continuations plus concurrent Retry/queued input preserve original write once. Duplicate Send now rejects consumed edits/reexecution.
- Queued permission updates, rejected active-model changes and immutable approvals; repeated readonly/approval/full-access transitions include stop/restart, stale/fresh approvals, post-effect failures and downgrade/retry.

Own and remove temporary stores/files/services/processes, preserve reports and unchanged source configuration/credentials.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Qualify these independent boundaries with native/viewer/API fixtures:

- Reuse an existing single-instance Mac process and preserve it after lease release. A 48-second first-window fixture must wait without relaunch.
- Multiwindow picker counts/literal titles preserve selection/focus; canceled close/quit retains process, pixels, sharing and explicit retry. Last lease release ends sharing, never the application.
- Unreadable/replaced surfaces never expire into closure. Confirmed final-window closure ends established physical viewers. Linux dialog-only apps reveal native-sized decoded dialogs.
- Stale quit selection rejects the whole set before termination. Unknown outcome retains error without inferred exit/retry. Read-only callers may list but cannot quit/detach.
- Network/reload retains process, suspends input/capture, frees buffers and reconnects the same session/current credential. Successor viewer revokes prior input/releases held keys/suspends capture first.
- Permission loss/lock has distinct recovery. Helper exit is sharing failure, not app exit; retire route/credential/buffers/helper before terminal state. Ignore late callbacks and retain unknown-terminal pages.
- Unproven foreground/window identity rejects input without replay/retargeting. Missing decoder negotiates same-process image transport.

Toolbar qualification: fixed bar with resizable content, bounded 320/390/1000 px popovers, keyboard menus, separate close/confirmed quit, late dismissal and no unconfirmed replay. Native quit covers catalog/session controls, visible/windowless apps, cancellation and stale generations.

The [display contract](../architecture/host-application-display.md) owns picture
behavior. Floe Native Apps owns capture, encoding and region decoding; Redeven owns

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Reproducible measurements
Compare baseline and candidate on the same host, browser version, source size and workload.

An SSH tunnel changes transport overhead and must be recorded.

| Metric | Definition and controlled viewer acceptance budget |
| --- | --- |
| Input to presented pixels | DOM key event through remote application to changed canvas pixels on the next animation frame; nearest-rank P95 of 20 samples below 150 ms in every mode |
| Input during motion | The same 20-sample measurement while document scroll continues; P95 below 250 ms, including Save data cadence |
| Presented FPS | At most one changed-canvas presentation per animation frame; Motion first at least 25 FPS during document scroll |
| Received payload | All incoming WebSocket data bytes, including JSON; excludes WebSocket/TLS/SSH framing and network retransmissions |
| Idle bandwidth | Below 0.25 Mb/s after settling; a fully unchanged document should send zero image bytes |
| Document-motion bandwidth | Below 5 Mb/s for Automatic/Clarity/Save data and 15 Mb/s for Motion first at the recorded source size |
| Decode work | No more than two current-target frames plus one retired decode; no reconnect on a picture change |
| First frame | Navigation to first decoded canvas presentation; excludes browser-process launch before the viewer attaches |

## Published-module product results
A sandboxed Chrome 153 client on Ubuntu passed all v0.21.0 viewer budgets over loopback, isolating capture, forwarding, decoding and presentation from networking:

| Application | Automatic Mb/s | Motion-first FPS | Static-input P95 across modes | Scrolling-input P95 across modes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Chrome | 2.14 | 27.0 | 46–65 ms | 129–237 ms |
| Firefox | 4.37 | 37.4 | 65–81 ms | 99–231 ms |

## Observed native pipeline improvement
Sequential tests on Ubuntu 26.04 amd64, Chrome 153.0.8010.36 (1292 by 753 pixels) and Firefox 155.0.1 (1000 by 700 pixels) compared the authentic v0.20.0 component with the v0.21.0 implementation.

| Workload | v0.20.0 | Automatic | Motion first | Save data |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Chrome scroll, Mb/s | 25.04 | 1.59 | 10.61 | 0.64 |
| Chrome scroll, FPS | 25.1 | 19.4 | 34.0 | 8.8 |
| Chrome input P95, ms | 59.6 | 52.8 | 49.9 | 81.3 |
| Firefox scroll, Mb/s | 30.64 | 2.20 | 6.53 | 0.59 |
| Firefox scroll, FPS | 32.4 | 28.7 | 37.4 | 7.9 |
| Firefox input P95, ms | 103.3 | 54.5 | 54.5 | 78.3 |

concepts.title: Deploy and qualify standalone Web Center

frontmatter.title: Deploy and qualify standalone Web Center

concepts.summary: Center binary/UI deploy separately from Desktop and Runtime. Evidence records source/artifacts, host, browser, real elapsed duration, cleanup and limits. Smoke tests cannot certify an eight-hour soak or a different native browser. Qualification uses isolated service names, ports and state, and preserves existing Runtime processes.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Release and install
Center installs independently beside Runtime/Desktop under one tag; upgrades never touch those services. Protocol/capability admission, not shared tag, decides compatibility. Formal artifacts are Linux amd64/arm64 archives with .manifest.json receipts, signed SHA256SUMS and remote readback. Native jobs execute each target; either failure blocks. macOS source is development only, no Windows/macOS service or registry image.

Archive contains binary/UI, two units, environment examples, Docker/Compose/.env, licenses, DEPLOYMENT.md and manifest. --version reports source/time without state. Verify every file/target/tag/digest; reject dirty source, extras/missing files, links or mismatch. Both targets share commit. Extract verified signed bytes into a new version directory. Target needs no build toolchain/Electron/local Runtime. Compose builds from package and exact .env; upgrades preserve state/settings. Runtime installer does not install Center.

Source uses pinned Node, Desktop package manager, Go and public dependencies. build_center.sh <new-directory> [version] emits complete package; omitted version is dev, production requires tag. Cross-builds need real target execution.

serve requires state-root/origin/tls-cert/tls-key/assets/connector-socket/connector-user/listen. Separate connector uses socket and center-user; both verify peer UID before credentials. Origin is immutable. DNS/TLS covers portal/Env/children; Center terminates TLS, edge TCP passthrough allowed, forwarded headers grant nothing.

Linux: nonlogin redeven-center/redeven-connector share group; root-owned /opt/redeven-center; private 0700 /var/lib/redeven-center and Center-readable keys. Install units plus /etc/redeven-center/center.env; Connector owns /run/redeven-connector/connector.sock without state/config access. Group traversal/kernel UID authenticate. daemon-reload and enable --now redeven-center start both independently of Runtime. Owner commands require Center/root. Stop-state backup/explicit replacement precede upgrade, never recursive deletion.

Compose: supplied Linux Dockerfile, Center UID/GID10001, Connector UID10002, shared socket, read-only roots/dropped capabilities. Only Center mounts private state/TLS. tls/server.pem/server-key.pem readable by 10001; configure CENTER_ORIGIN then compose up --build -d. Port 8443 must match external DNS/SAN. Exec Center setup for temporary credential. Preserve named volume; down -v deletes data. Operator owns DNS/TLS.

## First use and recovery
Verify trusted HTTPS /healthz. Owner runs setup with state root, then browser password/TOTP/recovery codes. Add access-only Gateway after fingerprint confirmation, assign Env origin and apply descriptor through Runtime owner CLI. Runtime factors stay independent; direct bookmarks bypass server relay.

Stop Center before preserving key/database/sidecars together with ownership/modes. Restore same origin/compatible binary. Restart invalidates devices, not Runtime workspaces. Never copy only live SQLite main/key or delete missing committed material to reopen setup. Factor loss uses recover or stopped offline recover --origin, completing browser factors. Route-key rotation closes exact route and requires new descriptor/current revision. TLS renewal restarts; master-key reencryption/pinned-origin changes are not exposed.

## Explicit qualification
check_center.sh verifies contracts/security/host/UI. REDEVEN_CENTER_BROWSER=1 Go TestCenterBrowserQualification with floeterm_native uses real browsers/Gateway/Runtimes and trusted TLS; WebKit is not Safari. EXTERNAL_FIXTURE selects owned remote state. Private factors stay out of Git; optional physical/model/container/file lanes require actual components and cleanup. Authorized model tests delete threads.

CAPACITY=1 creates 100 signed members/ten live Runtime tabs/90 offline. CONNECTOR_BIN selects built worker and tests restart. SOAK_SECONDS=28800 needs eight actual hours with terminal/Flower subscriptions and file roundtrips, no paid generation. Separate fixture heap from process RSS/browser memory. Failed/stopped preflight proves no soak time.

check_center_deployment.mjs validates package startup/setup/restart/recovery/missing-key/TLS denial. check_center_linux_deployment.mjs <ssh-host> <staged-root> <address> <image> runs real systemd/nonroot container with Chrome, peer denial and factor recovery. Require owned artifacts/trusted TLS/sudo/authorized host. Tool removes its units/container; caller removes staged artifacts/state after evidence review.

concepts.title: Gateway v6 protocol
concepts.summary: Gateway serves only redeven-gateway-v6, defined by spec/openapi/gateway-v6.yaml. Signed invitations carry admin-confirmed addresses; authenticated exchange returns the signed descriptor/all endpoints. Gateway owns paired Desktop permissions and Runtime-initiated membership. Mismatch/old config fails unchanged; old URL-profile/HTTP-forward routes are absent. Cloud v3 remains separate.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Wire authority
The signed Desktop surface includes pairing, identity proof, catalog, invitation, member removal, member and default policy, reevaluation, member access offer and service description, and Cloud configuration/status.

A Runtime mTLS certificate must be current for that exact member and version.

Service descriptions are signed separately and bind the Runtime's TLS application identity.

## Compatibility ownership

`protocol.Version` and `protocol.CompatibilityEpoch` own Gateway wire and host-authority admission. Desktop mirrors these in `gatewayMembership.ts`; Runtime Service compatibility changes do not change either. Preserve the deployed signed `compatibility_epoch` value 69 independently of Runtime release cadence. It remains covered by identity and pairing signatures. Different binary releases/commits are allowed within this contract; incompatible wire or authority contracts still fail explicitly. Runtime member version metadata is descriptive, not a software-version admission condition.

## Version and persistence
Member version controls removal and replacement. Directory and policy revisions prevent stale messages from restoring permissions.

[Gateway Cloud access](../gateway/gateway-cloud-access.md) owns publication, recovery and revocation.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: The OpenAPI document and signed DTOs are the protocol authority. Unknown routes, stale generations, and legacy URL-profile requests remain rejected rather than silently translated.

concepts.snippet: Gateway serves only redeven-gateway-v6, defined by spec/openapi/gateway-v6.yaml. Signed invitations carry admin-confirmed addresses; authenticated exchange returns the signed descriptor/all endpoints. Gateway owns paired Desktop permissions

concepts.title: RCPP v5 Cloud API
concepts.summary: RCPP v5 separates Cloud authorization from network route. CloudRuntimeBinding owns environment, Runtime identity, Namespace, user or Namespace principal and generation. One Runtime ConnectionController handles direct and Gateway enrollment, registration, heartbeat, reserve maintenance and recovery. Desktop never creates a second credential recovery owner.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Checks and provenance
AGENTS owns workflow/100-line cap, enforced by quick_ci_policy. Development is focused; staged commit checks locale/hygiene/notices/viewer bytes. Ordinary CI has one bounded source job. check_final_integration.sh runs once on exact clean rebased base/tip: pushed object equals main, ancestry fast-forwards, no unpublished merges. Earlier evidence cannot certify changes. Reuse fingerprints bind inputs/tools except variable macOS MANPATH; real-hook tests guard identity. List all formatting errors first; generators leave no diff.

Long-thread/browser/Electron/broad UI/Docker/native/stress remain explicit. Release needs authenticated artifacts and same-commit historical-conversation Actions. Staged notices use index snapshot, installed metadata and cached exact Go with GOTOOLCHAIN=local, no network/index rewrite. Main dependencies check full notices with GOWORK=off; development startup does not. Floe notice artifacts must match manifest/lock versions. Viewer checks staged source/locked deps without install/generation; buildHostApplicationAppearance.mjs owns generation.

Daily/manual CodeQL skips unchanged main only after a successful scheduled run; lookup failure scans. Review source/locks; dismissals need specific authority/input evidence. Unavailable/nonzero is not clean. Actions pins/Node 24 are independent of product Node.

## Build contracts
Exact Go patch comes from go.mod; first-party Node from .node-version. Gates/engines/README agree. Desktop allows only Electron/esbuild lifecycle, ignores electron-winstaller for internal NSIS. Dependency changes regenerate notices. README translations preserve structure/terms/hash; imagery has actual Runtime/shared provenance and localized alt. Root URLs are only the exact public destinations in hygiene allowlist; variants and implementation copies remain blocked. Commit three OKF outputs.

Build embedded UI before Go. Env checkout lock covers cleanup/typecheck/Vite/budgets/compression; same checkout waits, worktrees are independent. build_assets cannot compress unlocked or skip absent output. Native Linux/Darwin amd64/arm64 Runtime uses published cgo/floeterm_native; untagged attachment rejects. Contracts cover Bash 3.2 arguments; main checks source, native execution is explicit.

## Qualification and security
History workflow copies immutable released-writer state through public APIs/restart. Releases require same-commit success; ordinary checks validate fixture provenance. [Upgrade](../ai/flower-upgrade-compatibility.md) owns preservation. Use canonical headless carriers/fresh assets; [web dependencies](../architecture/env-app-upstream-web-dependencies.md) owns modes. Floe tests use real client/browser utilities except stated boundaries. Preserve scroll geometry/after-paint focus; PDF drag restores temporary scale removal.

[Desktop test lifecycle](../desktop/desktop-test-lifecycle.md) owns cleanup. Isolate preload/session/work paths and drain exact owned process groups/Windows trees. External SIGKILL fails. Pinned Electron preflight rejects AMFI/signals as environment failure; never resign/change trust/deps. Windows qualifies exact origin/main, Linux Runtime/two owned WSL distros and install/Start/Bridge/external-stop/Retry/Update/exact Stop before internal unsigned NSIS; only owned distros unregister.

Read/hash/consume manifests, logs, source identity, pins, keys and credentials through one no-follow descriptor, checking inode replacement. Computer proxy permits fixed Responses POST only; terminal TLS exceptions need isolated CA. Single-line bounded diagnostics/synthetic data/quoted SSH confer no authority. Secret scan excludes downloaded dependency caches but retains native/product build files.

## Release
Center shares tag but installs independently: native Linux amd64/arm64 static binaries with exact identity, UI/licenses/templates and same-commit digest receipts. Missing/mismatch blocks collector; checksums/readback include both. [Deployment](../operations/web-center-deployment.md) owns service procedure. CI/tag alone certifies no long-duration/device acceptance.

[Plugin artifacts](redevplugin-release-gates.md) and [integration](plugin-integration-gates.md) own their gates. Consumers pin Cosign. Desktop uses Corepack/frozen Env dependencies to stage Playwright/QuickJS without browser acquisition. Bash 3.2/Linux traps preserve staging and original failure.

Protected redeven-release supplies signing/notarization/Sparkle/Team secrets; public feed/key is credential-free HTTPS. Verify App/framework/bridge/DMG target, Team, hardening/notarization. DMG must be Accepted/stapled before receipts/feed; App ticket and distribution policy pass. Stable publishes two signed non-delta appcasts/notes then deletes temp keys; prereleases omit them and collector rejects feeds. Linux feeds match target. Installer/feed/notes join checksums/readback; [installer](self-contained-installer.md) owns activation and separate promotion.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Published source and trust

Consume the coordinated version pinned by go.mod and the Env App package locks. Boundary scans reject sibling wiring, Go workspace/replace, npm links, copied runtimes/contracts, Rust paths and duplicate platform-core; exclude generated output/dependencies and fail on scanner errors. Do not commit plugin packages/parallel catalog. Validated latest-only market snapshots choose immutable transport; ReDevPlugin verifies retrieval. Metadata is not trust.

Require exactly one upstream platform-release-manifest.json. Bind tag/source/workflow/attestation; independently verify Go proxy/SumDB h1/go.mod, both npm SHA-512 integrities/provenance, runtime/worker crates.io checksums/Cargo VCS, manifest version/closed coordinate order/contract-set hash. Extra assets/partial publication/local or mutable identities/registry mismatches fail before construction.

Manifest transport requires verified HTTPS through redirects. Initial attempt plus three network retries (including handshake):15s connect/60s transfer/120s retry-start bounds; last transfer may finish later. Exhaustion removes partials and stops before Rust preparation with release-specific diagnostics. Validation never retries. --manifest-file applies identical offline validation. Node CLI must validate/emit evidence from canonical or symlinked paths; empty success is not evidence.

## Native construction and admission

Build Linux/Darwin amd64/arm64 from exact published crate/packaged lock/Rust1.88.0; metadata cannot resolve another first-party path. Verify toolchain/target before preparation; warm caches avoid servers. Retry only transient installation failures, three attempts default/five maximum; integrity/signature/manifest failures stop. REDEVEN_RUSTUP_OFFLINE=1 means cache-only Rustup, not manifest/Cargo bypass. Honor standard Cargo/Rustup/proxies, disable probe auto-install, retain TLS/recheck installs/return exact Cargo. Download120s; waits2/4s capped60s; cancellation ends retries/cleans diagnostics.

Linux: static PIE, no interpreter/dynamic dependencies. Darwin: native target-exact64-bit Mach-O; Developer ID/hardened runtime/timestamp before evidence (development ad hoc). Emit binary/SPDX SBOM/resolved provenance/notices/signature/certificate. Release Sigstore identity binds exact tag workflow; ephemeral local Ed25519 fails --require-release. Cosign3 uses --new-bundle-format=false/--use-signing-config=false with workflow/OIDC/transparency verification.

redeven.redevplugin_runtime_build.v1 binds publication/product files/target/toolchain/source/workflow/signer. Consumption rechecks descriptors/target/profile/signature. Startup trusts expected marker digest, never field binary's self-computed hash. Runtime archives contain exactly Redeven, ReDevPlugin runtime, six evidence files, license/notices.

## Desktop packages and collector

Before replacing .bundle/<target>, validate name/closed flat inventory/Go target/native policy. Gateway stays separate. Include full evidence beside Redeven. macOS exclusion regex matches only independently signed runtime; preserve its bytes/evidence. Redeven/Computer/Sparkle/bridge remain signable. After Electron assembly copy complete Computer resource tree/licenses. Validate startup before signing and again after refreshing only signer-visited Runtime/Computer descriptors, immediately before enclosing seal.

Inspect final DEB/RPM/read-only DMG and emit v2 installer-bound receipts for runtime/six evidence files. Upload only installers/receipts/latest-linux*.yml, no diagnostics/unrelated macOS YAML. Use Apple tools/system text without ripgrep and consume full pipelines under pipefail. Require Team ID/signature/hardened runtime/updater key/stapling/distribution; Sparkle lipo takes binary before -verify_arch. Separate Linux relink source/object archives from runtime. Derive epoch/windows from reviewed contract; normalize feed names before signed inventory.

DEB permits POSIX ustar/GNU regular files/directories, bounded long names/metadata-only root. RPM disables optional build-id symlinks. Bounded no-follow snapshots reject noncanonical/duplicate paths, links/devices, privileged modes, sparse/PAX metadata, malformed trailers/trailing data/oversize.

Collector requires four Runtime/Gateway package directories, four Desktop directories, and two Center directories. Inventory: four Redeven/four Gateway archives, two DEBs/two RPMs/two DMGs/six target receipts/identical shared metadata, plus both Center archives/receipts described by [release gates](ci-and-release-gates.md). Open each source once no-follow, hash/copy same descriptor, verify inode/metadata, fsync/link without replacement; clean partial output on failure.

Windows managed_wsl_archive internally certifies one Linux amd64 archive bound to version/source/size/digest, rejecting redeven.exe. Formal collector rejects all Windows directories until signed-update/signing certification; no optional fifth target.

Final release requires release-only consumption, signed checksums/safe_extract_tar.py and complete draft names/sizes/hashes comparison before publication. [Installer](self-contained-installer.md) owns verify-before-execute, immutable suite activation/retention.

concepts.title: Self-contained installer distribution
concepts.summary:
Release packaging builds `redeven-installer_<os>_<arch>` for macOS and Linux,
AMD64 and ARM64, with CGO disabled. It renders `redeven-install.sh` from the
actual four binary digests and signs both the binaries and entry through
`SHA256SUMS`. No receiving-host Go, Cosign, Python, OpenSSL or package manager
is required. A standard shell, HTTPS downloader and SHA-256 utility remain
bootstrap prerequisites.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Trust and acquisition
The HTTPS bootstrap is the initial trust boundary. Its reviewed fixed digest authenticates the installer before execution. Upstream Cosign Blob API verifies exact repository workflow, OIDC issuer and tag through authenticated TUF roots, certificate transparency and Rekor. Accept detached .sig plus PEM/base 64 PEM only; no format guessing, mutable trust overrides, disabled verification or fabricated markers. Signature/digest failure never executes Runtime.

TUF requests are cancellable/time-bounded without writing user trust cache. Bound log responses before SDK parsing and admit detached X.509 hashedrekord/0.0.1 only; reject OpenPGP-capable/other types before the general parser. Pass unchanged bytes to upstream cryptographic checks.

Default installation resolves GitHub latest unless an exact version is supplied. Explicit managed channel uses the public version manifest and GitHub-first sources; self-upgrade environment semantics remain. Automatic resolution cannot downgrade a known version; explicit rollback can.

## Activation transaction
A no-follow nonblocking lock serializes the root. Closed bounded archive membership rejects links, duplicates, traversal, missing/extra files, bad trailers and changed bytes. Published artifact-cache owns verified acquisition/storage.

Stage complete suites in .redeven-runtime-suites/<archive-sha256>, sync, read back digests/inventory/version and prepare pinned ripgrep before atomic redeven symlink replacement. Ripgrep 15.2.0 uses Linux musl archives on both architectures. New/reused executables must actually run and report that version; missing loader, timeout, wrong version or oversized output leaves prior activation unchanged. Detect concurrent changes; restore and verify prior entry after post-switch failure. Distinguish unchanged from committed-but-unconfirmed errors.

Retain published suites and legacy flat resources: live older processes can still need them after multiple upgrades. Installer owns no process lifetime, so removal needs an explicit unused/rollback assessment; disk usage grows with distinct archives.

Fresh install uses a writable user directory without implicit sudo. Idempotent bash/zsh/fish blocks update future PATH; print the current-shell command or direct path for unknown shells. Upgrade changes no shell profile and starts/restarts no service. Runtime owns maintenance/re-exec after success.

## Publication and promotion
From v0.13.13, authenticated redeven-installer-contract.json declares minimum installer, closed targets and archive contract; older installers stop before incompatible acquisition. Render GitHub and Portal bootstraps from one template and four actual installer hashes; sign both through aggregate checksums. Portal uses its official mirror fallback, not another implementation.

Publish assets with --latest=false. Before promotion, check-distribution authenticates inventory/contract and each bootstrap's complete digest, tag, channel and four pins without relying on the current default. After promotion, --check-active-entry requires GitHub byte equality; Portal authenticates its active bootstrap against its own signed release and candidate minimum installer, permitting an older recommended Runtime. Read back GitHub's default independently.

README selects generated GitHub bootstrap; The Portal UI and install endpoint redirect to the generated Portal entry under its channel contract. Redirects confer no signature trust. No placeholder hashes/missing assets may activate. Public deployment is explicit. Rollback selects compatible immutable signed releases, never obsolete external-tool installers or duplicated shell code. Historical upgrade/native execution/page integration remain explicit acceptance, outside ordinary push gates.

## Dependency security
Consume checksum-verified published Cosign/Rekor patches. Require go-jose >=4.1.6 and no imported legacy golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp packages; preserve identity, signing time, roots and transparency. Qualify official releases plus tampering/cross-tag denial. The distinct general SDK OpenPGP finding and its format-rejection boundary remain documented below; a nonzero scanner is never a clean audit.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Verification is online; transparency or trust-service outages fail closed.
The bootstrap cannot defend against compromise of its original HTTPS script.
Cross-compilation alone does not certify execution on every target OS.

The dependency audit fixes the reviewed gRPC findings by selecting released
`v1.83.1`. The general SDK still imports the deprecated OpenPGP implementation
reported by `GO-2026-5932`; symbol scanning can continue to report it. The
installer rejects those input formats before SDK parsing. Do not describe a
nonzero scanner result as a clean audit, add a blanket suppression, or remove
this boundary without reviewing the upstream replacement and genuine fixtures.

concepts.summary: Runtime validates saved HTTPS identity; registered Desktop management exposes explicit create/import/regenerate/remove. Validity, trust and operation result are independent. sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Identity and trust
The user explicitly creates a device CA with `local-authority device-ca generate` and inspects it with `status`. Runtime startup never generates, replaces, or repairs certificate material.

Public export contains certificate material only, never the key.

## Explicit certificate changes
`import`, `regenerate`, and `remove` require `--confirm`. Reject malformed or extraneous PEM blocks, trailing text, encrypted/mismatched keys, invalid dates, invalid chains, missing SANs, and certificates unsuitable for server authentication.

This supports process-interruption recovery; it does not promise an OS trust rollback or filesystem power-loss durability.

## Coverage during network changes
[Local UI network exposure](local-ui-network-exposure.md) owns the two-second interface refresh and atomic public snapshot.

A signing failure retains only current addresses covered by the previous valid leaf and reports `certificate_refresh_failed`; retries recover automatically. Startup and explicit saved-identity preflight retain their strict validation boundary.

## Desktop interaction and private input
The compact HTTPS panel presents certificate validity, expiry, and system trust separately. Public path, fingerprint, and bounded selectable diagnostics live in the expandable details section.

Saving next-start HTTPS settings remains possible with an unusable certificate, with an explicit startup warning.

concepts.summary: New Runtime endpoints explicitly use HTTP localhost:23998; network exposure retains local access and requires fixed port/effective password. HTTPS is separate with strict certificate/trust checks. Pages and WS/WSS share the public port. TLS failure never downgrades; private Desktop bridge cannot become public fallback.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## HTTPS certificate ownership
[Local UI certificates](local-ui-certificates.md) owns creation, import, replacement, removal, validation, and client trust. It never creates or repairs certificate material, installs trust, or falls back to HTTP. Certificate replacement affects the next start; the running TLS identity and sessions remain intact.

## Listener and origin boundary
The public listener accepts only canonical authorities derived from its actual bound addresses.
An HTTP loopback listener also routes the exact plugin child origins derived
from its current parent authority and port exclusively to ReDevPlugin's Web
resource handler. Child routing strips parent credentials and never enters
Local UI management. A removed parent, different port, network-only address,
or HTTPS listener cannot use this loopback resource route. The platform still
validates each asset session, origin, ticket, and surface lifetime.

Its isolated `flowersec-private-loopback/1` profile is unchanged and cannot authorize public clients.

## Native Desktop default-port recovery
Only native Desktop launches with saved default `localhost:23998` and no explicit one-start bind override opt in through `--local-ui-default-port-fallback`. Other errors, custom ports, numeric loopback overrides, network binds, and wildcard binds never silently select another port.

External bookmarks containing the old fixed port cannot follow the temporary address.

## Network changes and current reports
While network exposure is enabled, Runtime enumerates eligible interfaces every two seconds. Its public list is explicit, including `[]`; private bridge endpoints cannot supply missing public addresses.

Address failures affect public availability and never assert that the Runtime process has stopped or expose private management URLs.

## Admission and lifecycle
A network listener starts only for a concrete non-loopback IP or wildcard with a fixed nonzero port and an effective password.

Occupied explicit ports fail with a startup error instead of silently selecting another port.

Flowersec owns admission, session establishment, liveness, handler dispatch, close, and lease release; Redeven does not copy those loops.

## Server-owned access configuration
[Runtime two-factor authentication](runtime-two-factor-authentication.md) owns the persistent credential authority, one-time bcrypt verifier migration, TOTP enrollment, recovery, replay protection, and ordinary-session revocation. Explicit password changes remain next-start settings when MFA is disabled; MFA-enabled settings cannot clear/replace that password or downgrade HTTPS.

Failed catalog saves roll back verifier initialization as well as replacement and clearing.

concepts.title: Permission policy and filesystem scope
concepts.summary:
Redeven treats endpoint runtime policy as authoritative. Control-plane grants can authorize a session, but the runtime clamps those grants with a local permission policy and file-facing features use explicit filesystem root policy.

Runtime permissions are clamped by local policy and file features are scoped by directory root policy.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
The local permission policy is a three-bit read/write/execute cap.

Explicitly configured read-only roots remain read-only; session caps, canonical path boundaries, and host filesystem permissions still constrain every operation.

Redeven persists only product authorization audit and does not maintain an approval queue, receipt, generation, revision, or recovery lifecycle.

## Descriptor-based reads

Repository-rule discovery and delivered-file reads use Registry.OpenRead. It
resolves current policy, rechecks the selected root, walks canonical components
through pinned os.Root handles, rejects substituted symlinks and compares opened
identities before returning a descriptor. Metadata comes from that descriptor.
A previously authorized pathname is not a reusable read capability.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Files path entry follows the shared [absolute filesystem navigation contract](../ui/filesystem-picker-navigation.md#product-presentations).

Browser state, display-only Home hints, provider metadata, and UI affordances cannot widen runtime permissions.

Provider wire configuration may enable multi-call generation, but it cannot grant permission, bypass approval, or alter runtime scheduling.

frontmatter.title: Plugin platform integration security

concepts.summary: ReDevPlugin receives authenticated host identity/source policy, never browser-claimed ownership/trust. HTTP checks auth, origin, CSRF and closed-action policy; direct calls check owner/action/resource. Package provenance, signature, execution approval, update eligibility and permission are independent. Integrity, runtime identity or scope mismatch fails closed.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Local process boundary
The `process.local` permission is an explicit high-risk grant and method-level Process Broker access is checked again for every Worker invocation. The Host does not inherit the complete Redeven environment and never injects session cookies, plugin tokens, or Host credentials.

See [Plugin process sessions](../architecture/plugin-process-sessions.md) for the lifecycle contract.

## Authenticated session boundary
The session resolver accepts only a Redeven channel id whose stored metadata has exact non-empty channel, user, and environment identities.

The bounded session cache is keyed by owner-session hash and accepts a hit only when all four hashes match.

Guessed owner sweeps and local teardown registries are prohibited.

## HTTP and direct authorization
The canonical route is `/_redevplugin/api/plugins`.

Method effect is resolved before local policy clamps it, while shared runtime management remains admin-only.

## Permission management projection
Plugin Center reads active grants and explicit plugin security policies through released ReDevPlugin APIs. It never writes registry tables, invents a default grant for a catalog plugin, or treats catalog identity as permission.

Its actual trust badge remains unchanged; only verified catalog trust may receive the `Official` trust badge.

## Package admission and trust
The retained release install/update path accepts only the exact source policy, revocation evidence, publisher, plugin, version, signed release metadata, package hashes, and Host requirement. Browser-supplied trust state, arbitrary package bytes, rollback, unknown publishers, invalid or revoked signatures, and invented fetch provenance are denied.

Redeven does not add a new authorization workflow; the existing official release-ref verification remains unchanged.

## Network routing and authorization

A VPN, configured proxy or enterprise DNS answer is routing policy, not evidence
that a user request is malicious. Host package downloads use normal host routing
while retaining upstream source, redirect and integrity validation. Authorized
HTTPS hostname connectors use the released host transport contract after grant
checks. This does not grant undeclared destinations or methods, bypass private
prefix bindings, or expose ambient host/session credentials.

Proxy discovery failures, timeouts and TLS failures reject only the affected
operation. Construction performs no network discovery, and plugin readiness does
not gate core Runtime readiness. Certificate validation stays enabled. Proxy
credentials apply only to the proxy hop; application writes with unknown outcomes
are not retried automatically.

## Capability confirmation plans
ReDevPlugin validates a capability preflight result against the Host-known capability response schema before it becomes a confirmation plan. Values in the reserved `redevplugin.capability.risk_plan.*` namespace must match the strict v1 risk-plan contract; an unknown or malformed reserved version fails closed instead of falling back to a generic object.

Replacing or replaying any of those values requires a new confirmation.

## Runtime trust
Runtime descriptors bind version, target, IPC, WASM ABI, and artifact hash. Darwin release bytes receive their Developer ID signature before the product digest and Sigstore evidence, and later Desktop signing must preserve that exact nested executable. Startup must not hash the field binary and accept that value as its own trust anchor.

## Business adapter and observability boundary
Plugin business adapters are invoked only after ReDevPlugin resolves lifecycle, permission, confirmation, lease, quota, revocation, and audit context. Product code cannot bypass that chain.

Raw adapter errors, tokens, secrets, cookies, query strings, absolute paths, and complete URLs are not copied into public or durable diagnostic detail.

## Plugin Web isolation

Plugin documents use a distinct product-allocated origin and the published Web surface handler. Local UI and AppServer strip parent authentication before delegating child traffic. Desktop verifies the actual requesting frame origin before attaching private bridge credentials. For frame-less worker requests, it verifies Electron's browser-reported initiator origin within the owning Runtime partition against the same exact private origin. Missing or opaque origins fail closed; a present frame remains authoritative, and worker requests never receive frame-only host-access or Tessiven source claims. Center binds child routes to an authenticated parent and cancels derived preparation on revocation; Gateway accepts only the expected child namespace and target.

The application owns its DOM and browser rendering. These freedoms do not grant product session, filesystem, process, credential or management authority. The released platform remains responsible for asset sessions, bridge binding, permissions and revocation.

Main-process `session.fetch` requests also pass through Electron's request hook. A contextless `other` request may retain authorization only when it already carries exactly one matching private bridge token from the owning Runtime session and has no frame, WebContents owner or initiator origin. Missing provenance alone grants nothing. Destination checks still bind the exact private origin; renderer and worker provenance remains authoritative, and frame-only claims are never inherited.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Session authority and lifetime
The gate alone decides channel authorization when registering the channel and its lifetime cancellation callback under one lock. Callers supply verified private-management identity or an ordinary login session ID, never an `unlocked` assertion.

Runtime restart clears in-memory sessions and incomplete operations; it preserves committed authentication state.

## Browser Cookie scope and continuity
Local UI alone issues, reads and clears `redeven_local_access_<http|https>_<port>`. Forwarded headers cannot select the scope.

Only an incorrect password or factor produces input validation feedback; transport failures and cooldowns retain their own messages.

## Desktop consumption and forwarding
Desktop Flower retains the complete Runtime-issued access-cookie `name=value` pair and returns it unchanged. It never derives the name from a bridge or forwarded client port.

No upstream platform capability changes are required for this product authentication policy.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Enrollment and management
Desktop Environment Settings / Access presents one two-factor row. If a different environment password has been saved for the next start, restart before configuring MFA; the old running verifier cannot overwrite the newer saved authority.

These commands do not alter SSH keys, sshd policy, PAM, host passwords, or execution identity.

## Session authority
[Runtime access sessions](runtime-access-sessions.md) owns ordinary session deadlines, browser Cookie scope and refresh continuity, challenge binding, native editor delegation, and revocation. MFA management changes revoke ordinary authority through that single gate; they do not create a second browser or Desktop authentication lifecycle.

## Persistence, replay and recovery
`access-auth.sqlite` is a versioned, private SQLite authority, separate from the transport authorization database. The committed database and initialized key become the sole authority; deletion, malformed data, unsafe modes, symlinks, unknown schema, or key loss cannot fall back to the retired verifier.

Authentication state and secrets are not diagnostic export inputs.

Missing committed authentication state fails closed; host recovery locks ordinary access until new credentials are committed.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Setup and storage

Owner command `redeven-center setup --state-root ...` issues the mandatory 15-minute setup credential. Password, verified TOTP and recovery-code confirmation commit together; partial setup grants nothing. Passwords use 12–72 UTF-8 bytes; recovery codes replace only the factor.

Unix owner socket authorization checks actual service UID or root. SSH accounts/tunnels, loopback and headers grant nothing. `recover` fences business and creates owner-authorized setup; `recover --offline --origin ...` requires exclusive stopped-state access. Unsupported peer verification fails closed.

An exclusive lock protects private AES-GCM SQLite state. `center.key` pins instance/origin/initialization; missing or corrupt committed state fails closed. Back up key and database together. Browser DTOs omit secrets/private keys; only owner commands print temporary credentials.

Audit records retain a closed sensitive-action category, never the request payload or its credential-derived digest. Exact action bindings remain only in expiring challenges/grants; password verifiers use bcrypt. Database version 2 atomically redacts version-1 audit references before readiness, preserves event facts and unrelated state, and rejects damaged or future stores unchanged.

## Authentication and devices

Password creates a five-minute browser/action/session/revision-bound challenge, with at most five factor failures. Password alone grants no business. Atomic TOTP-step/recovery consumption persists across restart. Login rotates device/browser sessions. Security changes revoke sessions, challenges, grants and derived connections.

Sessions allow one hour idle, twelve hours absolute and 16 devices. Only trusted visible input renews idle activity. Frozen pages, output, polling and heartbeat do not. Device revocation preserves other devices; restart invalidates all sessions, preserving credentials, directory and audit.

Sensitive mutations require fresh password/factor verification and ten-minute action/target/payload/revision grants. Password-change action bindings use PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (600,000 iterations, 32 bytes) with a domain-separated random login-device ID salt, mirrored by browser Web Crypto; raw password SHA-256 fingerprints are forbidden. Expiry/revision/session checks run again after derivation. Bounded same-session/request retry receipts prevent repeated effects. Valid sessions need no extra MFA for viewing/opening.

## Admission and resource limits

Bounded authentication concurrency and persistent administrator/direct-peer budgets survive restart. Failures back off and expire instead of locking permanently. Forwarded headers cannot choose source identity.

Device revocation/recovery cancels catalog/pairing requests. Budgets allow two per device/source, eight per device and 32 globally, preserving logout and other sources.

Current limits: 16 Gateways, 128 routes, 128 operation receipts with at most 32 per device, 16 live root/child operations per device, 16 concurrent proxy requests per access owner, 48 per device, 192 total. Repeated opens cannot let one device fill the global receipt budget. Revocation removes live admission immediately; five-minute tombstones retain retry outcomes. JSON/header sizes are bounded, file streams incremental, private egress restricted to signed approved endpoints.

Reopening a child creates a fresh browser-bound handoff while reusing its live authority only for the exact parent, resource kind/ID, Runtime instance and Runtime login cookie name/value. Paths may differ within that resource. Canceling or expiring a repeated handoff preserves the existing owner; revoking that owner invalidates pending reuse. Reuse still consumes bounded handoff receipts and cannot bypass another resource's admission limit.

Runtime accessgate remains target authentication/channel authority. Binding+revision+device scopes prevent cross-route/device replay; children add resource scope. Binding revocation fences new admission and channels without changing unrelated paths. Children cannot invoke Env APIs, spend sibling artifacts or set parent cookies. Changed proofs fail closed without downgrade. Portal framing stays denied; child framing follows Runtime policy.

`activityNavigation` stores version 1 with a current target and `recentBuiltins`. Module placeholders read that same binding for view mode and layout; temporary lack of runtime metadata must not select a different preference store.

Loading and cache authority follow [Env App resource snapshots](env-resource-cache.md).

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## One interaction mode
Desktop Welcome and Desktop-hosted Env App configure `mobileQuery: 'not all'`; the Env App recognizes its native host through the existing Desktop bridge.

Resizing a desktop browser cannot rewrite its saved Activity/Workbench choice or activate mobile terminal input.

A hidden toolbar action must retain an explicit reachable entry.

## Temporary desktop navigation
Shell, Flower conversations, Files/Git navigation, and Terminal sessions measure their own shared navigation/content region. When that region cannot fit the current sidebar width plus 480 CSS pixels of main content, the sidebar becomes a transient left side drawer.

Files/Git navigation begins with its mode switch, without a separate Files title row or reserved header space. The switch uses the published field height, including its border and padding, so the sidebar and single-row file toolbar dividers align at every interface scale. The mobile close action shares that row; desktop drawers retain their accessible dialog title and dismissal. Sidebar resizing and local tree scrolling remain available.

File filtering and entering or leaving idle path editing never add header feedback or change toolbar height. The shared bottom status bar owns the filtered item count and view indicator. Path editing keeps Enter submission, Escape cancellation, and blur cancellation without an instruction row; pending navigation and errors retain their accessible header feedback.

Mobile navigation retains its product-specific bottom/side panel behavior under the [mobile Shell](mobile-shell-navigation.md) and [Flower](flower-mobile-navigation.md) contracts.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
## Flower welcome
Desktop Flower retains its mark, title, introduction, working directory, four complete starter suggestions, and keyboard hints even when the chat region is 767 CSS pixels or narrower. Container queries adjust spacing and the suggestion grid; they cannot hide content or switch interaction mode.

Narrow layouts may ellipsize selection titles; explanations remain normal prose and mobile suggestion cards retain their compact presentation.

concepts.title: Dialog content placement
concepts.summary:
Published Floe Webapp owns the shared Dialog structure. Redeven supplies localized
titles, body guidance, and actions. Headers contain identity and controls;
instructions and consequences belong in the body. This applies to ordinary
dialogs, confirmation dialogs, drawers, and window-local confirmations. A missing
or misplaced description is a content integration failure, never a reason to
restore a header subtitle or hide the text.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Floe Webapp 0.84.0 removes the ambiguous `description` parameter from `Dialog` and `ConfirmDialog`. Custom headers and title JSX must not recreate the removed explanatory subtitle.

This contract changes no application connection, process, or window lifecycle.

## Header-safe bounds

Global dialogs and drawers reserve the visible application header before allocating
their body height. The shared Redeven stylesheet applies the larger of the native
Desktop titlebar and Floe's visible shell top bar plus its top safe inset, followed
by the published presentation gap. Floe owns the visible viewport, keyboard
response, remaining safe edges, panel maximum height, focus and dismissal. The
single product top-padding override is intentional because the published Dialog
sets that padding inline. Do not reintroduce per-dialog viewport subtraction or
minimum heights that can overflow short windows.

The shell header contract is Floe's `h-10` content plus its one-pixel border. A
headerless mobile shell adds no phantom header; inactive KeepAlive views do not
count as visible headers. Surface-local dialogs and Workbench window confirmations
stay within their existing host below the shell header without subtracting it a
second time. Side drawers keep their edge-attached presentation.

Headers, close controls and footer actions remain reachable while long content
scrolls inside the body. Flower settings, nested editors and conversation rename
use the published Dialog. Preserve the bounded loading geometry defined in
[page-loading continuity](page-loading-continuity.md).

concepts.title: Personal directory favorites
concepts.summary:
Runtime owns one directory-favorites store. Each authenticated namespace, endpoint
and user has an independent ordered path set and revision. Env App and Desktop
supply this metadata to published Floe controlled pickers and filesystem menus; the
existing filesystem navigator remains the only path validation and selection owner.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Persistence and authentication
The Runtime opens apps/filesystem/directory-favorites.sqlite through sqliteutil before service readiness and closes it with Code App. Schema v1 is initialized transactionally; existing tables, objects and records are verified and unsupported or future schemas fail before a writable open.

There is no ten-item cap, automatic deletion, move tracking, grouping or custom naming.

## Client ownership and interaction
One in-memory client per authenticated environment supplies every mounted entry.

Initial load failure offers retry; refresh failure retains displayed paths.

No separate title card, second path line or persistent favorite star occupies the sidebar.

Files composes Home, Computer and favorites into one Quick access list, deduplicated by absolute path with authoritative root labels and permissions preserved. All entries share filtering and scrolling; roots are not pinned separately. Short lists use their natural height, capped at the smaller of 16rem and 45% of the sidebar body. The directory tree owns a separate viewport. Filtering appears above five entries, matches labels or full paths, holds the viewport height while active, and restores the previous list scroll on clear. Refresh retains rows, focus and the query. Arrow/Home/End navigation reveals only the local target, including in scaled Workbench windows. Menu invocation retains the captured directory and published focus ownership.

Quick access marks only the exact active destination, never its containing root. The existing navigator supplies pending intent: selection and busy semantics update immediately; the progress icon appears only after 150ms of uninterrupted waiting to avoid fast-refresh flicker. Current-page semantics identify only the displayed path. Hover is weaker than selection; a leading marker distinguishes selection from focus. Selection never changes font weight, size or text geometry. Filtering never promotes another row to active.

The entire 32px-high shortcut row is a native navigation button, including padding and permission badges, except for the separate trailing 32px menu button. No dead gaps or overlapping actions divide these targets; pointer, keyboard and touch retain the same navigation/menu ownership.

Published Sidebar owns the outer width; the Files/Git body fits its content box without a second fixed width or outer scroll owner.

Flower exposes favorites inside its directory picker. Conversation transcript and thread-list menus do not mutate directory favorites; their directory actions follow [working directory navigation](flower-working-directory-navigation.md).

## Compatibility
Runtime compatibility epoch 69 requires this exact authenticated resource and Desktop route allowlist. Floret APIs, domain schema, conversation lifecycle, file-operation authorization and Runtime Service protocol version remain unchanged.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Drag-region synchronization
Desktop projects iframe-relative native drag regions. A settled snapshot must not schedule another frame by rebuilding itself; native pointer/geometry ownership remains upstream.

## Global bands
Ordinary windows use 1000–1099; expanded Flower 2000; its context previews 2100–2199; plugin Panel 3000 and plugin context menu 3100; product modals 4000; command palette 5000. Local menus, tooltips and recovery UI stay within their surface's global band.

## Dialog placement
Mobile plugin/tools navigation belongs to Shell content, not a global Launcher. Backdrop clicks close only the Dialog without reaching Activity beneath it; titlebar controls remain no-drag.

## Visible viewport boundaries
Published Floe owns visible viewport/safe areas, Safari fixed-origin conversion and projected-surface intersection. Do not bypass it with fixed positions, uncapped viewport heights or transforms. Temporary constraints preserve preferred size.

Upstream elastic dragging resists boundary overflow, retains a reachable header and returns the window inside safe bounds on release/interruption. Dragging a maximized header restores preferred size at the grab point and continues the gesture; controls, double-click and mounted body remain independent. Redeven supplies safe-area insets and persists only settled geometry.

## Movable window order
A Shell-lifetime provider registers stable IDs, retains multiply registered IDs until all owners unregister, and assigns bounded MRU order within each window band. Minimized Debug Console is a base-band launcher, not an open window.

## Flower dismissal
Expanded Flower sits above ordinary windows; owned previews sit above Flower and below plugin Panels. Dismissal never restores composer focus, which would expand it again. Host pointer/focus and trusted plugin bridge activation/focus/action events collapse Flower without consuming destination interaction, including cross-origin iframe interaction.

Published Floe keeps resize handles on the outer geometry surface, outside rounded content clipping. All eight handles remain pointer-reachable; compact and maximized windows expose none.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Window boundary
[Floating layers](env-app-floating-layer-order.md) own placement/clamps. Title/close/toolbar remain reachable; documents scroll locally.

## Reading area and zoom
Fit uses local CSS pixels excluding padding/scrollbars, independent of Workbench transforms. Initial fit may enlarge; resize preserves manual zoom. Attachments keep native PDF controls/contained images/shrinkable containers.

## Rendering ownership
Lazy published Floe PDF owns layers/scoped CSS. Each PDF/PPTX page has one renderer. Identity fences image callbacks/stale work; cancellation is neutral and errors local/retryable.

## Office and delimited files
Shared task-file/attachment adapters serve Desktop/Env App. Attachments retain native image/PDF/text; Env App retains file actions/Monaco/selected-Workbench wheel ownership. Never feed unsupported XLS/DOC/PPT to OOXML.

XLSX/CSV/TSV lazily use unmodified exact published @silurus/ooxml@0.89.7 XLSX. Send original copied bytes without flattening. Public XlsxWorkbook.load, visible-sheet metadata, getWorksheet, XlsxSheetViewer.fromWorkbook and explicit activation own rendering; worksheet reads surface parse errors before activation. Select every visible worksheet, skip hidden ones. Engine owns styles/merges/cached formulas/comments. Remove ExcelJS and its 200-row/50-column cap everywhere.

One toolbar row: sheet, optional cell value, search, zoom, information. Search opens explicitly/Ctrl-Cmd+F and returns focus on close. Cell/fidelity panels use published SurfaceFloatingLayer/useOverlayMask for narrow placement/input isolation; Escape closes them before parent windows. CSV/TSV retain table/source/encoding and literal cells (zeros, long IDs, formula-like text); editing/truncation forces source. Encoding changes only table, not source-editor decoding.

Limits: input 20 MiB, 100,000 rows, 1,000,000 cells, 64 MiB owned UTF-8, 128 MiB JSON. Disable Google Fonts/hyperlinks; comments only XLSX. Engine observer owns canvas resize, ignoring host transforms. Replace/unmount fences work and destroys viewer before workbook. Parse/render/search errors stay retryable; promise success cannot erase errors. Distinguish unsupported legacy from failed supported previews.

DOCX keeps docx-preview and off-DOM identity-checked commit; PPTX keeps published Floe document/page ownership, navigation and incomplete/external-content notice. Rich previews share 20 MiB/local retry. Never rewrite originals.

Only original-author releases: no forks, vendoring, patches, model rewrites or silent fallback. XLSX indentation/views/malformed fidelity may differ from Office. DOCX/PPTX migration awaits upstream fixes and Word-equivalent math/layout evidence. Lazy renderer/worker/WASM assets include licenses/notices. Build size is not installer size.

## HTML pages
[HTML preview](file-preview-html.md) owns page-first opening, explicit editing, bounds/isolation and rejection of incomplete HTML.

## Markdown enhancements
Mermaid skips diagramless work, caches themes and fences stale results. Contents starts closed in published right-drawer Dialog, preserving width/nodes/scroll; headings scroll then close it. File changes reset it; headingless files disable it. Main preview keeps its sidebar.

Floe semantic roles: headings/links interaction/info, lower headings/quotes tip, emphasis note, dedicated code ink; dark headings retain hue/lightness floor, tables/metadata subtle tints, GFM alerts semantic roles. Text/inset titles require 4.5:1 across presets/materials/floating windows. Keep underline/focus/readable selection/system forced colors. Theme changes preserve geometry/DOM/selection/focus/scroll.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Absolute paths and runtime authority
Released Floe DirectoryPicker/DirectoryInput/file pickers own navigation/validity/request lifetime. Redeven supplies connection, authoritative path context, i18n/form state. [Filesystem policy](../security/permission-policy-and-filesystem-scope.md) reauthorizes operations; Home/Root/context never invent grants.

## Navigation state and failures
Each picker owns directory/entries/input/hidden switch/validity. Fence stale success/failure by current intent; validation is no later authorization. Files uses released parsePickerPath/formatPickerPath without Home-prefixing absolute paths. Real viewports declare Workbench local-scroll; host/Floe retain modal/focus/keyboard.

## Live language changes
Translate Home/Root in place without replacing drafts/selection or reloading authority; Desktop/Env App share the adapter.

## Product presentations
A failed Files navigation retains its last readable listing and one dismissible notice:selectable full path, copy, recovery actions. Without a readable listing use a bounded recovery card. Paths wrap/controls reflow inside scaled/narrow views. Link input to this notice by ID; syntax/cancellation retain own explanation. Editing clears stale invalid-input state, not unresolved navigation. Retry keeps focus/geometry through pending/repeated failure.

Existing browse/cache owner shows only visited target's snapshot while verifying. Uncached targets preserve readable listing with separate pending intent. Current clicks do not reload; pending duplicates share a request. Unverified cached destinations still verify/commit. Superseded reads release queue immediately and cannot alter content/persistence/recovery. Manual/hidden-path changes verify first.

Reveal each changed tree destination once per visible container; revalidation cannot repeat scrollIntoView or undo user scroll. Pointer navigation keeps row anchor; selection typography/geometry never transitions.

## Creating a child directory
Released picker owns New folder and nonmodal anchored popup:parent, name, actions, focus, Enter/Escape, pending/stale-request handling. No extra backdrop/resize. Escape/Cancel/outside idle closes popup only. Failure retains name/local error. One authenticated callback serves Flower, DirectoryInput/Env adapters. Names are one child, not traversal/nested paths. Success refreshes parent; enter/confirm remain explicit. Canceling picker preserves draft and cannot undo submitted work.

Env App uses nonrecursive filesystem RPC/invalidation; Desktop exact POST /_redeven_proxy/api/fs/mkdir. Both share filesystem/scope/Git mutation owners. Require session write, strict fields, existing parent and preserve existing entries. No recursive creation, synthetic list or automatic retry. Unknown effects require inspection. All ten locales translate errors. Compatibility epoch 70 requires the Desktop resource; older peers upgrade. Gateway/Floret/schema unchanged.

## Shared directory favorites
[Favorites](directory-favorites.md) owns scoped persistence/refresh/failures; shortcut views cannot confirm an old selection.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Companion ownership
Published `BottomBarCompanion` owns geometry, viewport/safe-area clamps, motion, outside dismissal, Escape and mount handling. Its Portal uses the explicit Activity overlay host, never `document.body`. The collapsed field is centered; bounded detail grows upward without changing body geometry. Running work cannot prevent collapse or destination interaction.

## Activity Terminal footer
Desktop Activity Terminal supplies a 24-pixel anchor in its 28-pixel footer, centered in the terminal column with a shrinkable 360-pixel maximum width. Workbench/mobile terminals supply none. Placement does not create another Flower instance, alter transport or route Flower input through the terminal.

## Stable Flower placement
After first access readiness, one retained `EnvAIPage`/`FlowerSurface` moves among explicit hosts. Visibility drives `hidden`, `aria-hidden` and `inert` together. Available unfiltered Workbench placement survives deselection; canvas selection governs input/focus only. [Settings](flower-setup-and-settings.md#retained-panels) own retained panels/forms.

## Contextual Ask Flower
New companion conversations may capture the desktop Activity origin using its read-only page reader. [Turn launcher](flower-turn-launcher.md) owns sending/context actions.

## Presence and summary
[Presence](flower-companion-presence.md) owns collapsed priority, live tails, completion feedback, composer precedence and workspace observation.

## Dismissal, focus, and reads
Outside capture includes shell, anchor and classified Flower-owned Portals. Trusted cross-origin plugin bridge events join host pointer/focus dismissal without consuming the destination. Shared SSE summaries are activity-only; initial/reconnect read baselines and later read envelopes are scoped to the same `UserPublicID`.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Stable disclosure and safe content

Permanent folding-rail gutter aligns prose/activity/progress before grouping. Goal icons share that edge; expanded text aligns to summary. Tool/thinking metadata and disclosure follow text with a compact gap and full-row activation. Chevrons read existing aria-expanded: right closed/down open, including initially open screenshots; no second state owner.

Identity is thread/run/turn/canonical item ID. [Sequences](flower-tool-sequences.md) own grouping/bounded thinking; individual details remain available. Collapsed field summaries preserve intent/result shape without hidden payload. Disclosure reads selected values; long text uses 16 KiB ranges/128 KiB reading windows with explicit selection pins. Close/hide/navigation cancels demand. Markdown reads exact UTF-8 chunks and yields between batches, never sampling/removing meaningful whitespace. Selected Markdown remains a complete working set, not fixed-memory preview.

## Thread query and read details

Thread Query: and Thread Read: are fixed technical labels with model-authored intent in the user's language. [Queries](../ai/flower-thread-queries.md) owns privacy, lookup, limits and failures.

## Web search details

One localized visible/accessibility action title. Expanded details show real per-call results/errors, including URL-only sources, without repeating header query/URL/pattern/status.

## Semantic tool icons

Compact shared rows provide glyphs for registered tools, hosted search, sources, MCP and unknown extensions. Tool/thinking icons, prose and full/companion progress share the leading edge. Composer/status uses transcript's native scrollbar gutter. Existing resize observer reads gutter only on inline-size changes; existing layout scheduling publishes changed geometry. Row growth adds no width reads/observer/scheduler. Embedded hosts retain layout ownership.

## Intent, inputs and results

Collapsed titles describe invocation intent, not outcomes; presentation cannot supply execution input/authority. BrowserUse/ComputerUse omit absent-observation filler but preserve typed failures, uncertain effects, blank pages and unavailable targets.

## Viewport and gesture ownership

One transcript controller owns position; layout/focus/motion/growth cannot resume paused reading. [Sequences](flower-tool-sequences.md#geometry-and-input) own native nested scrolling; hidden controls are inert. [SubAgent details](flower-subagent-detail.md) own their viewport.

Transcript/child prose continuously approaches current bottom; chunks retarget without restart. One line settles about 160 ms, retaining fractions without overshoot. Geometry shares one scheduled frame; animation-only frames reuse measurements and skip history scans until settled scroll. No idle polling/output delay. Native input/selection pauses follow immediately; clearing selection does not resume. Initial positioning/navigation/resize/shrinking are immediate. Explicit return uses 220 ms arrival; automatic folds follow actual content without trailing space/competing scroll. Exclude paused-reading room from distance to latest. Reduced motion skips animation; hide/rebind/disposal cancels obsolete motion.

## Thinking duration

Canonical first/last chunk receipt times survive hydration/reconnect/restart/Fork, replacing page observations. Native continuation reopens the interval; last chunk ends it. Tooltips distinguish receipt duration from provider compute. Show <1ms or localized Not recorded; never infer from neighbors/turn totals. Legacy observations stay memory-only.

## Visual motion

Live thinking fills five petals clockwise then center, holds/fades over 2.4 seconds. Sealed/cancelled/disconnected rows are static. Theme/reduced-motion/high-contrast/forced-color variants use CSS without another lifecycle. Disclosure uses one reversible Web Animation: 180 ms open/140 ms default close, ignoring stale completions. [Sequence handoff](flower-tool-sequences.md#disclosure-and-bodies) owns 260 ms geometry, composited summary crossfade and stationary prose arrival.

Fresh tool/argument-preview/thinking titles reveal once over 168–360 ms in at most 32 width-adapted steps. Full text/geometry/accessibility/actions exist immediately. After sequence placement, viewport makes room over 220 ms before reveal; growth retargets without extending deadline. User scroll interrupts; paused reading stays paused; reduced motion skips. Delivery/results/controls never wait. Arrivals are independent; glyph shimmer follows reveal without typography changes.

Accepted receipt provenance/selection preparation gates execution-scoped arrivals. History/body restoration and queued reading consume claims and settle folds statically; post-ready live snapshots/deltas remain eligible. Two visible timeline receipts retain only an in-memory restore revision/live flag, no transcript copy/scheduler/timer/row observer. Claims exclude navigation/reconnect baselines/hidden disclosures/mounts delayed beyond 450 ms. They observe closure before lazy mount and survive preview promotion/remount/snapshot replacement/completion. Final snapshots may reveal new tools from the previously active execution.

Auto-fold waits for admitted title motion then applies reading protection; new prose waits for sequence closure, while delivery/manual actions remain immediate. Title nodes survive trigger changes; call identity transfers remaining time. Failure/approval acts immediately. Navigation/disposal/hidden documents/reduced motion clear clipping; no character timers/per-frame reactive state/persisted animation facts.
